nodes.lesson: The Hecke eigen-property is carried along by the shear (conjugated operators keep it at every tau); the only thing special at tau = 0 is that Hecke operators are translations, which is "completely multiplicative ordinary Dirichlet series" restated. Defect order in tau is 0 or 1 and cannot separate zeta from any completely multiplicative control. tau = 0 is the boundary of the sheared prime expansion's convergence domain, approached from the side where the conclusion is false, with l^1 size about exp(1/(4|tau|)).

nodes.name: Joint Hecke-primitive tests in the bridge energy H_c
nodes.statement: For a finite set S of primes, jointly S-primitive tests are dense (L^2 and Q) in the test class, so the infimum of Q/norm^2 over primitive tests equals the infimum over all tests: the restriction neither helps nor costs. The Gram matrix of dilations does not contain the function's coefficients. All-prime Hecke sums lie in the radical of the zero sum. Referee does not hold the result as written (Lemma 3(a) domain: inverse of M_S does not preserve compact support; 'this is P10 itself' not established).
nodes.lesson: Hecke/Moebius operators are translation multipliers with no zeros in the open strip, so restricting a translation-invariant form (Weil/Q_L) to primitive tests is a congruence and changes nothing; the orthogonalisation step is function-independent. Any multiplicative mechanism must act where the cutoff fails to commute with Hecke (window defect), and that formula is also kernel-independent. Reusable tool: plib.py computes Q_L from primes alone in an orthonormal basis (Loewner form) for zeta and four controls, validated against zero sums to 1e-12.

nodes.name: Windowed semidefinite coupling of Pick positivity with the explicit formula
nodes.statement: The real-node Pick matrix is linear in the zero measure, on-line pairs add PSD terms, and the LMI never contains the primes; so the joint window SDP equals the explicit-formula LP (delta*_joint = delta*_EF, T in 1e2..1e6, K <= 24; grid-certified on five node families, node-uniform statement open at (100,24)). No exclusion for L <= L*/2 at any height. Untested: an LMI whose on-line terms are not sign-definite (sector matrices P+-B).
nodes.lesson: A positivity LMI that is linear in the zero measure and monotone in on-line mass cannot couple to the explicit formula: it acts only where it already excludes the configuration with the window emptied (K of about 4 per zero below, i.e. the verified-height horizon), and it is blind to the prime data. Half-plane Pick kernels for Re z > a0 are implied by the support constraint. Weakest point: the domination constant is certified on a grid and on five node families plus 48 hill climbs, with only a factor 2.5 margin at (T,K) = (100,24).

nodes.name: Is the squared signal of the F_q[T] probe an intersection-form square
nodes.statement: F_q[T], prime cubic conductor, N <= 3, q = 5, 7, 11, exact. For genus-1 targets the Moebius sum is S_cop(k) = sum_j c_j t_j with c independent of the curve, and (sum c_j t_j)^2 = -D.D/(2 q^N) for every real quadratic 1 - a u + q u^2, on or off the circle: the equality is deg[m] = m^2 on an elliptic curve, uses no index theorem and carries no positivity. Fakes with off-line zeros pass (3444 of 3444). In genus 2 the equality fails (0 of 80; 0 of 624) and the index theorem bounds the squared signal from above (the Weil bound), the opposite side from the low input. M_N = h_N is not trace-linear fo
nodes.lesson: In genus 1 every symmetric function of the Frobenius eigenvalues is linear in the traces, so any squared signal is trivially an intersection-form square (deg[m] = m^2) and the test separates nothing: fakes with off-line zeros and the Liouville-twisted target pass. The Hodge index theorem acts on the squared signal only as an upper bound (Weil bound for the target), the opposite side from what the low input needs. Model targets must have genus >= 2 before a "square" identity carries positivity content; there the Moebius signal is the trace on Sym^N H^1 with 1/L' weights, not a Weil functional.

nodes.name: Lead 4 (n4 spectral window with Moebius twist): exact reciprocity dual of the off-diagonal
nodes.statement: Weight-1 (n4) sum: the exact dual of sum_c w(c) sum_n S(n, l; c) f(n) (Lemma R, classical; confirmed by derivation and to 1e-14) transforms (n, c) only. The twist l <= X^2 that carries A is a parameter, so the ledger map is A -> A; the lattice side has T^(2A-1) terms per l against T spectral terms, never shorter for A > 1. The saving needed is cancellation in l, which no reciprocity on file touches. Variants with a dual family (Motohashi cubic weight, Blomer-Khan level exchange) are recalled, not derived: lengths preserved with positivity lost, or dual family longer; a ledger entry, not a theo
nodes.lesson: Reciprocity identities act on the L-value variable (n or the spectral parameter) and leave the mollifier twist l fixed or turn it into a level; the saving n4 needs is cancellation in l, which none of them touches. Moving to weights that have a dual family replaces Katok-Sarnak positivity by functional-equation positivity, which E_a with real a also satisfies. P2 has an exact anchor B(t_rho) = -1 but no region of absolute convergence in t, so the convexity detector cannot be run.

nodes.name: TRO6: dual sum on squarefree n and Type I on average over the level
nodes.statement: Lemmas A and B (proved finite identities): the dual sum on squarefree n, the Type I level average with sign mu(a), and the trilinear Gauss-sum form are re-bracketings of one finite trilinear sum; the level variable enters only through incomplete sums of normalised cubic Gauss sums, not Kloosterman sums. Measured at X = 1e6, 1e7: no saving in the signed outer sum of either form at resolution 0.01 to 0.03 in the exponent (eight decision differences above -0.02, minimum -0.0093). The one firing of the pre-registered rule (level statistic of form (b), kappa = 0.4) is removed by projecting out the
nodes.lesson: A rule of the form "exponent below the seeded controls" fires on a coherent term that decays (polar term, first moment of theta_6), so the polar and class-mean components must be removed before the fit and that removal pre-registered; here it was chosen after the rule fired. All four sub-items of lead 17 are the same trilinear sum, and at reachable sizes the test resolves exponents only to about 0.01-0.03, far coarser than the Q^(-eta/80) TRO6 needs.

nodes.name: F_q[T] probe signal on genus 2 and 3 targets
nodes.statement: F_q[T] model, squarefree conductors of degree 5 and 7, N <= 3. S_cop(k) is a polynomial in L_1..L_N, the same for genus 2 and 3, linear in Frobenius traces only at N = 1. At N = 1, 0 <= S^2 <= (g/2)(-D.D)/q is Cauchy-Schwarz inside the symmetric block of the graph-class form; ratio anywhere in [0,1], no lower bound. The symmetric block reads only reality of alpha + q/alpha; the Weil bound sits in the antisymmetric block, which the signal does not meet. Registered outcome (b). J_k itself not computed (answer is for S_cop inside the round-8 law).
nodes.lesson: The probe signal and the diagonal class sit in the symmetric (Frobenius plus Verschiebung) part of the graph classes, where the Hodge form reads only reality of alpha + q/alpha. The Weil bound sits in the antisymmetric part, which the signal does not meet. A squared pairing equals a norm only in rank 1 (genus 1). At N = 1 the test is one inequality per L-polynomial, and it was largely decided by c10 4(c) and its referee's correction 5.

nodes.name: F_7[T] completed-row energy: registered exact decomposition at two sizes with seeded classes
nodes.statement: F_7[T], N = 6, d = 2, exact. The squarefree-n part D of the cube term is 0.569/0.603 of the diagonal at lam = 9, 3.9e-5/3.0e-5 at lam = 10, 0 at lam = 11, 2.798/2.980 at lam = 12: the registered constant 1.5 is exceeded at (6,12,2). Lemma M: the mean of |Tf|^2 over unimodular cube coefficients is q^2 sum_m nu(m)|S_0(m)|^2 (companion energy times a count). Random multiplicative-sign and free-sign vectors give D of the same size as the targets. Not established: unboundedness in lam; total row energy at (6,12,2); independent reproduction of the (6,10,2) full-row figures.
nodes.lesson: Before a heavy run, compute every part of the registered statistic that stored data already fixes. Here the stored companion row gave the cube parts at four lengths, decided the question before the run, and showed the registered second size (6,10,2) to be off resonance, so its threshold test is vacuous. Summing over primes first into a weight-independent table (new kernel ffy.c, identical to all stored rows) made the 48 seeded vectors free and cut cost per prime by 15.

nodes.name: Part B: de Faveri n-th order large sieve (n = 6) on rows Z12, Z6, Z5, Z14; Ji ledger replay
nodes.statement: Part B, relative to de Faveri 2610.04045 Theorem 1.1 (unrefereed; n = 6 coverage matching not checked) and the unrefereed 7/8 manuscripts. Replacing (KD)^(2/3) by the n = 6 bound changes no figure: Z12 count option 7/6 - delta is above R at every class (proved); Z6 Q^0.75 against Q^(1/2 - eta); Z5 Gram exponent 1/6 = the cap; Framework A on the Poisson dual has exponent 2 at every order; reduced LP floor 13/15 unchanged. The manuscripts use the sextic sieve only in the preliminary 11/12 stage (margin -1/24 unchanged). Abscissa stays 0.8748866470. Ji 2611.16665 has no P_a^(1/6)-type term and no
nodes.lesson: An optimal arbitrary-coefficient sieve cannot move the 7/8 ledgers. Its new off-diagonal term is exactly what the architecture already carries: the Prop 15.2 exponent 1/6, the polar branch b/12, and the amplifier factor H^(1/n). THIN, U and sign twists pass it, so it cannot raise R3. The standing figure's chain uses the sextic sieve only in the preliminary 11/12 stage, where the low side binds; its counts come from structured moments that are already smaller. Also: the window where the bound is not mean-value-optimal is still D^(1/2) < K < D^2, which corrects c10 item 1.

nodes.name: RS-1: matrix Dirichlet series over the regular representation of (Z/q)^* with the bridge square
nodes.statement: Stage A, for the displayed candidates (K), (E), (Q), (H) only. Every bridge object built from M_q lies in commutative C[G] and is a direct sum over characters (Lemma S). The vector 1 is in the cone and is the chi_0 eigenvector, so each cone-quantified statement restricts at v = 1 to a scalar statement about zeta; for (K) and (E) that is H_c^zeta >= 0, which is RH (Lemma P). (Q) at threshold o(1/phi) is a restatement. Entry positivity is character orthogonality and ends at s = 1; the functional-equation matrix has negative entries. Not a theorem that no inequality on M_q exists (cone-preservati
nodes.lesson: Periodicity carried by a finite abelian group representation decomposes with the functional equation character by character, so it adds no inequality. The only extra datum is the cone, and the cone contains the Perron (zeta) direction unconstrained. A CROSS-1 candidate needs a non-commutative or non-decomposing carrier, or a step that reads "every coefficient matrix is a permutation matrix" together with the functional equation; E_a and T-NR pass everything else.

nodes.name: RS-1: twist-modulus reciprocity of twisted second moments
nodes.statement: Stage A. J_p(s;a) = 1 - sum_chi |F(s,chi)A_chi(s) - 1|^2: for X >= p-1 with free weights sup_a J = 1 - #{chi: F(s,chi) = 0} (zero-one law, a restatement). The reciprocity (three-term identity at s = 1, odd characters, distinct odd primes) moves the twist into the modulus but reads only periodicity and the functional equation of the twists; the target's s <-> 1-s is read in 0 steps. T-NR's twisted second moments are a nine-term combination of zeta's at every s, so T-NR passes steps S0 to S4 and its S5 is false at its off-line zeros. Not established: E_a pass for candidate (C), centre statements
nodes.lesson: Twist-modulus reciprocity uses periodicity plus the functional equation of the twists (conductor aspect), which is the 7/8 read set; it never reads the target's s <-> 1-s, so it is not an RS-1 device. Moving l into the modulus reproduces the n4 wall (Moebius signs on moduli, conductor >= length). Any device whose steps are family positivity plus identities linear in Hecke twists is passed by T-NR as a finite Hecke polynomial at q.

nodes.name: RS-3: de Branges shift positivity and its variants
nodes.statement: Stage A. The entire-function condition implies zeros on the line and cos Delta_h >= 0 at every zero (Delta_h = sum over other zeros of arctan(h/(gamma_n - gamma'))); the weight form implies Delta_h = 0 mod 2 pi at every boundary zero. False for zeta: zero 34 at h = 1 (Conrey-Li, reproduced); weight form fails at the first zeros for h = 1, 0.25, 0.1 (measured). The (a,h) weight family is false for every conclusion half-plane sigma_0 <= 1 relative to Bohr (recalled). V1a = T3 and V2 = G6 are restatements. No Euler-product step. Not established: every-h failure in the entire-function form, tied c
nodes.lesson: Shift-accretivity conditions of de Branges type test bounded imbalance of zeros at a fixed scale at every zero. The Euler product (independence of p^it) is what violates this, so the device runs against R1. Contractivity of the same shift is the classical Hermite-Biehler property and is RH-neutral. Backward heat was not evaluated at the zeta-failing step; no failure at h <= 0.5 was measured below 1e4.

nodes.name: Bost-Connes crossed product C*(Q/Z) x N^x with Fourier duality
nodes.statement: Stage A, for three classes of states (sigma-invariant, type I dual extension, archimedean vector Mellin families). Sigma-invariant states factor through commutative C(Z^); vector states with Poisson summation read {L(s,chi)} and the inequality is a square; positive-definiteness of zeta(sigma+it)MF holds for sigma > 1 and fails on 0 < sigma < 1 (zeta(sigma) < 0); Weil's prime side is phi_{1/2}(H_g), a rewriting. T-NR is Tr(D e^{-beta H}) with D >= 1 a positive element of C*(Q/Z) and passes every step. Not covered: other states (e.g. weights on the type II_infinity dual at beta <= 1); no candida
nodes.lesson: Non-commutativity of the carrier is not read by the states that carry positivity: sigma-invariant states see only the commutative algebra C(Z^), and vector states with Poisson summation return the split over Dirichlet characters. T-NR is a bounded inner perturbation of the Bost-Connes dynamics by a positive element of C*(Q/Z), so any device invariant under such perturbations is passed by it. Round 10's reason "KMS read set is beta > 1" should read: KMS states exist for every beta > 0 and read finitely many local factors at real beta.

nodes.name: Depth-aspect (characters mod p^k) transfer of height by termwise exchange
nodes.statement: Exchange step (E). Lemma X: for an r-datum with s terms, H = p^ceil(k/r), |t| >= t_r and N >= H((kappa |t|/1.12)^(1/r) + A), every character mod p^k and unimodular c has max_{n<=N,(n,p)=1} |chi(n) - c n^(-it)| >= 0.479/s. So no termwise exchange for N >= about (q|t|)^(1/r). In the 7/8 format the depth characters are already targets and as rows give Parseval; there is no height slot. Not established: |t| < t_r, the range between log q and q^delta, transfers not through termwise agreement.
nodes.lesson: Height and depth are independent coordinates of the dual of R_{>0} x Z_p^x: the analytic conductor is p^k(1+|t|), a product, and the two twists never substitute. Integers below N supply multiplicative relations (Prouhet-Tarry-Escott products, congruent mod H^r) that are trivial p-adically and non-trivial at the real place as soon as N exceeds about (q|t|)^(1/r). A periodic family cannot carry a height by approximating n^(-it); U is separated from periodic characters by this lemma, which is an obstruction for the device, not a handle on zeta.

nodes.name: Part B: Xu-Sang 2610.17675 Theorem 1.2 against slots Z11, M1, M2
nodes.statement: Part B, relative to unrefereed manuscripts. The structured prime second moment Q^2.084184 sits at prime length z = 1; M1 needs z < 3/8 at r = 0, M2 z < 3/13, no witness factor. As a Chebyshev count at Z11 it is never selected: N - delta - R0(delta) = 6(delta - delta*)^2/(15 - 6 delta) >= 0 and R(delta,x) <= R(delta,0); at the critical class 0.614839 against 0.590332 (would need below Q^2.059677). Abscissa stays 0.8748866470. Not searched: Z10 and the preliminary stage.
nodes.lesson: A structured moment proved as a supremum over bins of count times size squared cannot, by Chebyshev, improve the count it came from. An input can move the Z11 count only as a level moment with a witness factor at prime length beyond M1/M2 capacity. The substitution is blind to every target-side control.

nodes.name: de Branges shift positivity: backward heat at (N2) and tied conductor family V3b
nodes.statement: Cell 1: q_1 < 0 at on-line zeros for each of six tau < 0 tested (11 to 25 below height 500); forward heat tau >= 0.5 passes (N2) below 500 at h = 1; (N2) fails for zeta, so the condition is on the wrong side of the flow. Cell 2: for the tied weight the outer function drops out on the boundary; Lemma S (no zeros/poles of the weight in 1/2 < Re s < 3/2) and Lemma T (Re m >= 0 on Re s = 1/2) are both violated for q = 5, 7, 13 (zeros with winding 1; certified negative values). T-NR fails the same boundary step. S_v > 0 up to T_0(q) for the full odd family is a mean-value statement over characters.
nodes.lesson: In the weight form the outer function drops out on the boundary line (W(x-i/2)/W(x+i/2) = 1/(m |W(x+i/2)|^2)), so any tied weight reduces to a sign test of Re m on Re s=1/2; tying characters only helps as a conductor-aspect average (orthogonality, no multiplicativity) and fails in every fixed family at finite height. (N2) holds for forward-heated zeta and fails at tau<=0.2, so it is on the wrong side of the flow. One run whose output is used exceeded the 20-minute local cap by 41 s; three others were stopped late and discarded.

nodes.name: Control UNIV (joint universality) and the W-adapted cone cell
nodes.statement: (a) Relative to joint/hybrid universality (Matsumoto survey statements): a sup-norm-closed height-independent condition on a fixed window in 1/2 < Re s < 1 for finitely many Dirichlet L-functions that holds off a density-zero set of heights contains every non-vanishing analytic tuple; so such a condition is empty, a zero statement in the same window, or false on positive density. Narrow filter (27 of 34 devices out of scope), not numerically checkable. (b) Cone K_F = {v >= 0, Fv >= 0}: linear functionals are entrywise at x and 1/x; at q = 5 the F-fixed extreme rays give zeta(s)(1 + 5^(1/2-s))
nodes.lesson: A height-uniform local inequality on L-values in the open strip carries no arithmetic: it is empty, a zero statement in the same window, or false on a positive density of heights. This filter is narrow, because most devices read the completed function, kernels or coefficients, and its verdicts cannot be cross-checked at computable heights. In cone language, "automorphism at every prime" and "kernel with polar terms non-negative" separate T-NR and E_a only as inputs; no inequality over a cone consumes the first, since cone inequalities are preserved by every cone endomorphism.

nodes.name: Hecke/Fricke loading on the real oval of X_0(4)
nodes.statement: Decisive test. On theta restricted to the arc, the summed complex isogenous points of T_{p^2} are dilates of theta; Mellin multiplier C_p = 1 + 1/p - R_p, R_p = 2p^(-3/2)cosh((s-1/2)log p); the relation is the identity c(pm) = c(m). C_p*Lambda is -p^(-3/2) times a T-NR twin. <D_l, W> acts on a W-fixed vector through Dirichlet polynomials; M_{1/2}(Gamma_0(4)) is one-dimensional. Termwise bounds on complex points lose (p-1)p^(-1/2). Second moment over tau+b/p is map row G16. Closed for the four listed forms; not excluded: a functional of unsummed complex points that is neither linear nor a secon
nodes.lesson: Base-side loading on the oval adds no input. Summing the complex isogenous points over b projects onto dilates of theta, so every Hecke statement on the arc is a multiplier times Lambda. A non-commutative Hecke/Fricke algebra acting on a Fricke-fixed vector collapses to its commutative dilation part, and M_{1/2}(Gamma_0(4)) is one-dimensional. The complex-point term is itself a T-NR twin. A device on this arc must read something that E_a and T-NR lack, i.e. the size of the Hecke eigenvalue.

nodes.name: Bettin reciprocity at height t for the bilinear pair, read as an antibridge J-form
nodes.statement: Decisive test. The reciprocity is Voronoi summation for E(z, 1/2+it): the height is a spectral parameter, zeta's functional equation enters only through the gamma kernel, arguments are tied at (s+j, s-j); no kernel in two heights and no Hermitian pair at t != 0. J-form entries (q/pi)^(1/2) Z_chi(t) Z_chi(-t) are real with sign (-1)^(zero count in the window), fixed by the argument principle whether or not zeros are on the line. The only one-sided statement is squares on real characters (identity). Mixed-weight cone statement (Theorem 4(d)) measured on q = 5, 7 only.
nodes.lesson: A bilinear pair L(s,chi)L(s,chi-bar) on the critical line is a point value of a self-dual real function: its sign reads on-line zeros mod 2 and nothing off the line, and positivity of such entries is the property of E_a, not of zeta. The exact reciprocity reads the height as an Eisenstein spectral parameter with arguments tied at integer offsets, so it gives no kernel in two heights and no Hermitian pair at t != 0.

nodes.name: Fourier interpolation with zero nodes (Radchenko-Viazovska, Bondarenko-Radchenko-Seip)
nodes.statement: Stage A. The BRS kernel is (F*(s)/F*(w)) x A_k(w,s) with A_k independent of the target (relative to arXiv:2005.02996); bases of one gamma class form one orbit under symmetric multipliers G(s)/G(w) (Lemma M, identity). The construction uses a Dirichlet series and a functional equation; the Euler product enters only through |mu| <= 1, which stops at Re w = 1. Off-line nodes move the partial-sum exponent from 1/4 to beta/2 < 1/2, compatible with the one non-identity inequality (exponent 1/2). 'Partial-sum exponent kappa implies no zero with Re rho > 2 kappa' is proved-rel in that direction only.
nodes.lesson: An interpolation basis with zero nodes is a universal object of the gamma class divided by the target. The target enters linearly through the coefficients of 1/F, so the device is covariant under every symmetric multiplier with zeros in the open strip and T-NR passes. The only Euler-product reading is the size bound |mu|<=1, which stops at Re w = 1. Hecke covariance of theta sits in the target-independent kernel factor, as in c12-x04.

nodes.name: Borel Eisenstein series on the loop group of SL_2 (affine Weyl shift)
nodes.statement: Stage A. Coefficients are chain products of M(u) = xi(u)/xi(u+1) at u = z+kc, kc-z; in the chamber 0 < Re z < Re c every denominator argument has Re > 1 and strip arguments occur only as numerator zeros (relative to the recalled Garland / Fleig-Kleinschmidt-Persson normalisation, sources not opened). Rank-one Maass-Selberg positivity for all T >= 1 is equivalent to N = z(1-S)/(1+S) being Nevanlinna in z^2 (proved) and is preserved under Blaschke factors over non-real conjugate pairs anywhere in Re z > 0 (proved), so it gives no constraint on numerator zeros. Scope: rank-one proved; closure for
nodes.lesson: Positivity of truncated Eisenstein norms and Langlands-Shahidi non-vanishing act on denominators xi(u+1), which stay at Re >= 1 wherever the mechanism applies; strip arguments are zeros of scattering coefficients, and the inequality is closed under inner (Blaschke) factors. The affine Weyl shift moves the chamber, not the information. Pre-filter for any scattering carrier: does the inequality survive multiplying the coefficient by a Blaschke product over non-real conjugate pairs? T-NR with c>2 is such a product.

nodes.name: Luo-Rudnick-Sarnak twist amplification on E*(z, rho/2)
nodes.statement: Stage A. At xi(rho) = 0 the completed Rankin-Selberg function has one simple pole pair, but at P = 2 - beta; the gamma pole read by the mechanism is at 1 - beta, so pole minus parameter is 1 for every beta. The vanishing forced there is the trivial zero L(0,chi) = 0 of even chi, an identity for every parameter. The inequality reduces to beta <= 7/4 (vacuous; exponent count reconstructed, paper not opened). Same for Borel Eisenstein data of any rank at regular parameters. Open cell without a candidate: non-Borel Hecke eigen-object with parameter rho, entire twists and pole strictly left of 2 -
nodes.lesson: Cuspidality enters LRS three times: entire twists, a single Rankin-Selberg pole, and that pole's position P=1 (square-integrability). A zero supplies the single pole but not its position: for Eisenstein data the pole sits at 1 plus the parameter in every rank, and the forced vanishing at the gamma pole is a trivial zero.

nodes.name: Search for a non-cone sign functional of the theta-normalised kernel separating L-functions from the control battery
nodes.statement: Registered question, outcome 'none' (MEASURED, finite search). Dictionary D (minors of orders 2-4 of K(u_i + log n_j); Turan-type expressions, also Hecke-compensated; kernels with and without polar terms; at most 3 real parameters): 12,994,697 functionals x 290 objects; none is one-signed on zeta and the characters q <= 13 and opposite on a battery member of every control class. Of 629,432 functionals one-signed on the positives, 0 reject battery DH and 400 reject backward heat. The positive condition itself does not hold out (held-out L-functions q 14-40 opposite at mean rate 0.287). Lemma H
nodes.lesson: Sign functionals of the theta-normalised kernel up to order 4 do not separate Euler products from the controls: the character kernels break the Polya-frequency sign pattern more often than E_a, backward heat, EIS-w and theta^w do, so anything one-signed on the L-functions is also one-signed on those classes and on the battery DH function. Backward heat only pushes order-2 expressions further in the direction log-concavity already gives (Lemma H). Total positivity of a local coefficient sequence says nothing about dilation minors of the kernel (T-NR prediction refuted). Float64 is blind where polar terms dominate (about 20% of entries) and gave one wrong sign on a cancelled polar kernel before a noise rule was added; ball arithmetic was needed there.

nodes.name: T-NR invariance pre-filter (Lemma P) and census of non-cone inequality types
nodes.statement: Pre-filter and census. Lemma P: T-NR with c > 0 satisfies every hypothesis of type S1 (linear identities), S2 (dilation-invariant convex cone conditions on objects linear in F) and S3 (conditions at primes other than p0); exclusions X1-X5. Device table: 13 of 37 types carry a T-NR record, 0 disagreements. Lemma L: T-NR weights totally positive iff c >= 2. Lemma E: the xi-kernel of E_a inherits every Polya-frequency order. Census of 12 non-cone types: no entry fails both T-NR and E_a at an unconditional input of zeta that another control does not pass; order-4 theta-kernel minors fail both in m
nodes.lesson: T-NR and E_a are separated by complementary kernels: translation-type determinantal conditions on the xi-kernel cannot fail E_a (convolution) and fail T-NR at order 2; theta-kernel conditions of order 1-2 with the constant term cannot fail T-NR (cone) and fail E_a. Total positivity at one prime is ordered against the target: it holds exactly when parameters are real and non-tempered. Low-order minor signs of the theta kernel follow its constant term, so zeta and primitive characters differ.

nodes.name: Joint-pair designs: ratio L(chi)/zeta winding, cross bridge Gram of (S_zeta, S_chi), twist-transfer Weil form
nodes.statement: round 14, score 0, referee holds: Stage A, all three candidates. J1: winding and Littlewood quantities of L(chi)/zeta are signed differences of member zero counts; a multiplier common to both members cancels (Lemma C, PROVED: T-NR at p0 = 1 mod q has identical ratios for any finite character set). The step that would give a statemen
nodes.lesson: The twist relation is a property of the character and holds for every pair lift, so a pair functional that consumes it exactly cancels the prime side and leaves an archimedean form. Functionals of the ratio are blind to common multipliers (T-NR at split primes). Sign (comparison in every window) and size (density in q) compose formally in Lemma A, but the comparison link is equivalent to the target and on all but q^(theta+eps) twists is the scalar zeta statement.

nodes.name: Search for a sign functional of a kernel pair (F, F twisted by chi) separating L-function pairs from nine lifted control classes
nodes.statement: round 14, score 0, referee holds: Registered question, outcome 'none' (MEASURED, finite search, lane-defined lifts). Dictionary DJ (mixed dilation minors of orders 2-4, Hermitian minors and forms, Turan cross expressions, with and without polar terms, at most 3 real parameters): 38,101,627 functionals x 833 pairs. Of 4,266,644 funct
nodes.lesson: Reading a kernel together with its character twist does not help: for HEAT, BLS and T-NR the twist commutes with the control's defining operation, so the control pair is the image of (zeta, chi) under one map applied to both members, and functionals homogeneous in each kernel see only monomial distortion (none at all for JC2 without polar terms, Lemma J1). Requiring one sign on (chi, chi') pairs as well cuts the one-signed set fivefold; held-out signs can follow the twisting conductor rather than the class, so held-out positives are essential. Caveats: finite search with lane-defined lifts; most signs float64 (PZ-tier counts not ball-resolved; no ball for the theta^w twist); referee is the author; a 2-core unit overlapped the 16-core unit for about a minute.

nodes.name: Lax-Phillips resonance states measured in norms built from the Hecke algebra (outside the energy norm)
nodes.statement: round 14, score 0, referee holds: Decisive test: in four families of norms the growth bound is the definition of the space or implied by admissibility. (a) A solid space containing a resonance state and the bounded compactly supported functions contains the constants, so ||T_p^k|| >= (p^(1/2)+p^(-1/2))^k; on the mean-zero subspace o
nodes.lesson: On the channel that carries the resonances, T_n is a sum of wave-group elements at times log(d/d'), so a Hecke-built norm is a wave-growth norm and the Hecke multiplication rule is an identity the wave group supplies itself. Positivity-based norms stop at the edge because constants are forced into the space. EIS-w and the non-arithmetic control pass every step where an inequality is proved. Not excluded: non-solid norms outside the four families treated.

nodes.name: Luo-Rudnick-Sarnak count on the weight-1/2 Eisenstein series on Gamma_0(4) at s = 1/4 + rho/2 (theta-orthogonal eigen-object)
nodes.statement: round 14, score 0, referee holds: Stage A, decisive first test. At s = 1/4 + rho/2 the whole square-index row vanishes (factor zeta(2s-1/2)/zeta(4s-1), Lemma 1'; not the single condition b(1) = 0: the odd-p Hecke relation gives odd squares only). The vanishing annihilates the first-moment (Shimura) series and does not change the gro
nodes.lesson: A zero can change a Rankin-Selberg pole pattern only through a constant-term coefficient, not through a Fourier coefficient. In rank one the dominant exponent survives whenever the Laplace eigenvalue is non-real, so pole minus gamma pole is 1 on every cover and for every vector. Vanishing of the square-index row at one cusp is a property of the vector, not of the zero.

nodes.name: Catalogue of twelve proved inequalities consuming a Hecke eigen-relation, with zero-indexed objects O1-O3 substituted
nodes.statement: round 14, score 0, referee holds: Paper lane. None of the twelve catalogued inequalities has all hypotheses met by O1, O2 or O3 at a zero in the open strip. Lemma T (PROVED): for a torus parameter every L(s, Pi, r x chi) is a product of shifted Dirichlet L-functions and rightmost pole minus rightmost local/gamma pole equals 1 for ev
nodes.lesson: A zero in the strip removes the constant-term coefficient whose argument is in the strip, never the one right of 1. The template "zero supplies cuspidality, a theorem contradicts it" is the classical proof on Re s = 1 and stops there. Inequalities that read an object through L(s,Pi,r x chi) cannot bound a torus parameter: pole and local pole move together for every r. Every catalogued bound below 1/2 needs L2, pole at 1, spectral membership or unitarity.

nodes.name: Control ZQ = zeta(s) m(s) with zeta's own functional equation and off-line zeros, for read classes U1 {FE, GEOM} and U2 {FE, SIZE}
nodes.statement: round 15, score 0, referee holds: U1 {FE, GEOM} and the SIZE branch of U2 are not control-free. ZQ = zeta(s) m(s), m rational in s(1-s) of degree 0, keeps zeta's functional equation, pole, order, N(T) and every prime-power atom of log zeta, has zeros at 1/2 +- eta +- i gbar, and its defect is an absolutely continuous density with su
nodes.lesson: With zeta's functional equation fixed, the family is zeta times a symmetric multiplier. Small-defect controls are absolutely continuous (rational multipliers); discrete ones sit at distance >= 1. A U1/U2 device must name the step that reads absence of coefficient mass off log N, or the sign of Lambda against a density of size O(eta^2+d^2); otherwise ZQ passes it. T-NR in symmetric normalisation already had zeta's FE (map row NR), so "no control on file has it" was imprecise. Process note: the first run of checks.py wrote checks.json to the repo root, where an untracked checks.json already existed; that root file is now absent and its earlier content may have been overwritten. The lane copy was rebuilt from checks.log and the script now writes next to itself.

nodes.name: Quantitative Eisenstein edge argument with a Hecke amplifier on the truncated norm of E*(z, rho/2)
nodes.statement: round 15, score 0, referee holds: Stops at the decisive first test. At a zero rho = 1 - delta + i gamma the truncated norm is exactly |xi(2-rho)|^2 T^delta/delta (Maass-Selberg), and at T = 1 the device inequality is the identity M = L + S. On truncated Eisenstein data T_m acts as a combination of truncations at dilated heights, so
nodes.lesson: An amplifier isolates one term of a spectral sum; it cannot improve an inequality whose two sides are one explicit vector with exactly known norm. Here the loss sits in two inputs outside the norm: a sieve lower bound for the divisor-type mean and sup|zeta'|. On truncated Eisenstein data Hecke operators act only by dilating the truncation height (same structure as rows G26, D9), so EIS-w and BLS pass the amplified part verbatim. The device is not in class U1: FE and local data are joined by an identity. Also: a spectral formula derived at a zero is not a check at a hypothetical delta (one reporting error corrected).

nodes.name: Stage-A read of klein-phase-transport-certificate joined to lemma-w-wide-support; repair of sentence E1; second reader on 15 silent nodes
nodes.statement: round 15, score 0, referee holds: The pair stops at stage A. Lemma W(A) (for all T >= T0) contains the strip |beta - 1/2| <= 1/(2A) as its own large-sigma part (kappa = 0, verified height not needed) and is strictly stronger than that strip at multiset level: a target-level hypothesis. The Klein certificate concludes Re xi'/xi > 0 a
nodes.lesson: A zero sum weighted by T^(c d) with c > 1 is a pointwise statement above abscissa 1/c: let T go to infinity to read off the strip before typing it as a density statement. A window certificate requiring R <= pi/(4M) cannot be sign-definite at height when M >= c log t. Scripts must write output next to themselves: my first run used a relative path and overwrote an untracked repo-root checks.json left by another lane (not recoverable; recorded in RESULT section 9).

nodes.name: Search for a non-homogeneous functional (quotient, logarithm, product kernel) of kernel pairs and triples separating L-function data from lifted control classes
nodes.statement: round 15, score 0, referee holds: Registered outcome 'none' (MEASURED finite scan, float64 with undecided pair-family nodes resolved by a reflection identity (360) or in balls; exact in the last real parameter except minors a2/a3; lane-defined lifts). Dictionary DN: 2,898,030 pair family-nodes (T-train 0), 1,598,273 quotient minors
nodes.lesson: Dividing or taking logarithms does not escape the Gaussian-multiplier blindness: any read unchanged by a common pointwise factor is passed by backward heat exactly, and the reads that are not (single-kernel log curvature, polar terms, convolution against pointwise product) still fail on HEAT or because the positives disagree among themselves. Solving the threshold parameter exactly makes a 3-parameter search exhaustive in one parameter at low cost.

nodes.name: U5: largest number of windows at height T passed by a translate, free-prime or interpolation control
nodes.statement: round 15, score 0, referee holds: Outcome (a): a control exists at every K = T^a, a < 1, at fixed tolerance. For windows inside one span [T, T+L] the translate zeta(s + i alpha), alpha ~ 2pi/log(T/2pi), has relative FE defect pi L/(T log(T/2pi))(1+o(1)) on the whole span (PROVED to leading order), optimal among translates with |alph
nodes.lesson: The number of windows is not the controlling variable. Against translates only the relative spread of heights counts (L/T >= eta log(T/2pi)/pi), and adjacent windows cost about 0.36 real conditions each, not 30. STRATEGY 4.0 (b) should speak of conditions at heights whose ratios differ from 1 by more than eta log T/pi, not of sqrt(T)/log T windows.

nodes.name: U7: Fejer-tapered sections of the prime chain with P = t^theta read through J-contractivity on the gamma one-port
nodes.statement: round 15, score 0, referee holds: Class U7 closes as a row. For the Fejer-tapered section L_F(s) = sum_rho K_u(s - rho) with Re K_u >= 0 on Re w >= 0, so J-contractivity on Re s > 1/2 at every P is a Fejer-smoothed form of Re xi'/xi > 0 and of map row P45 (the Weil form): the limit step is sound (Harnack, Vitali) and the stage inequ
nodes.lesson: A tapered section makes the limit step sound (the positive-real class is closed and Harnack gives compactness), which moves the whole target into the stage inequality at unbounded P. Tying P to t^theta only weakens the target to (argued) a neighbourhood of the line of width c/(theta log t). Band-by-band square-root bounds do not separate zeta from random sign chains; the one-sided sum over all bands does, and that is the Weil form.

nodes.name: Hecke amplifiers with T < N on the truncated Eisenstein series: closed Gram formula and gain against N^delta, with EIS-w
nodes.statement: round 16, score 0, referee holds: Family 31 item 'T < N': measured obstruction on the stated range, not a proved closure. PROVED: T_m Lambda^T f = lambda(m) f minus pseudo-Eisenstein series cut at heights Td/a; coset c enters the pairing of cuts h_i, h_j iff c^2 h_i h_j < 1; closed Gram formula (G) for all T >= 1, N; R2 = 1 for T >=
nodes.lesson: Below the truncation height Hecke operators stop acting by dilation and coset terms cross the truncation line, but the effect is a bounded constant: under 1 per cent on the gain, and on the lower side at most the mass fraction the unamplified inequality drops below y = 1. EIS-w shares both. A pre-registered decision clause needs the control comparison written into it.

nodes.name: Proposition 5 of c15 (C(theta) against a zero-free region) decided for arbitrary configurations by Poisson rows and Turan power sums
nodes.statement: round 16, score 0, referee holds: C(theta) is not a zero-free region. A positivity statement at P = t^theta reads only the band-limited part (frequencies <= theta log t) of the zero measure. PROVED in window form: a lattice row of spacing 2pi/(theta log 2T) contributes the constant 2pi/d for every u <= theta log 2T and every offset
nodes.lesson: A positivity statement at P = t^theta reads only the band-limited part (frequencies <= theta log t) of the zero measure. Its zero-side reach grows linearly with the local number of off-line pairs and is not a zero-free region; one-pair heuristics overstate what such devices exclude. Passing rows are fine-tuned to about 100 P^(-b) in the ordinates. No step uses multiplicativity; ZQ passes in the window with 3 or more quadruples.

nodes.name: Ball-arithmetic conversion of the 67,138 float64-undecided canonical-tier nodes of dictionary DN and draw-stage recount of DJ
nodes.statement: round 16, score 0, referee holds: Registered outcome 'none' (MEASURED). On the registered c15 node set of dictionary DN, canonical tier {T-NR, E_a, HEAT}: 67,138 float64-undecided family-nodes decided in balls (360 reflection-identity; 37,634 excluded with HEAT not rejectable; 29,144 T-train; 0 undecided); 0 hold out under the c15 r
nodes.lesson: Use a relative acceptance test for balls: an absolute floor made 256-bit balls containing 0 count as decided. A hold-out read at one fixed threshold hides nodes that pass at another, and held-out positives repeating the zeta kernel do not test one-signedness; A-only families need a full character set.

nodes.name: Lemma POS-FE: zeta's functional equation, pole at 1 only, finite order and non-negative coefficients on [1, inf) force G = r zeta (Theorem P)
nodes.statement: round 16, score 0, referee holds: An identification, not a statement about zeros. Theorem P (PROVED; three independent referees hold): G = int_[1,inf) x^-s dN, N >= 0, (s-1)G entire of finite order, zeta's functional equation => G = r zeta, by Poisson-summation rigidity (triangle / sinc^2 test function; the one-dimensional LP-bound
nodes.lesson: With zeta's functional equation, positivity of Lambda acts only through non-negative coefficients of G, and that plus "no coefficient mass below frequency 1" is Poisson-summation rigidity (triangle / sinc^2 test function, the 1-dimensional LP-bound equality case). The {FE, POS} class identifies zeta without the Euler product and says nothing about zeros. Fully fractional LP relaxations are uninformative: their minimum falls like 1/K from non-integer multiplicities.

nodes.name: Filter Q-P / Q-B / Q-S / Q-A / HEAT over the silent cells U3, U4, U6, U8 and 71 geometric-program nodes
nodes.statement: round 16, score 0, referee holds: Lemma QA (PROVED): a step reading only the functional equation, poles, order, zero count up to O(1) and prime-power atoms is passed by ZQ; twist families by NR-q at every lift value. ZQ passes strict compact certificates and heat-box certificates (t >= 0) once the removed pair is high; M_ZQ is Schur
nodes.lesson: Every silent geometric-program node is target-level or passed by a control; ZQ passes finite certificates and atom-only steps inside zeta's own functional-equation class. The five cell rows with no passing control (U3 as an inequality, U4 residual, U6 c, e, f) all read the integers as an additive set (a reading, one reader). A critical-line step must be discontinuous in the coefficient measure at zeta: the margin is zero, f(eps) >= 0.48 sqrt(eps). Sign searches on compact parameter sets (U8, DN canonical tier) sit inside the flow-blindness wall: a survivor there is not a device with R3.

nodes.name: Cell U6 (g): Gram positivity of truncated rank-2 (SL3 minimal parabolic) Eisenstein data read off the zero set
nodes.statement: round 16, score 0, referee holds: Stops at stage A. Relative to the recalled rank-2 Langlands inner product formula (checked for M = 1 against the direct integral; source not opened), Gram positivity adds one condition to rank one: a zero of M with 0 < Re a < 1/2 forces a zero at 1 - a (Lemma R, PROVED), which is the functional equa
nodes.lesson: Rank 2 adds one condition to rank one: left-half zeros of the scattering coefficient must be reflected, which is the functional equation of the zero set. Reading f(z) = f(1-z) or the exact normalisation does not leave the Blaschke control: its symmetric form is zeta times a symmetric polynomial and stays positive on a larger set of T than zeta. The BLS control row's "lacks f(z) = f(1-z)" is wrong for symmetric zero sets.

nodes.name: U3 as an inequality: the discontinuity functional from Theorem P, Proposition M and ZQ in three relaxation directions
nodes.statement: round 17, score 0, referee holds: Target-level in all three relaxation directions; multiplicativity enters no proved step. PROVED: (1) the functional-equation defect enters Theorem P at Step 6 as int sinc^2 against the off-integer part of N, Lipschitz with constant 0.0485883; (2) Proposition W: zeta(s)(q^(s-1/2)+c+q^(1/2-s))/(2+c),
nodes.lesson: A quantitative identification ("defect delta implies zeros within f(delta)") on any class containing zeta at defect 0 is the target itself. What can be proved without the target is stability, which reads the functional equation and integrality, not multiplicativity. The sqrt(eps) reach is the discriminant of a function real on the line, not an arithmetic discontinuity. For a finite coefficient vector with a defective functional equation "a zero" is not defined by the data; the symmetrised functional used here builds the square-root law in and hides the linear shift mechanism (n^alpha: zeros at distance alpha, defect 1.14 alpha at X = 4000). A real-ray theta defect delta controls G only for |t| <= (4/pi) log(1/delta), so complex rays are needed. NR-q cannot be excluded through multiplicativity by any functional.

nodes.name: Cell U6 (e): positivity of non-invariant states on the Bost-Connes algebra against the twin ladder
nodes.statement: round 17, score 0, referee holds: Stops at the first lemma (stage A not passed). Lemma G (classical): omega -> omega(b* . b)/omega(b* b), b invertible, maps states to states in the same GNS representation; T-NR (b = D^(1/2)), finite DEL and the gauge twins have this form, so positivity of a state cannot separate them from zeta; only
nodes.lesson: State positivity is invariant under conjugation by any invertible element, so twins of the form b xi (T-NR, finite DEL) can be rejected only by an exact relation, never by positivity. The overlap of two product-vector states is either the convergent Euler product or 0: for beta <= 1 the states are orthogonal, so no function of tau remains that could read a zero.

nodes.name: Cell U6 (f): norm, Jensen gap and discriminant of the p^2+p-2 complex isogenous points of theta
nodes.statement: round 17, score 0, referee holds: Cell U6 (f) closed for three non-linear reads. Norm = theta(x)^(p^2+p)/(theta(x/p^2) theta(p^2 x)) (PROVED): a dilation-module identity with Mellin multiplier p^2+p-p^(2u)-p^(-2u) on zeta(u)zeta(u+1), so the read is a pointwise function of dilates. Jensen gap < 0 on the whole arc, limit log(p/(p+2))
nodes.lesson: For a Hecke eigenform with a product formula, both the sum and the product of the values at the isogenous points are dilation-module quantities on the arc, so any read built from the mean and the norm is a pointwise function of dilates. Epstein forms pass such reads prime by prime at inert primes; the discriminant sign is a parity count.

nodes.name: Restricted U8 search on dictionary DU (three or more monomials of distinct heat exponents), gated on Lemma H
nodes.statement: round 17, score 0, referee holds: Registered outcome 'none' (MEASURED, finite): 0 hold-out survivors on dictionary DU (minors of orders 5 and 6, sign and thresholded; three-term Turan forms on 5 and 6 nodes; K3 on [-4,4], Kpol on [-3,3]; lifts T-NR, E_a, HEAT with |tau| <= 0.005; thresholds scanned). Lane prefix 1,966,200 family-nod
nodes.lesson: A scanned-threshold hold-out read can be passed by an identification (threshold within 2e-52 relative of zeta's own value) when all held-out members of a class move the functional in one direction; register a minimum relative margin. The search code rounded breakpoints to 128 bits (conservative; 96 false "undecided", fixed by a post-pass). The copied ballk.BEA returns E_a balls of relative radius above 1 in a range of the Bessel argument; ballk.gauss_series drops tails whose float bound underflows. Server gave about 0.9 core for an 8-core unit; deadlines in the first driver were soft.

nodes.name: Window information law: every band-u positivity device as the quadratic form of one operator T_Z (replaces rows S12b, Q30, P45 addendum)
nodes.statement: round 17, score 0, referee holds: A band-limited positivity device has a density reach, not a zero-free region. PROVED (one referee): the complete band-u device is the quadratic form of T_Z on L^2 of an interval of length u (classical Weil/Yoshida frame; C(theta) tests modulated indicators only); n off-line pairs give exactly n nega
nodes.lesson: The reach of a band-limited positivity device is a density condition, not a zero-free region: off-line pairs hide only at local density of order u/2pi, and two bands are structural (P = sqrt(t/2pi) for count-preserving configurations, P = t/2pi for exactness). Multiplicativity is present exactly at every band (truncated Euler product in the truncated-shift algebra) for every multiplicative chain, so the missing input is a one-sided operator bound tied to the functional-equation reserve, not the factorisation. Above the Nyquist band only M = 0 has full power, and that is the target itself in a window.

nodes.name: Exact-relation rigidity: which exact relations stay admissible once multiplicativity is the relation (Hamburger, Theorem P, Klein seam, spinor square root)
nodes.statement: round 18, score 0, referee holds: Closes at the decisive test. Multiplicativity replaces no clause of Hamburger / Theorem P. FE clause deleted: TN1 = zeta(s)(1+q^(3/4-s)) is integer-frequency, multiplicative, non-negative, single pole at 1, zeros on Re s = 3/4. Pole clause deleted: HQ2 = zeta(s)(1+eps u^2/(1-u)^4), u = q^(1/2-s), ha
nodes.lesson: Rigidity on file is linear algebra in the coefficient measure (FE, integrality and the pole clause intersect in a line); multiplicativity is linear in a different coordinate (log G) and is never needed. The one clause that completes the identification, analyticity on the critical line, is the only one not stated right of 1. In the coefficient topology zeros are discontinuous even inside {FE, INT, MULT, N>=0}. Do not look for a control that fails through multiplicativity inside an exact relation.

nodes.name: Server run: certified sign of the completed band form and of N(theta), 1/2 < theta <= 1, zeta and control classes at heights 1e6 to 1e12
nodes.statement: round 18, score 0, referee holds: Registered outcomes (c) and (b) (MEASURED; signs certified relative to a hand-derived radius; 96 Fourier modes; 40 windows; 44,600 cells). (c) The registered reflected completion (atoms n -> t/(2 pi n)) is not a positive extension of zeta's data: zeta fails in 600 of 600 cells, and for every global
nodes.lesson: N(theta) with tolerance of order 1 does not separate zeta from multiplicative sign chains near theta = 1/2. Separation appears only toward the Nyquist band, where zeta's own margin goes to 0. The linearised reflected completion is not a positive extension of zeta's data. The server shares CPU per unit, so work has to be split into single-thread units.

nodes.name: One-sided bound N(theta) on the band operator T_Z with the reflected half of the approximate functional equation as completion
nodes.statement: round 18, score 0, referee holds: Stops at the first lemma. Exact identity (PROVED, classical in content; referee removed a spurious log|a_P| term): for a_1 = 1, a_P != 0, u = log P, h in H^1_0[0,u]: -2 Re<h, A_P h> = -u||h||^2 + sum over zeros beta of the partial sum D_P of the convolution forms e^((beta-1/2)|xi|). N(theta) is ther
nodes.lesson: Truncation of the prime data is exact at the level of logarithmic coefficients for any series with a_1 = 1, so N(theta) is a statement about the zeros of the partial sum D_P and uses neither multiplicativity nor the reflected half, which lies entirely outside the band. For theta' < 1 the conclusion holds for ZQ, so no argument for it can meet R3. The passage to target level happens exactly at theta' = 1, where the reflected half is exhausted.

nodes.name: Cell U4 residual (iv): multi-point group-law (3-4-1 type) inequality with every term finite left of abscissa 1
nodes.statement: round 18, score 0, referee holds: Stops at stage A (controls pass). Cell U4 (iv) closed for the read 'positivity-derived inequality on shifts s+ikt or powers of a character'. Lemma GL (corrected by the referee): the inequalities hold iff at each atom the evenly extended sequence k -> Re Lambda_k(n) is positive definite, so the group
nodes.lesson: A 3-4-1 inequality left of 1 is either a convergent test of the sign of Lambda (read set inside the P56 identification class; pole term dominates beyond log2/length of the line Re s=1) or a pointwise bound equal to the target. The group-law step reads each prime separately, so it carries no R1. T-NR is not a passer of log-level devices; with long tests it still satisfies the inequality at 0 of 1e5 random points negative (pole dominance), which shows truth of the inequality does not separate it. Incident: `$S:rh-push` expands as a zsh modifier; use `${H}:path`. A stray local directory from this (also holding a duplicate of another lane's fe_lp.py, original intact) was removed.

nodes.name: Cell U6 (c): Whittaker constants on covers of GL(3): cubic theta (Gauss-sum array) and the double cover (local dimension 4)
nodes.statement: round 18, score 0, referee holds: Cell U6 (c) splits; cubic half decided. Cubic theta on GL(3) (unique Whittaker model): tau(p^l1,p^l2) != 0 iff (l1,l2) = (0,0) or (1,1) mod 3 (recalled Kazhdan-Patterson criterion; l2 = 0 opened in Friedberg-Ginzburg 1403.3929; consistent with smoothed A_2 double sums at X = 1e5, 2e5 on 57 indices);
nodes.lesson: Where the Whittaker model is unique (cubic cover of GL(3)) the global constants are forced to be Gauss sums and add no object beyond rows Z14/Z15. Where it is not unique (double cover, local dimension 4) the squarefree-class constants are global period-type data that no Hecke relation reaches. Neither half gives an inequality: the cubic reads are identities shared by multiplicative twists, and the zeta controls have no lift to the cover.

nodes.name: HQ2 as a screen over 20 device rows that read functional equation + integrality + multiplicativity + positivity
nodes.statement: round 19, score 0, referee holds: Screen complete, no device type. Coefficient-level reads (FE, integer frequencies, prime-power support, N >= 0) reject HQ2 only by the pole clause. Three reads reject HQ2 by another step: (a) sign of the log-derivative coefficients at powers of q, removed by the new siblings HQ3, HQ4 (nu >= Lambda,
nodes.lesson: A one-prime twin with zeta's functional equation carries its off-line zeros and extra poles inside one local Euler factor, in Re s >= 1/2. Coefficient-level reads (FE, integer frequencies, prime-power support, N >= 0) meet only the pole clause; any read of local factor shape rejects the twin at that prime with no clause inside the strip; local positivity conditions do not (siblings HQ3, HQ4 with real poles right of the zeros pass them). Band devices order controls by distance of off-line zeros and by the pole lattice, not by multiplicativity. Compute note: repeated ball multiplication by a unit complex ball inflates radii about 1.4x per step; the first server unit was stopped and discarded for this.

nodes.name: Server run: band device N(theta) completed by the sign-change measure of the Riemann-Siegel main sum; defect against the prime-side data, zeta and controls at 1e6 to 1e12
nodes.statement: round 19, score 0, referee does not hold as written: Registered outcome (b): the device is closed by ZQ. The referee does not hold the lane as written (E1: 'sigma >= 0 for every point set' and 'T_sigma >= 0 on every band' are false as stated; repaired form: on m = 96, 192, 384 modes centred at t_w, T_sigma >= -3e-11 Lg); no number changes and the obst
nodes.lesson: A completion that is positive by construction moves all content into its defect against the data, and the positivity lemma reads only the defect's smallest eigenvalue. An off-line quartet enters that through a pair form that vanishes with eta, so the device can prove only N(theta) with tolerance, which ZQ satisfies (forced on paper before the runs, then confirmed). The two-sided defect does exclude every pair, but it is the target in the window. Mode count: completion verdicts do not change with m; data-form chain pass rates fall with m (0 of 192 at M = 0, theta >= 0.80, m = 384).

nodes.name: Cell U4 residual: inequalities quadratic in the log-derivative or reading phases at several primes jointly, on zeros of D_P
nodes.statement: round 19, score 0, referee does not hold as written: Stops at stage A (controls pass); the referee does not hold the lane as written (E1: the Liouville twist fails candidate (J) at p q^2 for P > 12; the lane's check at P = 10 saw only the atom 6); the obstruction stands after that correction. Candidate (J), cross-prime positivity of the pair form from
nodes.lesson: Sign relations between atoms at different primes do make T-NR and sign chains fail at a cross-prime step, but the read set is "all atoms in phase", which E_a, DEL and Liouville satisfy. Zeros of D_P at P = t^theta are blind to primes above P (K3), so any conclusion needs the functional equation at height t; with INT that is Hamburger's identification, and at theta >= 1/2 it is the target in a window (this last dichotomy is argued, not proved).

nodes.name: Cell U6 (c), double-cover half: (K3) as a 2 x 2 product test on genus-sum arrays of <1,1,d>
nodes.statement: round 19, score 0, referee holds: Registered outcome (i): cell U6 (c) closed as global period data without a Hecke relation. For primes p = q = 1 mod 8 with (p/q) = 1 the genera of <1,1,d>, d in {1,p,q,pq}, interchange local similarity classes at every place (proved), so a product-form array has K(G_1)K(G_pq) = K(G_p)K(G_q). The ide
nodes.lesson: A "pure tensor" test on period arrays needs scale-invariant inputs and quadruples matched by local similarity class, not isometry class. Fixed-n theta coefficient arrays are Siegel products yet fail the 2 x 2 identity, so "class numbers are not multiplicative" was the wrong reason for the Eisenstein row. The cusp computation was reachable without downloads: Hejhal data to primes below 3000 plus an invariance-validated GL(3) expansion; the largest m2 used was 167.

nodes.name: Commutator of the cutoff with Hecke dilations in the bridge energy
nodes.statement: D_p = [Q_c,V_p] = -P_c V_p Q_c has range L^2(c - 2 log p, c] and carries the prime only as a length. The defect form is -||Gamma_- D_p v||^2 (zero for one prime or any translation iff RH); in a-space it is the Weil form restricted to one-sided tests, independent of c. No multiplicativity is used. No bound on the negative index of the window operator follows from node matrices.
nodes.lesson: The cutoff commutator of a Hecke dilation is kernel-free and its range is a whole window, so any form built on it is the cutoff (Weil) form restricted to a window. That form separates kernels by the functional equation and by the height of the lowest off-line zero, not by the Euler product: non-multiplicative DH passes, completely multiplicative Liouville fails at 1e-8. The count of negative directions is set by test-space dimension, not by P.

nodes.name: Partial Euler products sampled at zeros (Krein zero sum R_S)
nodes.statement: No one-sided inequality on R_S separates zeta from the controls. The lower inequality R_S >= 0 for all tests is the target itself (P10). The upper depletion inequality is the Landau-Gonek mean value -2 sum_{p<=P} log p/(p-1); its every-window form needs a sup-over-height bound on a prime sum outside S and is unproved. R_S tends to 0 as P grows and a partial Euler product damps off-line pair weights, so the multiplier is not an amplifier. The exact S-periodised explicit formula (Lemma B) holds for every control with the functional equation and samples zeta'/zeta only on Re s = 1.
nodes.lesson: Putting the Euler product on the test side gives only a mean-value correlation with Lambda (Landau-Gonek); it hides off-line pairs (left partner damped roughly like exp(-li(P^(2 beta-1)))) and sends R_S to 0 as P grows, so it is not an amplifier. The local functional equation of zeta_S moves the trivial positivity range from support < log 2 to < log(2 N_S), at the price of sampling zeta'/zeta on Re s = 1.

nodes.name: Scale run: partial Euler products at zeros, heights 1e3 to 1e8
nodes.statement: The suppression of the truncated product at zeros is the Landau-Gonek diagonal term 1 - 2 c_P/L, a function of log P / log T: not uniform in height at fixed P, not uniform in window length (fails for 25-zero windows), and above 1 against the one-spacing shifted reference. It uses only the prime-power coefficients of -F'/F.
nodes.lesson: Suppression of a truncated Dirichlet series at its own zeros is the Landau-Gonek diagonal term. It needs only the prime-power coefficients of -F'/F, holds for DH at on-line and off-line zeros, and depends on log P / log T, so it cannot discriminate zero location. Shifts within one mean spacing are not an independent reference (they tend to half the mean); use the continuous t-mean.

nodes.name: Euler cone intersected with the functional equation in a window
nodes.statement: Exact uniqueness is Hamburger's theorem and uses neither the cone nor multiplicativity. In one window [T,T+H], lattice translates zeta(s + 2 pi i k/log(T/2pi)) are cone elements with functional-equation defect about (|alpha|H + alpha^2)/(2T), so the feasible set at fixed tolerance grows with T; a window gives about 30 real conditions against about sqrt(T)/log T free primes, and a prescribed zero at 3/4 + i t0 is feasible (float64 model, T up to 1e6). The multi-height constraint only says F equals zeta in the window.
nodes.lesson: The functional equation is linear in a(n) and the Euler cone is convex in log F, so "cone intersect affine space" holds in no single variable. A window of length H gives about 30 to 35 real conditions independent of T, against about sqrt(T)/log T free primes; pinning in one window needs H of Riemann-Siegel size. Windowed functional-equation tests cannot separate zeta from its lattice translates or from L(s, chi_5) at height T/5 (measured residual about 50/T). Stability around zeta can never exclude zeros uniformly because inf |zeta(3/4+it)| = 0. Multiplicativity only reduces N unknowns to pi(N) (cone pinned, relaxed model unpinned at T = 1e5 in the multi-height model).

nodes.name: J-inner linear-fractional sections in several delays, finite and infinite P
nodes.statement: A J-contractive several-delay section holomorphic on the full polydisc with Schur termination equals M(H)V0 with V0 constant J-unitary and Re H >= 0 (Lemma R): the defect is rank one and additive, so the family is the unipotent one. No nonconstant such section splits off xi'/xi (first-moment bracket >= 1.17 Re a_1 > 0). On 1/2 < sigma < 1 convergence either excludes the zeta orbit or is equivalent to zero-freeness. Not covered: sections on a Reinhardt shell; sections including the gamma term. Theorem A' has one referee pass.
nodes.lesson: The normalisation S(x) -> -1 (gamma growth) plus a maximum principle for the Potapov-Ginzburg transform forces any J-contractive multi-delay section into the unipotent family, so matrix freedom gives nothing. The first-moment no-go needs only the functional equation and a Schwarz-Pick bound on the coefficient pairing, not multiplicativity: it holds for DH too. Pointwise torus bounds are the wrong tool here (the integrand minimum is 1 - kappa^2/pi_P and would go negative for large P, while the bracket stays positive).

nodes.name: Multivariate (polydisc) Lee-Yang bound on renormalised Euler stages
nodes.statement: Polydisc stability gives exactly prod(1-|z_p|/R_p) <= |F| <= prod(1+|z_p|/R_p), i.e. |E_P(s)| <= E_P(sigma), the trivial bound. Any bound valid on a torus-rotation-invariant class is at least the torus maximum; a unimodular twist is a rotation. At fixed P, limsup_t |G_P(sigma+it)| = E_P(sigma), so no bound is both height-uniform and sub-trivial: R2 and R4 conflict at stage level. Not excluded: statements coupling P to height; stability regions that are not rotation invariant.
nodes.lesson: Stage stability classes are invariant under torus rotations, and a unimodular twist is a rotation, so no stability tool reads the angles t log p. U lacks no per-prime property; it lacks joint linearity of the angles in log p at bounded slope. Height-uniformity (R2) forces any bound on G_P up to the trivial one, so R2 and bounded renormalised stages (R4) conflict at stage level; a usable statement must hold t fixed while P grows.

nodes.name: Projection domination with the window-local Landau-Gonek prime side
nodes.statement: One off-line pair of depth delta forces |short twisted prime sum| >= 2|W| sinh(delta log N) - M_on, which is below the trivial Brun-Titchmarsh upper bound for every H, N and delta < 1/2 since N^delta < sqrt(N). Closing the gap is the zero-free statement. Only the support and size of Lambda are used. Referee: obstruction stands; the claim as worded is false in three places (the identity has a remainder of about H(8H/T)^7 log T and needs H = o(T^(7/8))).
nodes.lesson: Window-local explicit-formula identities are exact, so there is no error term to beat. The comparison that matters is off-line amplitude N^delta against the trivial sqrt(N) bound on short twisted prime sums, and closing that gap is the zero-free statement itself. Only prime-power support and the size of Lambda are used (inputs the sign twists keep); multiplicativity of the test polynomial D gives no gain. Every control with a symmetric zero side fails only at size or support; the Liouville twist passes every step. The averaged form is MV-CAP (P27, Q9, Z17); the single-window form stops at the Re s = 1 wall (P29).

nodes.name: One-sided bound in P at a fixed strip point for the renormalised Euler stage
nodes.statement: The Laplace transform in log P of G(P;s) has singular points w = 0 and w = rho - s for every zero at every height, so a one-sided bound Re G <= C P^alpha or >= -C P^alpha at one fixed point is equivalent (up to eps, with the exceptional ordinate t = gamma for the upper sign) to Theta <= sigma + alpha: the Landau target of rows T2/P10 in twisted form. No unconditional input is known to give the one-sided bound without the two-sided one (survey, argued). The step from fixed P to all P is the statement to be proved.
nodes.lesson: A one-sided bound in P at a fixed strip point is a global Landau equivalence, not a window statement: it reads zeros at all heights with weight P^(beta-sigma)/(|s-rho| log P), holds for every control verbatim as a criterion, and U lacks nothing at hypothesis level. The sign information (zeros, not poles) shows in Re G only at t = gamma. A fixed-height test with P <= Pmax cannot separate zeta from a control whose zero is farther than Pmax^(beta-sigma)/log Pmax.

nodes.name: Helson exceptional set on T^inf as a tail set; functional equation as selector
nodes.statement: chi = 1 lies in Helson's exceptional set E (pole at 1); E and E_zero are tail, flow-invariant, null, dense and comeagre, so no closed set, G_delta or rotation-invariant class contains the good set and misses E. A property holding at chi = 1 cannot be both tail-measurable and fail for finite modifications: strip zeros are a tail datum, the functional equation a one-orbit datum. Every every-window statistic that sorts E_zero correctly (Mertens sum, half-plane outer, band-limited window mean) is equivalent to zero-freeness. The band-gap identity for window means of log|F| holds for DH and E_a as
nodes.lesson: On T^inf the strip zeros are a tail datum (coset of chi under finite or summable changes) while the functional equation is a property of a single flow orbit, so a tail-measurable property cannot fail for finite modifications of zeta; Helson's a.e. statement does not reach chi = 1 (in E by its pole, E comeagre, Dirac mass singular to Haar), and every every-window statistic that sorts E_zero correctly is the zero-free statement itself.

nodes.name: Lemma B with poles shifted to Re s = sigma_0 and S growing with T, using the 7/8 half-plane
nodes.statement: With the residues bounded in absolute value through sup bounds of zeta'/zeta on a vertical line, positivity is certified only for support T_w <= f(sigma_0) log log T, f = (sigma_0-Theta)/((1-Theta)(sigma_0-1/2)), f(1) = 2 for every Theta including RH: the Littlewood scale X = (log T)^2. Support c log T is not reached; the 7/8 input gives nothing beyond absolute convergence or the classical no-multiplier Weil range 2 log log T - C. For sigma_0 > 1 the residue sum is the Weil prime sum. This is an obstruction of the bounding method, not a proof that positivity fails beyond 2 log log T; a signed
nodes.lesson: Any zero-free input (7/8 or RH) used through sup bounds of zeta'/zeta on a vertical line stops at the Littlewood scale X = (log T)^2, i.e. support 2 log log T; moving poles into the strip loses (log T)^(8(1-sigma_0)) against a gain N_S^(sigma_0-1) and growing S only adds small-divisor factors. Lemma B is the explicit formula regularised, with no sign of its own. Constants are T-independent, but only on a non-resolving class. Not run: DH form, Beurling, T-NR, heat, theta^w; Lemma 1 constants not numerical.

nodes.name: Referee of Lemma B (S-periodised explicit formula), DH form, Poisson test in k
nodes.statement: By Poisson summation in k the residue sum over the poles 1 + 2 pi i k/log p equals Weil's pole term minus the prime sum for the test Z_S w, truncated together: Lemma B is the explicit formula for a non-compactly supported test, regularised, with no sign of its own. The only inequality step is the classical zero-free region (Littlewood/Vinogradov-Korobov form). DH satisfies the identity, so nothing in it separates zeta. Proved for |S|=1; for |S|>=2 only for C_c^infinity tests, with a Baker-type bound whose constant was not checked against the source.
nodes.lesson: Lattice samples of zeta'/zeta on Re s = 1 (or on Re s = 1 - theta with a shifted multiplier) are Fourier coefficients of the periodised prime measure: any identity built from poles of a finite Euler factor on the test side is the explicit formula for a non-compactly supported test, regularised. The only inequality step is the classical zero-free region; it is false for DH but true for the height-shift twist, so it does not separate the controls. The sqrt(p) in Corollary B1 came from a worst-case profile estimate, not from zeta.

nodes.name: Adversary: unimodular Euler product passing the functional equation in m windows with an off-line zero
nodes.statement: For any fixed m, H, eta there is an integer alpha != 0 such that zeta(s + i alpha) passes all m window tests above a height T_0(m,H,eta) (phase identity, defect 2|sin(Psi/2)|; Dirichlet simultaneous approximation): no statement 'defect <= eta in m windows implies chi(p) = 1' holds with m and eta independent of T. In the finite model, unimodular Euler products with defect below 1e-9 and a simple off-line zero exist below a crossover m* of order pi(N)/30 (within a factor about 2; beyond it local search found none, no certificate). Past the crossover the conclusion is 'F = zeta on the window', wh
nodes.lesson: A window functional-equation test reads the analytic conductor, one phase and about 30 further real numbers per window; it never reads the Euler product. Multiplicativity only changes the unknown count from 2N to pi(N). Rigidity needs a window count growing like sqrt(T)/log T (Riemann-Siegel size), and lattice translates n^(-i*alpha) pass any fixed number of windows at large height (Dirichlet simultaneous approximation). Filter entry: a window argument with a T-independent number of windows fails against the unimodular twist.

nodes.name: Hermite-Biehler position of the Riemann-Siegel half-sum at matched height
nodes.statement: F_N(s) = sum_{n<=N} n^(-s), N = floor(sqrt(t/2pi)), has zeros in Re s > 1/2 at about one per five zeros of Z in every matched window tested (0.17 at 1e4 to 0.215 at 1e12; arb-certified lower bounds 5372, 7260, 8835 in windows of length 1e4 at 1e8, 1e10, 1e12). Smooth cut-off and unequal lengths do not remove them. By the Siegel/Levinson identity the family is the unmollified Levinson method with loss equal to the right-zero count; the mollified pivot is closed row P27. Positive density is measured or certified in finite windows, not proved for all heights. Multiplicativity affects the size of
nodes.lesson: Any splitting Z = 2 Re f with f a Dirichlet polynomial in the theta frame depends on |a_n| and the functional equation only: by a Gaussian second-moment model the negative-phase fraction is (1-r)/2 with r = c1/sqrt(c0 c2) < 1 (Cauchy-Schwarz), about 6.7% for the sharp cutoff. Multiplicativity never enters; the functional equation only confines the right zeros to within about 2/log N of the line. Close pairs of Z zeros (7 of 8 tested, including Lehmer 7005) carry a right zero of F_N nearby.

nodes.name: Twin ladder with a prime-built Hermite-Biehler chain (de Branges ordering)
nodes.statement: For every X >= 2 and every real symmetric normalisation, Theta_X = E_X^#/E_X has poles in Re s > 1/2 at 1 + 2 pi i k/log p, at 1 and at 3, 5, 7, ...; about T theta(X)/pi lie below height T, so the stage kernel has infinitely many negative squares and no stage de Branges or Pontryagin space or Hamiltonian exists. Adjoining a prime is neither contractive nor expansive; K_X(w,w) is not monotone in X. The negative-square count goes to infinity along the stages and to zero in the limit, which no monotone or semicontinuous device follows. The Euler factor is lossless only about Re s = 0; the functio
nodes.lesson: The de Branges kernel about Re s = 1/2 needs the stage at the reflected point 1 - s, where the Euler product diverges; the functional equation is not an input of any finite stage. Each Euler factor is lossless about Re s = 0 only, and moving the axis to 1/2 turns the Paley-Wiener chain into negative squares one for one (density theta(X)/pi). Zeta's own Theta about 1/2 is a Moebius factor, so its space is rank one with or without RH: the negative-square count goes to infinity along the stages and to zero in the limit, which no monotone or semicontinuous device can follow. Unimodular twists, Liouville, E_a, RZ_b and Beurling fail at the same step as zeta, so the construction does not separate controls.

nodes.name: Functional-equation-symmetrised Euler stage with Rouche against the approximate functional equation
nodes.statement: Gonek's stage P_X + chi conj(P_X) has all zeros on the line for any non-vanishing P_X: the on-line property contains no arithmetic. The Rouche (degree) inequality zeta/G_X not in (-inf,0] on a box boundary implies the box is zero-free and is implied (Gonek Thm 5.1) only by zero-freeness at sigma_0 - C loglog t/log X; nothing strictly weaker implies it, and at fixed X it fails at arbitrarily large height (Montgomery, recalled). The boundary quantity log zeta - log P_X - log(1+Theta) is a sum over all zeros; the approximate functional equation re-expresses it. With Fejer weights the k = 0 comb t
nodes.lesson: A stage whose zeros are on the line by construction (functional equation as input) carries no information in that property: it holds for any non-vanishing P, including U. All content sits in the comparison zeta/stage, which at fixed distance from the line is the Hurwitz comparison zeta/P_X (c1 Thm. D), and whose prime-side form is a two-sided bound on the prime tail beyond X at abscissa below 1 (Landau target, twisted local form). The FE term has modulus (t/2pi)^(-d); in the layer d <= 1/L it helps short products (X=2: 0 vs 76 crossings in 2000 units) and lowers the measured margin for X >= 100. Lead 13 is not answered: U fails only at the step that is the conclusion.

nodes.name: Power-saving discrepancy of a completely multiplicative unimodular chi versus a zero-free region
nodes.statement: Landau's argument on H = F F*/zeta^2 = exp(-2A), A a non-negative Dirichlet series, gives ord_F(s) + ord_F(conj s) = 2 ord_zeta(s) on Re s > sigma_0 (sigma_0 = top real zero of F in (theta,1), or theta): the hypothesis compares F with zeta and nothing else, so a zero-free statement for F right of sigma_0 is the same statement for zeta (circular). The proof does not use the additive spacing of the integers and transfers to Beurling systems. Real zeros of F unrelated to zeta can lie right of theta (measured: greedy thin twists have a double zero at b with discrepancy exponent near b/2), so f(the
nodes.lesson: Power-saving discrepancy plus Euler product compares F with zeta and nothing more: the proof never uses the additive spacing of the integers and passes the Beurling control unchanged. r1 is true only for this relative theorem (Euler product gives the non-negative series A; DH fails there), not for any conclusion about zeta. The planner's expectation that a thin twist has discrepancy exponent b was wrong: measured about b/2, so sigma_0 > theta on the evidence (not proved; a proof needs prime exponential sums over S). c3's bounded-discrepancy citation is corrected to Klurman-Mangerel-Pohoata-Teravainen, arXiv:1911.06265 (abstract only read).

nodes.name: Hecke operators compressed to the Lax-Phillips space; norm bound on resonance states
nodes.statement: On the Eisenstein channel T_p = U(log p) + U(-log p) = 2 cos(log p sqrt(-L)): a function of the wave group, defined for any group. Its compression to K is Z(log p) + Z(log p)^*, of energy norm at most 2 for every inner scattering function; resonance states are not its eigenvectors. For the uncompressed T_p in the weighted-L2 family admissibility of the resonance state already implies the eigenvalue bound; on finite spans a norm bound for all p is equivalent to resonance location; no positive-definite form makes T_2 and T_3 both symmetric on a resonance state. The only inequality obtained is Re
nodes.lesson: On the continuous spectrum of PSL(2,Z)\H the Hecke operator equals 2 cos(log p sqrt(-L)), so it adds nothing to the Lax-Phillips semigroup; all arithmetic sits inside phi, and the operator framework is identical for every inner function, including non-arithmetic groups and moved resonances. Any Hecke norm bound on resonance states is either implied by admissibility (weighted L2) or equivalent to resonance location. The truncation-Hecke defect lives on the window (a/p, a) and is the automorphic form of closed row G25.

nodes.name: Ramare / Matomaki-Radziwill factorisation as a source of every-window or one-sided statements
nodes.statement: (i) Bandwidth alpha in (1,2) in the inertia chain needs the Fejer-averaged Hardy-Littlewood error below X^(1/alpha) log X with H = X^(1-1/alpha): a power saving of exponent 1-1/alpha, against proved log-power savings (range H >= X^(8/33) recalled, source not opened). (ii) Outputs are mean squares on Re s = 1; the large-value count at threshold P^-a is T^(2a), against exponent 0 needed at a = 1-sigma to exclude a zero. (iii) Pretentious and log-averaged statements are invariant under finite modification and rotation (tail type), with tolerances (log x)^-A above the size x^(beta-1) of a zero ter
