nodes.lesson: The Matomäki-Radziwiłł family is a mean-value device on Re s = 1 whose saving is capped at a power of log (integers without a prime factor in [P,Q] have density about log P/log Q). Its conclusions are closed under linear combination, so DH passes: multiplicativity is essential to the proof, not to the conclusion class. A zero at beta < 1 enters at relative size x^(beta-1), below every tolerance in the family. Add it to the closed families under MV-CAP and tail type.

nodes.name: Law of stage-zero collisions and of the Rouche margin for the symmetrised Euler stage
nodes.statement: The prime-only exit event (double zero of the stage, Re D_X(1/2+it) = theta'(t)) is invariant under torus rotation and has a positive height-independent rate at fixed a = log X/log T (torus model followed to T = 1e20), so it carries no zero information. The Rouche inequality on Re s = 1/2 + c/log T fails at a height-independent positive fraction of sampled points for a = 0.5, c = 1, 2 (zeta 0.6-1.0% and 0.1-0.25%); whole-window passes occur only at (a=0.25, c=4) and (a=0.1, c=8) for T >= 1e8. The Davenport-Heilbronn two-character stage passes at comparable height-independent rates (1.3%, 0.6%)
nodes.lesson: The prime-only exit event of the Euler stage is invariant under torus rotation and has a positive height-independent rate at fixed log X/log T, so it cannot carry zero information. The Rouche comparison does not use the Euler product (the Davenport-Heilbronn two-character stage passes at the same rates and tracks its off-line zeros) and gives box counts, not location. Matching defect falls roughly like 1/a (0.05 spacings at a = 0.75) but no stage is exact. Ball products of ~1000 complex factors lose all precision by wrapping; sum logarithms instead.

nodes.name: Thin sign twist with a real zero in (7/8, 1) as a control for the 7/8 mechanism
nodes.statement: Control lane. The completely multiplicative eps = -1 on a thin regular prime set S gives F = zeta(s)(s-b)W(s) with a simple zero at any b in (1/2,1) (relative to a Hoheisel-type short-interval theorem cited from memory). In a walk of the 7/8 proof by hypotheses (not replayed), every multiplicative and local-size step holds for eps; the first unavailable step is Proposition 5.1 / Lemma 5.8: periodicity of the target weight to a ray-class lattice (also Lemmas 4.8, 8.1, 17.5). Proposition D: the low estimate (2.4) and the high comparison (2.5) cannot both hold for the eps-probe; which one fails i
nodes.lesson: Complete multiplicativity, unimodular parameters at every prime, continuation, the pole and density-one agreement with zeta at primes are consistent with a zero at any b in (7/8,1). The one extra input of the 7/8 mechanism is lattice-translation invariance of the coefficients: every sextic twist is periodic and has a Poisson dual uniformly in the modulus. It is used in the conductor aspect of a family, never as s <-> 1-s for the target. THIN passes local temperedness (table row 34), complementary to the one-prime twin Z18.

nodes.name: Angular family lambda^(6k) over Q(sqrt -3) and ring-class characters as a coherent set of exponent 1/2
nodes.statement: The transform in the family variable is Fourier inversion on a compact group with no Gauss sum; the root number is +1 (theta inversion; Froehlich-Queyrut recalled), so the Moebius coefficient is mu itself and the rows are Moebius sums of the family. For K <= Y^(1/2-eps) the probe equals its k = 0 row for arbitrary coefficients. The ray coherent set of exponent 1/2 couples s to conj(c) and, with corrected weight N(c*)^(-1/2), does not exceed the Cauchy-Schwarz level: net gain 0, abscissa >= 1 for all K, Y. The model ledger (1+kappa)/2 has its conclusion as input. mu is absorbed only through a n
nodes.lesson: A coherent set of exponent 1/2 is not enough: it must be coherent for every (s, c) pair, as squares are. In a group family (characters injective in the row parameter) the only uncoupled coherent row is the trivial character, which is the Moebius sum itself. mu is absorbed only through a nontrivial weight-1 cocycle of the epsilon factor (Jacobi sums, order >= 3); at order 2 and for characters trivial on a subfield's ideles the cocycle is a root of unity or 1.

nodes.name: Seven crossing devices outside the ROADMAP table
nodes.statement: Each device is closed by what it reads. Baker bounds and finite Turan sums read the frequencies log n only (every Dirichlet-series control passes). p-adic/Iwasawa data read zeta at non-positive integers only (the interpolation twin zeta + c L(s,chi_-4) L(s,chi_5) has the same values and a zero at any prescribed point). The tensor squeeze bounds local parameters only (every unimodular twist passes). Carleson/corona criteria assume S bounded, which is RH. The strip Dirichlet-to-Neumann identity holds for DH with its pole sum; the positive prime-side term is a vanishing fraction of the mean phase
nodes.lesson: Before work, ask what a device reads: frequencies only (coefficient-blind), discrete special values (passed by the interpolation twin), size of local parameters (passed by every unimodular twist), or the zero set itself (identity that holds for DH). Only the additive-against-multiplicative pairing fails both DH and the sign twists at non-identity steps, and that pairing is Vinogradov-Korobov, capped because log|zeta(1+it)| is unbounded. Device (b) is closed by argument, not proof; Turan's equivalence and other classical statements were cited from memory.

nodes.name: Prime marks with l - lx = 2: circularity of the order-2 branch
nodes.statement: Inside r3's reduced system (transcribed, not re-derived; uncompensated high side a guess; polar decomposition MODEL), referee does not hold the claim as written (one sentence of claim A false: r3's 'G = 0, l = 2' vertex is geometrically consistent). Standing: no geometry with marks outnumbering rows has abscissa <= 1; B = 1/2 is LP-feasible only at tall h = 3 points, where the needed low estimate |I| << Z^(lx/2+eps) (with DH and LH) is equivalent to GRH for the family; for h > 3 a low estimate below lx/2 + (h-3)/6 is false; on the compensated ray the abscissa is 1 minus the power saving in the
nodes.lesson: The heuristic's stated mechanism (GRH-strength prime sums against few rows) never occurs: that configuration is infeasible. The branch closes for a different reason: a comparison system reaching 1/2 sits at a critical point (h = 3) where its low input is equivalent to the conclusion, and any geometry-uniform norm or correlation package extends to h > 3, where it is false. On the tall compensated ray the abscissa is 1 minus the power saving in the TRO6 polar correlation, so TRO6 at large b is a restatement of the conclusion. Impose compensation geometry (M >= 2l, ly >= l) in every future LP.

nodes.name: Target functional equation inside the order-2 ledger: does reflection relax h <= 1
nodes.statement: Lemma U (proved, Prop. 2.1 format): the signal constant c of a probe J is an invariant of J, so no re-expression of the same probe (row functional equation, Voronoi, approximate functional equation) changes h. The reflection of the target variable is already manuscript Prop. 5.1 and is the origin of the K-loss; s <-> 1-s cannot act on 1/L without crossing the zeros. Exact LP in the source geometry (lx, ly >= l) with height w: infimum 13/15 at w = 0, reflected branch >= 13/15 + w/15, unreflected >= 1 with the polar term kept, 5/6 floor unchanged, r = 3, 4, 5 follow 1 - 4/(5r) and 1 - 1/r. Verti
nodes.lesson: The abscissa of a probe in the Prop. 2.1 format is (true exponent of J) minus c, and both are invariants of J (Lemma U). Re-expressing a probe can only improve the proved low exponent; it never moves the signal. The target's functional equation is already used in the conductor aspect (Prop. 5.1) and is the origin of the K-loss; s <-> 1-s cannot act on 1/L without crossing the zeros. Any route to h > 1 needs a different probe with lx < l, where the reduced system is inconsistent and the false input is not yet identified.

nodes.name: Discrepancy hypothesis for all additively twisted sums of chi, uniform in the modulus
nodes.statement: Strict form (no main term at q > 1): sum over a mod p of the twisted sums equals p chi(p) S(x/p), so any theta < 1 forces chi = n^(-i alpha) (chi = 1 if the main term is cx): an identification with no inequality; with S(x) = o(x) the hypothesis is the strip hypothesis itself. General form (main terms allowed): THIN passes with error O(q x^(b+eps)) (proved) and has a zero at b. For real chi the twisted series equals L(s,psi) exp(-A(s,psi)) right of sigma_0 without any twisted hypothesis. One referee; Lemma A step (c) to be refereed.
nodes.lesson: Modulus-uniform additive-twist hypotheses on a unimodular completely multiplicative chi are either an identification (strict form: only n^(-i alpha) passes, at any theta<1) or passed by THIN (general form). Periodicity of twists separates zeta from THIN and Beurling but carries no inequality. Separately: the greedy THIN set is biased in residue classes (mod 3 imbalance 26000 of 1.02e6 at 1e8), giving twisted errors near x^0.8; the random set does not show this.

nodes.name: Theorems B and C of the marks lane against the manuscript text; the h = 3 / GRH equivalence
nodes.statement: The reduced exponent system drops the normaliser H_eta = zeta_F^S(2)^-1 L^S(6s-3,(alpha eta)^6) E_eta of Prop. 2.1. H_eta has infinitely many zeros with 7/12 <= Re s < 2/3, so hypothesis (2.2) is false for sigma_0 < 7/12 and the format's unconditional conclusion stops at abscissa 2/3 (h = 2, effective order 3). Relative to an unsourced identity and high side: GRH => low input (N) => (R) [beta* <= 2/3 and top-layer zeros common with L(6s-3,(alpha eta)^6)]; (R) => GRH open. For h > 3 no low exponent below C(1/2) holds. Every h > 1 geometry has lx < l and lies outside all proved low estimates. In
nodes.lesson: A reduced exponent system must carry the normaliser H of Prop. 2.1, not only C(s). For the sextic rows H contains L(6s-3, infinite-order character), so the format's unconditional conclusion stops at abscissa 2/3 (h = 2, effective order 3); every h > 1 geometry has lx < l and lies outside all proved low estimates.

nodes.name: Probe bilinear in the target (bridge pair) in the Prop. 2.1 ledger
nodes.statement: The estimate system is degree-one homogeneous in the target-row length: the pair system equals the single c5 system at (lx/2, ly/2, (l1+l2)/2) (0 mismatches in 36,000 exact comparisons), so with both compensations h_pair <= 1 and the model values 13/15, 31/36, 5/6 are unchanged; with the full source ledger the least value at h_pair >= 1 is 52/57. The functional-equation pair (rho, 1 - conj rho) has product of size Z for every beta, so it carries sign information only and does not compose with the coherent set's size comparison. The shifted product zeta(s) zeta(s-d) is the E_a scaling. Points w
nodes.lesson: The estimate system is degree-one homogeneous in the target-row length, so any probe of higher degree in the target (pair, n-fold, unequal rows) is the linear probe at a rescaled point. The functional-equation pair product is beta-blind in size (Z^beta * Z^(1-beta) = Z), so the bridge's sign information and the coherent set's size comparison do not compose.

nodes.name: Degree-2 positive forms in zeta and companions (device map-open-9)
nodes.statement: Degree-2 positive forms split into three classes. Log-level squares are linear in -L'/L and lie in the P25 cone. Products of two log-level forms are non-negative at n = pq only if both factors are already admissible linear forms (Lemma Q; with companions relative to a cited Sato-Tate joint density). Coefficient squares sum |b(n)|^2 n^-s are non-negative for every sequence, invariant under every unimodular twist, and non-negative for DH (exact). For b = lambda_Pi the series is L(s, Pi x Pi~) H(s) and its Landau abscissa is fixed by the leading pole for every zero configuration: the device reach
nodes.lesson: A coefficient square |b(n)|^2 is positive without any multiplicativity and is blind to unimodular twists (THIN included). Multiplicativity enters only through factorising the series into L-functions, and at the leading pole every factor is evaluated on Re s >= 1. So quadratic coefficient positivity cannot see inside the strip, and DH passes everything except the factorisation.

nodes.name: Covariant squares of Q_L with an automorphic intertwiner: Weyl laws and Hecke rules
nodes.statement: A covariant square of Q_L is a Hilbert-Polya space, so sub-selection defeats every counting test. Fixed Hecke rules: no GL_2 cusp form has lambda_p = psi(p^(-it)) for continuous psi, nor P(lambda_p) = p^(-it), deg P <= 4 (Theorem H2; proved as written for trivial nebentypus; one referee); the eigencharacter of a zero is that of E(., 1/2 + i gamma) in the continuous spectrum. Casimir class: Weyl laws R^2 or R^3, never T log T. Compact at infinity: rank one closed; rank >= 2 without a Hecke rule open and carries no R1. Non-L^2 rank-one family: F(gamma_n) not constant, Euler-blind. The free Borel
nodes.lesson: A covariant square of Q_L is a Hilbert-Polya space, so sub-selection defeats every counting test; only exact tests decide (multiplicity one with Rankin-Selberg, or a single ordinate missing from the spectrum). Every fixed Hecke rule fails because the eigencharacter of a zero is that of E(.,1/2+i gamma) in the continuous spectrum. These no-gos are properties of the automorphic target and hold for all controls alike, so they give no R3. Check push/ for an existing lane before treating a STRATEGY lead as never run.

nodes.name: Anticausal Hankel block under the 7/8 input and the Proposition 2.1 family
nodes.statement: Gain 0. The gapped anticausal trace is sum conj(r_j) r_k e^(-(conj z_j + z_k) c)/(conj z_j + z_k)^2 over right-half-plane poles (finite pole sets); its decay rate is 2 min Re z_j, and a positive-weight family sum has the minimum over members. The 7/8 input bounds max Re z_j < 3/8 identically for one member and the family and bounds no count. The sum of bridge forms is the bridge of the product; the negative index adds over distinct off-line zeros. Every-window content is the input restated (row G20); below tilt 3/8 only family-mean (density) bounds exist (MV-CAP). Not covered: infinite off-lin
nodes.lesson: The 7/8 mechanism and the anticausal Hankel block read opposite ends of the off-line pole set: 7/8 bounds the largest real part (growth of the causal prime-side kernel, a half-plane device that is height-uniform), while the summed anticausal trace reads the smallest real part and the index is a count that no growth exponent sees. Family sums of bridges are either a direct sum or the bridge of the product; neither couples members, and for a positive quadratic quantity orthogonality keeps the diagonal. For unimodular twists n^{-i alpha} a family sum is literally a height average, so family bounds on the index are densities.

nodes.name: Proposition 2.1 probe in F_q[T]: does h > 1 occur in the region lx < l
nodes.statement: F_q[T], q = 7, 13, N <= 4. Base probe at lx < l re-expresses blocks with h <= 1 - M/2 (span identities exact to d = 6; pre-registered threshold not met literally at N = 2). Uncompensated marked probe: h = 1 + l - M/2 > 1 holds where RH holds, but the diagonal-level row bound it needs bounds the target's Moebius sum (Cauchy-Schwarz) and fails for the control weight mu with the same moduli (excess up to 6.3). Exponent-level equivalence argued through the uncomputed staircase r >= 7; threshold test undecided at N <= 4. Not computed: the compensated probe (12.5).
nodes.lesson: The h>1 vertices of the ledger at lx<l are real in the function-field model, but their low input (diagonal-level mean square of unreflected marked rows for N'<=d<2N') contains the coherent term, which is the squared signal. It is false for the Moebius-twisted weight with coefficients of the same modulus, so no sieve-type estimate can supply it. The ledger's sub-1/2 vertices came from omitting that term. Raw thresholds on h at N<=4 are dominated by O(1/N) terms, because the sixth-power count is constant for r<=5. Process: for about ten minutes my server requests summed to 18 cores against the 16-core cap, and two local runs bypassed memcap (one killed at 1.1 GB); both are recorded in RESULT.md section 9.

nodes.name: Mechanism of the 2026 Landau-Siegel claim
nodes.statement: The statement is a corollary of the locally compiled Dirichlet 7/8 theorem (c = (log 3)/8). The independent Lean tree (read as text, not compiled) uses an interpolation determinant over a box in Z[sqrt d, sqrt 2] with Frobenius-congruence divisibility against the classical prime bias of a real zero. The zero enters only through the bias at s = 1 + 1/log X: the device is empty for 1 - beta > c/log q and has no height-aspect form (n^(-it) is the failing control U). No R4 mechanism.
nodes.lesson: The proof's arithmetic half is an L-function-free field statement (inert primes carry at most 13/16 of the log-mass up to q^A, by product formula); the zero enters only through the classical bias at s = 1 + 1/log X, so the crossing has the classical width c/log q. The height aspect n^{-it} is exactly the failing control U. R1 holds only in the device's own class (real characters, conductor aspect), read from an uncompiled tree.

nodes.name: Sections of the prime chain on a Reinhardt shell, gamma one-port included (remainder of Q12/Q22)
nodes.statement: Laurent/shell class: first-moment bracket = 2 int F_P dmu, sign forced iff Re F_P >= 0 on the torus (zeta: iff sum arcsin p^(-1/2) <= pi/2; fails from {2,3,7}). Gamma-coupled class: mean 1 + conj(int F_P m), sign free (ARGUED and measured). No forced sign for zeta and none for DH, every statement holds for DH. Twisted first moments single out the reflected Euler stage, whose shell contractivity is the height-coupled reserve inequality log(t/2pi) > 2 sum log p/(sqrt p - 1) of g-passive-cascade. Limit step void in measure form. Open only: a section with P(t) growing like a power of t.
nodes.lesson: The forced sign of Theorem A' comes from Harnack on the polydisc, where the integer frequencies are the whole spectrum. Once a section has rational non-integral frequencies, or is coupled to the gamma ratio, the bracket is a torus integral of the P-part F_P against an arbitrary positive measure or unimodular function, and the sign is free for zeta and DH alike. First-moment signs cannot separate zeta from DH in any section class; twisted first moments single out the reflected Euler stage, whose shell contractivity is the height-coupled reserve inequality log(t/2pi) > 2 sum log p/(sqrt p - 1) already in g-passive-cascade.

nodes.name: General cap for probes of the Proposition 2.1 format
nodes.statement: No bound h <= 1 on the parameter (format gives h <= r/2). The abscissa is capped: square-root level + K-branch + floor-class high bound give B >= 1 - 1/r + lx/(2r) for all lx, ly, l >= 0 (exact identity; LP for r = 2..12), and the K-branch is the Hilbert-Schmidt lower bound of the reflected row operator, so no l2-l2 operator-norm (large-sieve) estimate passes it. The cap is target-independent (U, DH, THIN). Phase-blind low estimates have B >= 1 (ARGUED: aligned probe for the Liouville-twisted target). Only escape: a vector-specific mean square (E-K) of reflected theta rows for QP > Z, undecide
nodes.lesson: The 1 - 1/r cap does not need lx >= l: K-loss plus the trivial row bound suffice, and the K-loss is the Hilbert-Schmidt lower bound of the reflected operator, so no large-sieve (operator-norm) improvement can pass it. The cap is target-independent (holds for U, DH, THIN). The 31/36 and 5/6 tiers exist only under a non-operator, vector-specific row mean square. Inputs at lx < l are MODEL (no numbered source).

nodes.name: Uncompensated high side from MS (12.5)/(16.1) with the normaliser kept
nodes.statement: Dropping the compensation costs l*delta/2 on the high side and changes neither the signal nor the normaliser H_eta. Vertices with 1 < h <= 3 exist on the cone (t, t, 2t-1), but their single low input (K + D energy bound for coherent marked rows) implies their conclusion: marks are coherent at sixth-power frequencies, so the row energy contains the squared signal and B_low >= beta* for M >= 1 + l (Lemma C, ARGUED: needs control of non-sixth-power dual frequencies). The high-side line beyond the slot term S_i is ARGUED in the ideal model. Factorisation (10.18) holds only for Re s > (2 + theta_om
nodes.lesson: In the unreflected regime (rows >= columns) a Cauchy-Schwarz low bound with true norms is always at or above the signal, because coherent marks put the squared signal into the row energy; h > 1 by marks therefore needs an energy input that is itself the zero-free statement. Dropping the compensation costs only l*delta/2 on the high side and changes neither the signal nor the normaliser. Also: c5 tiers_fe2.log rows Y2, Y6 do not reproduce with the current script (0.9 and 0.8810, logged 1.0 and 0.9103). Disclosure: no server job was run; one ssh connection running only `true` was opened to the box.

nodes.name: Joint Hecke recurrence and measure rigidity on Eisenstein resonance states
nodes.statement: Referee does not hold the record as written: Lemma G2 (i), labelled PROVED, is vacuous (the DH-type object on Gamma_1(5) is identically zero; DH not run). Standing: truncated mass at a resonance is exactly Y^(2 sigma-1)/(2 sigma-1), free of gamma (Maass-Selberg); the recurrence bound is uniform in gamma with P-exponent -1 for every sigma in (1/2, 1), so it does not contradict the cusp growth; the off-resonance Eisenstein series E(z, w') satisfies every hypothesis the device reads, so the device cannot locate sigma; m_sigma is an A-conformal (not A-invariant) Hecke eigen-measure for every sigma
nodes.lesson: On the modular surface, "a step fails for U and THIN" is necessary but not sufficient: those controls fail only because they lack automorphy. The sharper control is E(z,w') off resonance, which keeps the group, functional equation, Euler product and Hecke algebra. A device there must read phi(w)=0, not the existence of a joint eigenfunction; under RH resonances sit at Re w = 3/4, off the unitary axis, so invariant-measure tools do not apply.

nodes.name: One statement for 'row energy at sixth-power frequencies = squared signal'
nodes.statement: The coherent term is the Cauchy-Schwarz step of Proposition 2.1 solved for the row energy: max_sigma E_sigma(Z) >= c_0 min(X,Y) |I_mark(Z)|^2 (relative to MS (6.2), (12.5), Lemma 6.2). The exponent statement (C1) of round-7 Lemma C follows only relative to the unproved high half (HC) and only if beta* > 2/3. In F_q[T]: E = S + Rem, Rem >= 0, S explicit at dual length 0 (exact). E >= D + S fails in the computed cases; a third Weil target has signal above the diagonal, so target and aligned control are not separated at these sizes. Not established: Lemma C reading (b), identity (3.2), threshold
nodes.lesson: The round-7 "coherent term" is the Cauchy-Schwarz step of Proposition 2.1 solved for the row energy, so it cannot give a conclusion without the format's high half. Lemma C stays a debt in its original form: later lanes may cite only "(C1) relative to (HC), beta* > 2/3" or the F_q[T] identity. The squared signal and the exact diagonal are not additive in the model, and a third Weil target has signal above the diagonal, so target and aligned control are not separated at these sizes.

nodes.name: Bridge form built from one completed probe row
nodes.statement: A cubic-theta row is T = L0 D with L0(s) = L(3s - 1/2, psi). The row's reflection axis Re s = 1/2 is Re w = 1 for L0, at distance 1/6 (in s) from L0's own axis Re s = 1/3. The reflection quotient of T about its axis has no pole from a zero of L0 (classical non-vanishing on Re w >= 1); where T(s_rho) != 0 (float fit at eight low zeros, one unweighted row) the zero is a pole of D with reflected real part (5/2 - beta)/3, which restates beta with no sign or rank condition. About Re s = 1/3 the form is H(T) - H(L0) with no sign from the row's functional equation. The target L(s, eta) enters a singl
nodes.lesson: A theta or Eisenstein-type row carries its Euler factor at the edge: its unitary axis is Re w = 1 for the L-function in its coefficients, 1/6 (in s) from that L-function's critical line. Bridges built on single rows land on the right-of-1 side of the R4 wall (Langlands-Shahidi / Sarnak setting). The target L(s, eta) appears only after the sum over rows, never inside one row.

nodes.name: (E-H): target excess of the non-principal row cancellation at r = 5
nodes.statement: F_q[T], q = 7, (k, N') = (6, 6), r = 3, 4, 5 (and (5, 5), r = 3, 4 by the referee): NP is a linear functional of the weight with a target-independent kernel (proved); the measurement places the targets inside the range of random vectors, which supports norm-type cancellation (linearity alone does not imply it). The pre-registered target excess over random multiplicative and random non-multiplicative signs is not detected at any size, including against 24 seeds per class at r = 5 (resolution 0.05-0.07 in the exponent). Second same-kind obstruction after c8-eh-nonprincipal-row-cancellation. MEAS
nodes.lesson: A gap of 0.1-0.2 in a cancellation exponent between single control weights is inside the seed spread (0.04-0.19 per geometry). Seeded control classes plus a pre-registered rule decided what one-seed comparisons in round 8 could not. Writing the row sum as a linear functional of the weight shows directly that row cancellation is a device property unless the target is unusually close to the functional's kernel; it is not (target a leans low at r = 5 in two of four geometries, target b does not).

nodes.name: Positive-term sum rules (Szego, Killip-Simon, Simon-Zlatos) on the prime stub chain
nodes.statement: Five forms: (i) window form = Littlewood's lemma, coefficient side 0 at every stage for every unimodular chain; the bound-state term is a tail invariant bounded from below only; (ii) mean form E + 4 pi delta = log zeta(2 sigma) is the classical density identity; (iii) at fixed stage no continuous functional of the phases separates zeta from U over window positions (Kronecker-Weyl, row Q21); (iv) the Simon-Zlatos difference condition holds for zeta on Re s > 0 and for THIN on Re s > b/2 with THIN's zero at b right of the line; (v) the H^2 point-evaluation step reaches only Re s > sigma_0 + 1/2
nodes.lesson: A sum-rule device outputs Lieb-Thirring (density) bounds; to give "no bound states" its coefficient side must vanish, and then its limit step is the target. Test any coefficient condition against THIN first: tail-thin sign changes keep every smoothness-in-delay condition while placing a zero right of the line.

nodes.name: flow functional x square-root lane x prime cascade
nodes.statement: A functional that vanishes on the critical configuration and is monotone along the heat flow must decrease forward, so it only transports information from t < 0 (where the conclusion is false) to t = 0. Differentiating the Hankel data in t does not change row Q4: the prime side is causal for every twist (argued) and the difference is the residue sum over zeros.
nodes.lesson: Reject combinations whose engine is a heat-monotone functional of the anticausal Hankel block or of zero configurations.

nodes.name: INT + GEOM input / compactness of dual measures
nodes.statement: The cofinal limit of dual-feasible points keeps none of nu_1(x) ~ sqrt x: integer unit steps against Y log Y force any bounded-discrepancy cofinal dual to density 0, and the LP optima live at t ~ x in x-dependent Moebius-resonant configurations that are not sections of one measure. A fixed cofinal b is controlled only in mean square (MV-CAP); the pointwise bound is the open Moebius sum sum_k mu(k) r_b(x/k) (the source's Step 7).
nodes.lesson: Do not re-run limits of optimal Legendre duals. The only open item is the pointwise sum of mu(k) r_b(x/k) for one fixed r_b.

nodes.name: one-height Landau transport with an Euler-product anchor
nodes.statement: The decisive test 2 pi^2 c > C fails for every fixed c > 0: the Euler product modulates the compression ratio q of adjacent zero pairs at the anchor by order 1/L^2 with both signs, above the trace x^{-C/(2 pi^2)} a past collision leaves. The anchor step returns its input half-plane (f(theta) = theta); the certificate needs S transport below the anchor, i.e. zero positions at the vortex height. Nothing below 0.874886647.
nodes.lesson: Any heat-time certificate must supply S transport below the anchor; the anchor alone separates no control. Graph repair: 'Prop L' in the proposal is the theta-collision Proposition L, not Lemma L of the contradiction file; the edge to landau-transport-lemma-l is a naming collision and that node is left out of the closed set.

nodes.name: one-sided Landau target through an exact bilinear identity
nodes.statement: After the forcing is removed by two linear conditions on the mollifier, every identity of this shape is a linear combination of the half-weight Legendre identity (1*Lambda = log) with symbol exactly 1 at every zero; at full level Lambda >= 0 is implied (system has the single solution Lambda), and the remaining one-sided polylog bound on K'[R] is equivalent to RH (Theorem OS). Positivity enters only in Landau's lemma.
nodes.lesson: Filter out any combination whose only new ingredient is a different Type-I/Type-II split or mollifier of this shape; a live route must use positivity non-linearly or the size normalisation that separates zeta from E_a. Restricted-level Legendre plus positivity is NOT closed by parity: it is the Legendre LP lane.

nodes.name: 7/8-type mechanism: effective order 2
nodes.statement: On double covers a Moebius sign on a quadratic symbol and centring on the unitary axis did not occur together in any computed case: the symbol enters Hecke relations as a Gauss sum over p, so the reciprocal sits at shift 1/2, cancelling the largest order-2 gain h/r = 1/2. Model abscissa 1 or detection only for beta >= 1.
nodes.lesson: Order-2 (quadratic) analogues of the 7/8 mechanism through theta or half-integral weight GL(2) forms are closed. Untested: genuine cusp forms on the GL(3) double cover; exact Whittaker coefficients of cusp-induced Eisenstein series.

nodes.name: Neron-Tate positivity x Nyman-Beurling span
nodes.statement: Averaging over discriminants cancels nothing: every Heegner bracket is of Davenport-Heilbronn type with off-line zeros. The NB ratio is 1 + distance^2 to the constant in L^2(dy/y^2): non-increasing by definition, smaller for a non-multiplicative control, and blind to a Blaschke floor (< 1e-24 above verified height) at values near 3. inf R = 1 would imply RH; no step bounds the distance; nothing passes from finite spans to the limit.
nodes.lesson: Reject Nyman-Beurling span combinations whose only arithmetic is the choice of spanning family. Open and not attacked: density of the family under RH/GRH; non-fundamental discriminants.

nodes.name: Euler phases and functional equation at one height
nodes.statement: The torus exclusion set is entered by the zeta main sum itself; the sign of the Laguerre expression is decided by the Riemann-Siegel remainder of size N^-1/2, so the statement is one-point with no margin (rows S4, Q13) and restates verified height. The coupling theta' = log(main-sum length) is the functional equation alone and holds for DH up to O(t^-2). Order-1 Laguerre detects an off-line pair only if 2/beta^2 > S(gamma).
nodes.lesson: On the prime torus the Euler product enters only as the identity of one orbit point. Any torus exclusion set needs tolerance |R| ~ N^-1/2 and has no margin. Diagnostic only: (orbit time fraction in B_N)/(torus measure of B_N) is 0.002..0.1 for zeta, 0.4..0.8 for DH, about 1 for translated orbits.

nodes.name: control with Euler product and functional equation; self-adjoint crossing
nodes.statement: Selberg zetas do not supply the missing control: the s <-> 1-s equation belongs to the order-2 function, while the degree-one unimodular Ruelle product has poles where Z has zeros, so every Landau-positivity mechanism holds with reversed inequality. Its off-line zeros are real and finitely many, so it tests nothing at height > 0. The Selberg companion for Theorem PC is closed: sigma* >= 1/2.
nodes.lesson: What separates zeta from the Selberg family is the integers (additive structure), order one and the sign of the zero side; filter new attacks on those. Do not re-attempt Selberg companions for Theorem PC.

nodes.name: propagation: one off-line zero forces many, then density
nodes.statement: A recurrence hypothesis whose returns each produce a zero is bounded by the zero count, so it is as strong as the zero-free statement (restatement). zeta_P never vanishes, so an off-line zeta zero is a Haar-null event carried by the tail beyond every finite prime set; Kronecker equidistribution gives frequencies only for sets of positive Haar measure. Closed at step 2.
nodes.lesson: Reject combinations whose amplifier is 'one zero implies many zeros' via Bohr sets or almost periodicity.

nodes.name: integers + all primes: pointwise Moebius sum of one fixed sawtooth remainder
nodes.statement: By Moebius inversion the sum sum_k mu(k) r_b(x/k) equals psi_b minus universal sums of mu(k)/k: for density 0 it is -c x m(x) plus a nonnegative O(log^2 x) term, so the pointwise bound is the pointwise bound on x m(x) (Mertens-type, RH strength); for density a > 0 it is the statement for e_b itself. Positivity of b contributes only a polylog term. Landau turns an assumed one-sided bound into Theta <= theta, never the reverse; every other input is a mean square (MV-CAP).
nodes.lesson: A Moebius sum of sawtooth remainders of a fixed measure holds for every coefficient sequence and returns the control's own exponent. Item 1 of 'least blocked after batch 1' is withdrawn.

nodes.name: filter lane: a twist control with an off-line zero, and the local-defect bound as a statement shape
nodes.statement: 'Zero offset <= local defect' is GRH with defects: for shifted L-function factors it is equivalent to RH/GRH for the factor with the largest shift, and an equality read off E_a silently assumes RH. Local defect is a property of the prime system, not of the function. RZ_b passes every prime-side identity and size inequality after s -> s+1-b and F -> 1/F, so a valid argument needs a step not covariant under shift and reciprocal: the sign of Lambda, or the position of the pole and symmetry line relative to the chain. The chain l^2 threshold sees only infinitely many primes (T-NR: threshold 1/2, z
nodes.lesson: Add RZ_b as a standing control: any step covariant under shift and reciprocal is defeated by it. The 9x7 control table is mostly ARGUED, not replayed.

nodes.name: 7/8 mechanism at effective order 2: rows from cuspidal objects on the double cover of GL(3)
nodes.statement: Order-2 rows need three conditions together: Moebius produced by the row, shift 0, and a coherent set of relative size 1/2. Signed Waldspurger coefficients at product indices give none (signs at random level); square classes give the first and third only at shift 1/2, the case closed by e1-gl3-theta-order2-rows. Transfer to the Eisenstein series on the double cover of GL(3) is by analogy only (field hypothesis of Brubaker-Friedberg Thm 4.1 not met over Q; exponential sum H and coefficient index not derived).
nodes.lesson: Signed square roots of central values behave as random signs against mu*chi. Do not re-run GL(2) half-integral-weight product-index rows. Untested: explicit genuine GL(3)-cover cusp forms.

nodes.name: integers + positivity: restricted-level Legendre certificates, Riesz order x level
nodes.statement: Every certificate value is >= psi_k(X)/X^k, whose excess is Omega_+(X^(Theta-eps)) (Landau), so the certified exponent is never below Theta. From level D about 2 sqrt X the exact LP is Dirichlet's hyperbola identity and returns the truth for every Riesz order; Riesz order and level restriction remove only method losses (forced Moebius head, sawtooth triangle inequality). The residue is a one-sided bound for a Moebius-weighted spline sum over the Type-II range (source Step 7 / (DR)); the upper half of the sandwich is proved from M(y) << y^(Theta+eps). Positivity of Lambda is already spent; unif
nodes.lesson: Restricted-level Legendre LPs are pinned to the truth from D ~ 2 sqrt X for every Riesz order, so the exact LP carries no information. Do not re-run level x Riesz-order variations. The open residue is the Type-II one-sided Moebius spline bound, at RH strength; E_a is not separated.

nodes.name: 7/8 mechanism: one lemma with a confirmed model price
nodes.statement: A slot lemma uniform in bounded prime coefficients is sign-twist invariant on its slot side, and the cubic Gauss-vector configuration shows such a statement cannot exceed capacity m/2 at r = 0. A relaxed slot must use the specific coefficients (prime sums of a Hecke character times a Moebius sum), i.e. a GRH-type below-level estimate ((M1+), unproved). Not established for the sextic rows of the lemma or for r >= 1/2; non-principal configurations and the two-Poisson recursion are untraced. Reduced-model tests at U <= 5e5 have no power for slots shorter than U^0.4.
nodes.lesson: Do not look for a coefficient-uniform relaxation of the slot condition. The price even if relaxed is small (abscissa stays above 13/15).

nodes.name: renderer spin sign x 7/8 probe: period on the 6-fold cover
nodes.statement: The rows are complex conjugates of the additive Gauss functions up to mu(c) Psi(c), so the signal form and the Gram form share matrix entries: no grading or linear operation on the row variable (the Z/2 factor of Z/6 included), the modulus class or the Hecke grade distinguishes them. Any separation must come from the modulus weight mu(c) Psi(c), which is the tro6-period (MB) form already recorded. The proposed period is Z/2-odd and vanishes. NOT established (referee): that the exceptional P_a^(1/6) term has a definite Z/6 or Z/2 character; the measured 'index 0' concerns the diagonal k = 0 ter
nodes.lesson: Gradings on the row variable cannot separate signal from exceptional term. The renderer spin sign has no arithmetic counterpart here. The pivot (mu as the Hasse-Davenport constant) returns positive-list item 33.

nodes.name: 7/8 mechanism: functional equation of the theta-dual m-series
nodes.statement: The m-reflection is target-blind Gauss-sum algebra (same for every eta and for DH). It lowers x only from points with 2x+z < 3/2 where nothing is known; every chamber it adds lies in x >= 3/2, so the hull abscissa equals the input. Its chamber is reached only by meromorphic continuation across the zeros of the Kubota normalising L-factor, and a hull of a meromorphy tube gives no control of the polar set. Existence of the functional equation for the full m-series is open; order-6 equations cannot be tested by dual lengths at norm 1e7 without the S-data matrix.
nodes.lesson: A second reflection in the modulus adds no region below the input abscissa. Side finding: the 8-piece set of n1-tube-hull is not closed under symmetry transport, so its piece rule is argued, not proved.

nodes.name: 7/8 mechanism: joint detector scales and a class-restricted fourth moment
nodes.statement: The restricted fourth moment (H) and the two-scale detector are not independent inputs: both reduce to a count saving at the saddle pair (r*, m*), whose cheapest open form is the one-scale below-level mixed moment (N < 1.1366) or (M1+). The binding numerator block is m* = 0.4183, not m = 1/2, so a central-only saving is worth at most 1.13e-4. Lemma 18.1 admits no Moebius-coefficient factor at central length. Finite-U numerics cannot test (H): no zero-carrying rows exist in the sample and true rows match random multiplicative rows. (H), (TS) and the one-scale mixed moment remain open.
nodes.lesson: Do not combine (H) with detector scales again; the three items map-open-2, map-open-13 and target-0874-restricted-moment are one item (count saving at (r*, m*)). True rows are exact conjugate duplicates in the sample (halve reported counts).

nodes.name: Overflow onset of the cosh completion at s0 = arcsinh(1)
nodes.statement: Degree-0 bridge mass B = sinh(aU)/a - U; raw deficit D_0 = [cosh(aU) - sqrt2 + arcsinh(1)]/a - U; margin B/D depends on s = aU only. Excess fraction phi(s) has a double pole C/(s - s0)^2 at s0 = arcsinh(1), C = 0.16776, and decays exponentially; its integral diverges at onset.

nodes.name: p=2 resonance blow-up at t_k = 2 pi k/ln2 blocks every local or finite-rank pole bridge past ln2
nodes.statement: Un-weighting by (t^2+1/4)^{-1} is nonlocal and breaks the support constraint. The direct Krein positive extension has pole directions concentrated on the same p=2 resonances. E_S o Q grows linearly along t_k=2 pi k/ln2 for every 2a>ln2. The ln2 obstruction is shared by the local, finite-rank and fixed-measure class.

nodes.name: P47 late-cell WOL-C floors (cells 417-424)
nodes.statement: Lambda < 0.145 by route P needs 125 missing P47 late-cell floors; cells 417-424 (0.88 sharp) need point bound + 0.008 and stalled at 0.10-0.19. Floors are suprema over the Kronecker torus with all prime phases free and carry no height coordinate.

nodes.name: p-adic interpolation and the Iwasawa module read zeta only on s = 0, -1, -2, ...
nodes.statement: The Kubota-Leopoldt function of zeta for each p, and the characteristic ideal of the Iwasawa module (Mazur-Wiles), are functions of the values zeta(1-k), k >= 1. A device built on them for all p together passes the interpolation twin unchanged. Under the functional equation the data are the values zeta(2k), right of 1. No comparison between p-adic zeros and complex zeros is known outside function fields, where both are roots of one polynomial.

device.evidence: c5-device-table-extension; interpolation twin zeta + c L(chi_-4) L(chi_5) passes

nodes.name: Montgomery form factor versus GUE on Odlyzko zeros
nodes.statement: Empirical F_N(alpha) of the first 1000 zeros against 1-(sin(pi alpha)/(pi alpha))^2; nearest-neighbour spacings of the first 10000 zeros against the Wigner surmise (32/pi^2)s^2 exp(-4s^2/pi). F(alpha) is proved only for |alpha|<=1 under RH.

nodes.name: Pair correlation is rearrangement- and beta-blind in short windows
nodes.statement: Ordinate-only pair / n-level statistics are consistent with any rearrangement in windows of length o(T) and do not see real parts. Loss-free count certificates pass only at w <= 2 (lattice) / 4 (GUE mean) spacings. Obstruction map P31.

nodes.name: Pair kernel: D_t(x) = int Q_t(v) cos(2xv) dv
nodes.statement: With K_t(u) = e^{tu^2} Phi(u), D_t = H'^2 - H H'' has D_t(x) = int Q_t(v) cos(2xv) dv, Q_t(v) = int u^2 K_t(v+u) K_t(v-u) du. D_t >= 0 for all x is positive-definiteness of Q_t, a u^2-weighted self-convolution; positivity of K_t does not give it.

nodes.name: Insensitivity lemma: n-level statistics are beta-blind
nodes.statement: A normalised pair or n-level statistic with fixed bounded compactly supported test changes by O(H (log T)^{c_n}/T) when zeros in windows of total length H are changed; so GUE + O(T^{-delta}) is consistent with moving zeros off the line in windows shorter than T^{1-delta}. Point-set statement only.

nodes.name: Palm two-slot mirror count trails its mean by 1/y0
nodes.statement: Neutral rigid lattice, spacing 2 pi/ln N, mirror kernel 2[2y/(D^2+4y^2)], y0 = 0.165: palm2(ln N) = ln N/2 - 1/y0 + o(1), 1/y0 = 6.0606, so frac = 1 - (400/33)/ln N; 0.5345 at ln N = 22, 0.9879 at ln N = 1000.

nodes.name: Parity AM-GM factor 2 is Gram-sharp
nodes.statement: The boundary Gram G* = tridiag(1; rho*), rho* = 1/(2 cos(pi/(K+1))), is PSD with lambda_min = 0 and lambda_max = 1 + 2 rho* cos(pi/(K+1)) = 2 exactly for every K >= 2, attained on the lowest sine mode. The factor 2 cannot be lowered from adjacent-block Gram data.

nodes.name: Parity-pure MAJ witness class and its certified rate threshold
nodes.statement: Chain of cluster-correlation caps (rate thresholds 9/20, 2/5, 69/250, 1/4, 0.24505, 0.23208) against explicit witnesses: Theorem DW gives a two-packet-in-block witness with certified class lower end 0.2320723; satellite-bulge witness has hollow lambda_max = 1.000000176 at mu = 0.2320723.

nodes.name: Twin-ladder / Volterra machinery does not apply to partition parity
nodes.statement: Applicability assessment against the Parkin-Shanks conjecture on p(n) mod 2: fails; no kernel with the needed self-duality exists.

nodes.name: Annular cofactor as adjacent Pascal/carry mean comparison
nodes.statement: RH iff C_N<=S_N eventually, with log(S_N/C_N)=2760N(mean_{345N<=u<529N} log K_u - mean_{225N<=u<345N} log K_u), K_u=(u+1)^u/(u! rad(u!)). K_u rises at composites, falls at primes. v_3(S_{3^L}/C_{3^L})=-4923*3^L+15, so divisibility, pairwise and per-block proofs fail; cross-factor cancellation is open.

nodes.name: Euler product as lossless sections converges only for Re s>1
nodes.statement: The cascade identity S21*zeta=const is established from the Euler product on Re s>1 and extended by the identity theorem; no passivity or contractivity statement of the infinite cascade transfers into the strip. Obstruction map row G10 (and Q10: chain is l^1 only on Re s>1).

nodes.name: Analytic ceiling for the cosh passive core
nodes.statement: For all f in L^2([0,U]): Q(f) = int sinh(a tau) f^2 / int cosh(a tau) f^2 <= tanh(aU) < 1, sup not attained; operator form (P - H) >= (1 - tanh(aU)) P. Scalar-core statement; extension to the rank-2 matrix core depends on which shear is meant.

nodes.name: Passive delay realization of the finite inverse Euler ratio
nodes.statement: An ideal passive scattering network with prime-indexed delays realizes the attenuated inverse finite Euler ratio; the bridge h is a pole-zero damping separation, not a Hermitian coupling. The forward response W_Q is not passive; no infinite-cutoff transfer.

nodes.name: No closure route is both PCC-free and not RH-equivalent
nodes.statement: Enumeration: twin-ladder routes A/B/C/D, Volterra, normalised R / mu^pass and the off-diagonal Hankel cover are each already RH-equivalent (Theorem 16.1 plus section-26 verdicts). The target set {pair-correlation-free AND not shown RH-equivalent} is empty.

nodes.name: PCC route exhaustion: 11 routes, 4 families
nodes.statement: Eleven closure routes for Montgomery pair correlation (5 moment-method, 3 new-input, 2 RH-equivalents, 1 sieve) audited; verdict: genuinely open pending new input. Five of thirteen paper conjectures are subsumed by RH.

nodes.name: Theorem PCR: a zero-free pole-coupled model at rho_0 exists iff zeta(rho_0) != 0
nodes.statement: Because g = 1 (G = zeta) lies in the class, Lemma Z(rho_0) is equivalent to zeta(rho_0) != 0. Any argument built from Euler product, pole, domination and Landau positivity alone reproduces zeta's zeros. DH has 461 negative Landau coefficients for n <= 3000.

nodes.name: Coulomb self-energy of the mirror quadruple is anti-confining
nodes.statement: F_C''(0) = -4S < 0 (Earnshaw): the log-gas self-energy of an off-line quadruple pushes it off the line; only arithmetic phase cancellation confines, and boundedness of R_sigma(t) as sigma -> 0 is Weil positivity on Gaussian probes.

nodes.name: Route D: defect-pair free energy is not confining as modelled
nodes.statement: F(delta) = -log(2|delta|) + 2 sum_p p^(-1/2) cos(gamma ln p) sinh(delta ln p). The prime term is odd in delta (zero curvature at 0, nonzero tilt Re Psi(1/2 + i gamma), e.g. -0.7635 at gamma_1); the Coulomb term is a barrier at delta = 0 decreasing in |delta|.

nodes.name: Per-site flow depth s_k = c g_k^2
nodes.statement: Collision time tau_c ~ g_k^2/8 and the Gronwall floor-pinning depth both scale as g_k^2, so running each pair backward only to depth c g_k^2 keeps the floor exp(-2s/y^2) non-vacuous. A single global depth makes the Gronwall floor vacuous (intrinsic). Scaling estimate plus one RK4 run.

nodes.name: Per-window number-variance residual is Gaussian at accessible heights
nodes.statement: The per-window (C-E) residual on zeta zeros passes Kolmogorov-Smirnov at six heights (KS 0.030-0.08 below 0.886/sqrt(n)); extreme-value comparison shows Gaussian tails without anomalous spikes; the raw tiling has positive lag-1 correlation, so windows are not exactly independent.

nodes.name: Theorem U: permutation architecture is A_{k,h}-universal
nodes.statement: Algebra generated by T_p=diag(1_{p|n}), p<=97, equals span{T_d: d|P}=span{c_q: q|P} (Ramanujan sums), dim 2^25. Every freeze-calculus word is a basis choice on one number; no in-algebra mollifier removes alias content. Single alias has in-algebra energy 1/phi(q).

nodes.name: Permutation atlas: isometric families give no gain
nodes.statement: All 25! prime orders, divisor / 25-defect / five-shell / Heat-Euler fibre forms and DFT / chirp / bicomplex / twistor isometries are conditioning or alternative coordinates only; budgets cannot be added.

nodes.name: Permutation defect: reordered operator product within sum of commutators
nodes.statement: For contractions T_1..T_m and a permutation pi, ||prod_pi T - prod T|| <= sum over inversions (i,j) of ||T_i T_j - T_j T_i||; a bubble chain hits each inversion exactly once. Weighted form for non-contractions.

nodes.name: Phase-blind no-go for the Lambda<=0.14 family |C_E,17|<R_ex
nodes.statement: Five-shell orthogonality plus reproducing kernel gives at best rho_RSS=sqrt(sum|z_g|^2)>=m/sqrt(n); at shell mass m=0.919 the floor 0.41099 exceeds R_ex=0.27969 for every mass distribution. Any phase-blind bound fails; signs of the alias amplitudes are needed.

nodes.name: Phase-priced signed seam certificates
nodes.statement: With theta the phase-alignment ratio of the signed packet family: R <= e^(-y_min)/(2 theta) (PHASE-CERT) and R(f) <= (e^(-y_min)/4)(1 + 1/theta) (PHASE-AM), from entrywise L_mn <= (1/2) e^(-y_min) M_mn and an orthant cross-term drop. The 1/2 ceiling is broken on co-centred families.

nodes.name: Phase retrieval: |zeta| on one line fixes zeta up to off-line flips
nodes.statement: G = e^{i alpha + lambda(s - 1/2)} xi prod_S B~_rho(s)/B~_rho(1/2) (9 configurations per off-line quadruple). FE + reality force +-xi. Two lines (Poisson-Jensen) locate every zero with beta > 1/2 without the FE (DH: 8 off-line zeros below 400). Hilbert phase defect on the line <~ 1.48e-12 t.

nodes.name: Twin-ladder phase tomography carries no information beyond Hardy Z
nodes.statement: Reality of Z(t)=e^{i theta(t)}zeta(1/2+it) forces theta(t)+arg zeta(1/2+it)=0 mod pi, so the tomographic phase observable is determined by S(T); the ladder axis is transverse to Lambda.

nodes.name: Twin-ladder shift axis commutes past the heat-flow axis
nodes.statement: Ladder phase tomography (Hardy Z decomposition) is circular on the line; the shift d/da is transverse to d/dt of H_t, so ladder phase data carry no Lambda information unless a deformation with non-vanishing commutator [d/da, H_t] is constructed. None was found.

nodes.name: Phased forcing of the Dyson flow loses effect with N
nodes.statement: A resonant forcing (k0* ~ 2 pi/min_gap, tuned phase velocity) reduces the collision statistic by a factor 185-111 at N = 500, but the reduction factor degrades with N at fixed (k0, omega).

nodes.name: Super-exponential law of the Phi autocorrelation A(tau)
nodes.statement: A(tau) = int_0^inf Phi(s) Phi(s+tau) ds satisfies -ln A(tau) = pi e^{4 tau} + c_inf + (3/(2 pi)) e^{-2 tau} + O(e^{-4 tau}), c_inf = -ln((pi/2) Phi(0)) = 0.354292284; Watson remainder |rho(tau)| <= 3.46 e^{-4 tau} (numerically verified).

nodes.name: Positivity range of the truncated kernel Phi_N
nodes.statement: Phi_N (N theta terms) stays positive left of the last per-term sign flip u_1* = (1/2) ln(3/(2 pi)) = -0.36963; leftmost zero u_0(N) ~ (1/2) ln(5/(2 pi N^2)) with Gaussian-curvature correction coefficient 5/(14 pi) and subleading -3/4.

nodes.name: PICK-ID: the seam pencil is a Nevanlinna-Pick matrix
nodes.statement: P(rho)_ij = (rho^2 - w_i w_j)/(nu_i + nu_j) = (rho^2 G - D G D)_ij with w_i = e^(-d nu_i). Hence Lambda(nu,d) = min ||g||_inf^2 over bounded analytic g on the right half-plane with g(nu_i) = w_i; every interpolant certifies an upper bound (NP-CERT) and the minimum is attained.

nodes.name: Theorem PICK-WEIL: Weil form on exponentials is a Caratheodory-Pick matrix
nodes.statement: On span{e^{-nu t}1_{t>0}}, nu>1/2, the Weil form equals [(xi'/xi(s_i)+xi'/xi(s_j))/(s_i+s_j-1)], s=1/2+nu; the prime side is (Z_i+Z_j)G_ij with Z=-zeta'/zeta(s), not a free signed lattice sum. Checked with 869 zeros (tail 7e-7).

nodes.name: PICK-WEIL: the Weil form on the exponential span is a Caratheodory-Pick matrix
nodes.statement: On E_V = span{e^(-nu_i t) 1_{t>0}}, s_i = 1/2 + nu_i > 1: W_ij = [xi'/xi(s_i) + xi'/xi(s_j)]/(s_i + s_j - 1). Positivity for all finite node sets is Lagarias' criterion (equivalent to RH); finite node sets follow from verified height. Obstruction map rows P3, P18.

nodes.name: Theorem PZ: a planted off-line zero enters the Legendre dual with factor zeta(rho_0)
nodes.statement: If zeta(rho_0) != 0, a single-cutoff plant (sqrt x <= T_0 <= x^{1-eta}) enters the sawtooth data with factor zeta(rho_0) and moves the LP objective by only O(kappa/|zeta(rho_0)| + kappa). Fake-zero gains stay O(1); valid from x about 1e28.

nodes.name: Pointwise number variance of zeta zeros sits at 0.35-0.48 of the GUE value
nodes.statement: On the first 10^6 zeros, the local count in windows of half-width Delta is calibrated in mean (|mean(C - E)| < 0.04) with std 0.57-0.67 zeros; r(T) = variance / GUE Sigma^2(L) lies in [0.35, 0.48], mean 0.40, T = 1e4..5e5, with no drift toward 1. Later module flags window-overlap bias.

nodes.name: RH as a Poisson representation with half-width 1/2
nodes.statement: RH iff q(t)=int dmu(u)/((t-u)^2+1/4) for one positive weighted measure mu (from the a=1/2 inner anchor B(w)=xi(w)/xi(w+1)).

nodes.name: Poisson domination of the left edge by prime tail energy
nodes.statement: Poisson domination removes the sum-frequency covariance and writes the variance as an integrated squared tail of the fixed prime coefficients; smooth density contributes at most (K^2/2)T^{-917/500} for Q<=sqrt T. Unique factorization gives moments up to order 12 outside an exceptional set.

nodes.name: Local-count channel capped at L/4; triangle method below de Bruijn ceiling
nodes.statement: S_t(x,eta) = -Im(H_t'/H_t)(x + i eta) is the Poisson(eta)-smoothed zero count, and any x-uniform lower bound q satisfies q <= L/4 + o(1). The Polymath15 triangle criterion at X controls arg H_t only above sqrt(1-2t) for t <= 0.137. Ideal B2 channel ceiling Lambda about 0.148.

nodes.name: Theorem PC: pole-coupled Landau positivity conserves zero mass
nodes.statement: For completely multiplicative g with |g| <= 1 and G pole-coupled at 1: r_G(w) + conj r_G(conj w) = 2 ord_w zeta for Re w > sigma*(g); N_g(x) = sum_{n<=x} Lambda(n)(1 - Re g(n)) is non-decreasing and O(x^{sigma* + eps}).

nodes.name: Pole-term bridge as a codimension-2 positive extension
nodes.statement: PW_a = P0 + span{cosh(x/2), x sinh(x/2)}, P0={hhat(+-i/2)=0}. Full Weil positivity from pole-free positivity is a rank-2 Schur-complement problem: the rank-2 pole block is positive but cross terms are indefinite. The Sonine route computes this Schur complement as D_S<=L_S.

nodes.name: Three orthogonal gaps between T_a[sigma_2]>=0 and full Weil positivity
nodes.statement: Axis I reach (certified 2a<=0.96; LP wall and Rayleigh direction are one obstruction). Axis II pole term: the only assembled bridge D_S<=L_S is obstructed at 2a=ln2. Axis III criterion completeness: Weil positivity quantifies over every support; a per-support certificate is one slice.

nodes.name: Off-diagonal correlations defeat componentwise Pollaczek bounds
nodes.statement: Tp=Fp'+2F'p, X[p]=|Tp|^2, H[p]=|Fp'|^2, X-H=int V p^2, V=2(F'^2-FF''). Pollaczek Q_j^*=P_j^{(9/4)}(t/2;pi/2) have H/X<=C/log(j+2), yet R_n=sum a_k Q_{n-2k}^*, a_k=(-1)^k(7/4)_k/k!, has H/X->1.

nodes.name: Polynomial de Bruijn / Polya-Schur theorem (Lean)
nodes.statement: For a real polynomial p with only real roots and t >= 0, heatOp t p = sum_k (-t)^k p^(2k)/k! has only real roots. Proof: Hermite-Poulain shift plus the limit (1 - (t/n) D^2)^n -> e^{-t D^2} with root continuity. Sorry-free, standard axioms only.

nodes.name: Polya Phi cosine transform evaluator
nodes.statement: Xi(t)=int Phi(u)cos(tu)du with the theta-derived kernel Phi locates gamma_1..gamma_5; basis for the autocorrelation A(tau) of Phi, moment ladder M_0..M_4 (M_0~7.675e-4, M_2=4.537e-6, M_4=9.62528e-8) and saddle-ratio studies.

nodes.name: Polymath/Raymond hybrid gives no gain
nodes.statement: Joining lemma B'_P: a hybrid's bound is the max over its bands, Lambda <= max(U_1..U_m, t0 + y0^2/2). Any Polymath band from existing rows gives 0.1758354, which is +0.030141 above route P; the best split has no Polymath band.

nodes.name: Two numerical detectors of ind_-(K_a)
nodes.statement: Rectangular argument-principle winding and Birman-Krein spectral shift return the same integer index; with several injected off-line conjugate pairs the winding equals the exact pole count. An injected off-line zero moves the Pick index of the reconstructed m-function from 0 to kappa.

nodes.name: Negative index ind_-(K_a)=0 on window grid; off-line controls give 1,2,3
nodes.statement: Pontryagin negative index of K_a tracked as an argument-principle winding for a in (0,5) is 0 on all windows; the absolute Birman-Krein spectral shift of the twin-ladder operator reproduces 0 without reference subtraction, and planted off-line pairs give index 1,2,3.

nodes.name: Porting the barrier gives parity with Lambda <= 0.2, not an improvement
nodes.statement: With S_barrier ported the far-tail bridge has one remaining conditionality (GUE, on the vanishing share sigma) and matches Platt-Trudgian Lambda <= 0.2. The finite-height figure L_pt ~ 0.121 is a conditional reading in a different regime, not an unconditional bound.

nodes.statement: T_{a,p}[R](z)=p(zR+a)/(z+aR) maps positive-real R to positive-real, with Re T=p[(|z|^2+a^2)Re R+a(1+|R|^2)Re z]/|z+aR|^2. With L_0=F'/F, p_j=L_{j-1}(a_j), nodes dense in [1,2]: all pivots positive implies L positive-real on Re z>0, hence RH.

nodes.statement: Dependency graph over 270 modules, 6 layers: Hilbert-Polya (self-adjoint extension), Weil positivity, de Branges/Hermite-Biehler, Beurling-Nyman each reduce to one positivity statement equivalent to RH; 13 surveyed strategies share it.

nodes.name: Conjecture 15.4: Re xi'/xi(sigma+it) > 0 for sigma > 1/2
nodes.statement: Pointwise domination of the prime-delay echo train (log p) p^{-m/2} e^{-iTm log p} by the gamma/kernel drift. Equivalent to RH (every paired Hadamard term u/(u^2 + (v -+ gamma)^2) is positive); numerical audit only confirms the triviality under verified height. Compare map rows G8, P8.

nodes.statement: Infinitesimal shift contractivity: the completed rightward drift of xi dominates the prime-delay echo train right of the line. Re xi'/xi(s) > 0 on Re s > 1/2 is RH-equivalent (Lagarias 1999). Obstruction map P8 / G8.

nodes.name: Conjecture 18.2 prime-delay domination: test stops at Re w=1/2
nodes.statement: Re xi'/xi(1/2+w)>0 computed from primes p^m<=1e4 plus archimedean drift: holds at 12 points with Re w>1/2 (min margin 0.022); the 16 points with Re w<=1/2 are inconclusive because the truncated echo train sum Lambda(n)n^{-s} diverges.

nodes.statement: Z_X(beta)=prod_{p<=X}(1-p^{-beta})^{-1}: midpoint minimizes log Z_X(sigma)+log Z_X(1-sigma); normalized energy difference tends to a Gaussian. Theta kurtosis in [2.79110285146369,2.79110286487817] vs pure quartic 2.18843961522647. At X=2,J=0,g=1e-4 fourth cumulant>2.9: not Lee-Yang.

nodes.name: Prime log-phase caustics and resonance heights
nodes.statement: theta_p(t)=t log p mod 2 pi. Coherent-prime count #{p: |theta_p|<eps} as a field in (sigma,t) with weight p^{-sigma}; two primes align at t=2 pi k/log(p_j/p_i). Phase cylinder: each prime is a straight ray (helix). Descriptive geometry.

nodes.statement: |sum_p cos(j log p + k t_0)| over (j,k), t_0 a zero ordinate (default gamma_1=14.134725), 200 primes; Bragg-like peaks at integer harmonics of 2 pi/log p; DC term equals the prime count.

nodes.name: Prime-square pole forces super-sqrt(N) runs of valid scales
nodes.statement: Unconditionally: liminf D_{23,15}(N)/N^{3/2}<=-11081.705, liminf D_{32,21}(N)/N^{3/2}<=-40805.171 (negative residue at s=3/2 plus Landau). Each late checkpoint stays negative over floor(sqrt(N) exp(0.8 sqrt(log N))) consecutive scales; starts may be sparse, so no eventual sign.

nodes.statement: After separating prime-square modes the j>=3 logarithmic remainder satisfies |R_3(t)|<=C_3(s_0), C_3(s)=[2^{-3s}+2^{1-3s}/(3s-1)]/[3(1-2^{-s})], uniformly in cutoff and height for every s_0>=1/2.

nodes.name: RH iff one nonnegative prime tent on (N,4N]
nodes.statement: RH iff 2 sum_{N<p<=2N}(p-N)log p + sum_{2N<p<=4N}(4N-p)log p <= 3N^2 eventually. The dilation F(4N)-3F(2N)+2F(N) cancels primes p<=N. On RH the prime-square bias dominates the zero wave: L_+V_theta <= -(0.155951-o(1))N^{3/2}.

nodes.name: Route E: primon-gas response functions peak at sigma=1, not 1/2
nodes.statement: With Z(sigma)=prod_p(1-p^{-sigma})^{-1} as a Bose partition function, susceptibilities peak at the condensation (Hagedorn) edge sigma=1; the strip is inaccessible to the thermodynamic reading.

nodes.name: Route A: primon reflection Gram about sigma=1/2 is not PSD
nodes.statement: G_ij=(p_i p_j)^{-1/2}exp(-c(log p_i+log p_j)^2) from Gaussian-windowed critical-line pairing of f_i=p_i^{-s}: indefinite from N=4. The Gaussian-damped off-line detector decays like e^{-t gamma^2}, reaching the noise floor at gamma~5.6/sqrt(t).

nodes.name: Reflection positivity of the primon gas
nodes.statement: The finite-N reflection Gram is indefinite at every N (lambda_min -> -inf like -p_N^{1/2 - nu}); infinite-N reflection positivity holds numerically but is equivalent to Weil positivity (Lagarias-Pick).

nodes.name: Route E: primon-gas response maxima sit at sigma = 1, not 1/2
nodes.statement: VarE(sigma) = sum_p (log p)^2 x/(1-x)^2, x = p^(-sigma), and Cv = sigma^2 VarE are strictly decreasing on sigma > 1 and diverge at 1. The Euler product does not define the gas inside the strip. Instance of the common wall: nothing passes from the region right of 1.

nodes.name: Boundary-extension constant C_PS = pi/sqrt(2)
nodes.statement: For the model cusp density |x|^{-1/2}: |m'(i eps)| about C_PS eps^{-3/2}, C_PS=lim eps^{3/2}|m'|=pi/sqrt(2)=2.221441. Finite-window correction: C_ren-C_PS about (4/3) eps^{3/2}; general cusp exponent gives coefficient C(alpha)=2/(alpha+1).

nodes.name: Theorem D: the 7/8 probe equals the aggregated theta-row form
nodes.statement: I_mod(Z) = Theta(Z) + O(Z^{17/96 + eps}): nothing unproved stands on the low side between the probe and the complete sextic theta coefficients. The P_a^{1/6} loss is exactly the Cauchy-Schwarz norm of the theta-row form; removing a power of it is the improved zero-free half-plane.

nodes.name: Linearity of the floor in the probe measure
nodes.statement: Kernel inequality, self cap and the Lemma H2 far-field inequality are linear in the probe measure, so mixtures of certified components need no new kernel certificate (lambda = min of components). Six certified lambda<2 two-point kernels give -2.28e-4.

nodes.name: Xi prolate-Weil bridge checkpoint: P0 invalidated
nodes.statement: PR 6 isolates an exact sufficient theorem and replays Connes-Consani-Moscovici finite matrices, with Fourier projection on N=C ceil(lambda^2) and Mellin projection on O((log lambda)^2); its proof item is recorded as P0_INVALIDATED. No signed Weil or sector floor transfers.

nodes.name: Proper powers: summable credits, logarithmic memory
nodes.statement: B(r)=sum_{p^k<=e^r,k>=2}(log p)p^{-k/2}=r/2+kappa+O(r^2e^{-0.59 sqrt r}), kappa=-gamma+sum_p log p/(sqrt p(p-1)); sum_p sum_{k>=2}|c_{p^k}|<inf. With H~_p=sum_{l<p}log l/sqrt l+(1/2)log p+kappa-b: R(X)-sum_{2<p<=X}c~_p converges.

nodes.name: Verified height binds the Lambda<=0.2 floor
nodes.statement: Interval-rigorous audit: verified zero height X about 3e12 binds; barrier slack (margin>=1.2) and AFE tail (margin about 1.047, X-independent) do not. Lambda<=t0+y0^2/2 improves inversely with log X and cannot reach 0.

nodes.name: Box-pulse leakage below 1/8 and divergent preimages
nodes.statement: For f_0=1_[0,1], g_0=C_0 f_0 (alpha=1): leakage |Q_1 g_0|^2<=0.124030166<1/8 by a rational three-feature witness. Regularized preimages a_eps have L^1 and L^2 norms tending to infinity while int a_eps -> 1/F(0). A single inverse-Blaschke toy shows no universal leakage gap.

nodes.statement: |Q_1 g_0|^2=lim_{eps->0}[<a_eps,Delta_1 a_eps>-|B_1 a_eps|^2] with a_eps=(A*A+eps)^{-1}A*f_0. Show the limit is zero. Leakage is an orthogonal Hardy model-space projection; genuine poles give Cauchy-Gram lower bounds. All derivative orders at one point are equivalent to the global kernel sign.

nodes.name: Pole-free subspace as the de Branges space H(E_a S)
nodes.statement: PW_a is the de Branges space H(E_a), E_a(z)=e^{-iaz}, with sinc reproducing kernel. With S(z)=z^2+1/4, the map g -> Qg, Q=-d^2/dx^2+1/4, is an isometry of PW_a onto H(E_a S); the pole-free constraint hhat(+-i/2)=0 is membership in that subspace.

nodes.name: QRH strip 1/8 <= Re rho <= 7/8 and Lambda <= 9/32 in Lean

nodes.name: Twin-ladder Weil norm square Q_TL
nodes.statement: Q_TL[h] = A_inf[h] - 2 sum_p sum_m (log p) p^{-m/2} Re C_h(m log p): the Weil explicit formula in log-prime delay coordinates. Under RH the zero side is a square; off-line zeros give negative-norm ghost states.

nodes.statement: p_{n+1}=t p_n-Cn^2p_{n-1} (C>1) keeps the theta profile, positive quadratic recurrence coefficients, real simple interlacing roots and log localization but has no conditioning reserve of order log n. Exact signed stationarity must distinguish the actual ladder.

nodes.statement: floorUlp(n) of the graded Gauss-Legendre moment quadrature shows 16 cluster peaks on n in [400,1200] with irregular spacing, flat inter-cluster troughs, no gap-height correlation; apparent height growth is a two-point artifact. Saturation node budget about 186. A numerical-precision effect, not arithmetic.

nodes.name: Exact quartic heat model with an off-line quartet
nodes.statement: P_u(z)=z^4+(12u-5)z^2+12u^2-10u+4 with u=-tau, z=-2i(s-1/2): an exact polynomial heat solution carrying an off-line quartet, used to calibrate channel and coupling diagnostics over -0.13<=tau<=0.

nodes.name: R2: true-flow collision time below the map upper bracket
nodes.statement: Claim t_c_flow(N) <= t_c_hi(N) (map upper bracket 1.2e-3 at N = 2000). Order-robust references (RK4, DP45, BS3, dense output) support it at N = 500..4000; the N-independent overshoot sign is mechanistic and empirical, and the discrete order-preservation lemma lifting per-step lag to collision-time ordering is open.

nodes.name: R5 tail monotonicity splits into a finite part and an irreducible tail
nodes.statement: Monotonicity of tau_c(N) on any bounded window is a finite computation not using GUE (certified window {50,100,200,500}); the tail N -> infinity part is equivalent to the GUE-universality conditional C_mb (imp-486).

nodes.name: RH as Eisenstein Satake points in the Ramanujan cube
nodes.statement: In the Hecke picture RH reduces to: every Eisenstein Satake point Kron(gamma_rho) = (cos(gamma_rho log p))_p lies in the Ramanujan cube, via Lemma 4.11(iii), which is only argued; Prop 4.15(ii) is unproved.

nodes.statement: With R_1 = 1, R_(n+1)(x) = n(1+x) R_n(x) + x^2 R_n'(x): the coefficient triangle of P_n is R_n read in reverse; boundary values (n-1)! and (2n-3)!!; R_n(1) = n^(n-1); generating function via the tree function T(z) = -W(-z). Verified n = 2..12.

nodes.name: 16 random Platt windows at 1.06e13 to 3.09e19

nodes.name: Two-point shear kernel is rank-2 antisymmetric
nodes.statement: Gshear_anti(u,v)=Phi(u)Phi(v)sinh(a(v-u))=p q^T-q p^T with p_i=Phi_i cosh(a u_i), q_i=Phi_i sinh(a u_i); i*Gshear_anti has spectrum {+mu,-mu,0,...}. It is a different matrix from the symmetric Hankel Gram Gsym and gives no bound on its off-diagonal terms.

nodes.name: Theorem RATE-MONO for the two-rate signed constant
nodes.statement: Lambda_2(x,r) is strictly decreasing in the rate ratio r on (1,inf) for every x=nu_1 d>0, from the coalescence cap (r->1+) to the single-rate floor e^{-2x} (r->inf).

nodes.name: Rayleigh quotients bound the top eigenvalue from the wrong side
nodes.statement: For self-adjoint A_S23, R(psi)<=lam_max for every psi, so finite test families give only lower envelopes. Putting lam_max strictly below 1 is the min-principle on I - A_S23 (coercivity over all psi) and needs effective diagonalisation. Kato-Temple thresholds stay at order 1e-3 for every admissible anchor.

nodes.name: Reciprocal total positivity: direct PF-infinity route excluded
nodes.statement: PF_inf kernel iff 1/g(s)=e^{as^2+bs} prod(1+delta_k s)e^{-delta_k s}, delta_k>0. A certified negative 5x5 Toeplitz minor rules out PF_inf for the actual kernel; the rotated reciprocal 1/X(is) is RH-equivalent, not a reduction. Map row G4.

nodes.name: Reentry band is a floating-point artifact of the surrogate
nodes.statement: Under contraction rate r in (0,1), positive floor EPS and ceil-quantised iteration count: for each fixed N there is EPS*(N) > 0 with band count B_N(EPS) = 0 for 0 < EPS < EPS*(N). Floor-slide identity d xArg/d log(FLOOR) = -1/ln(1/r). Band [10^27.08, 10^37.17] has no continuum residue.

nodes.name: Regular-representation matrix Dirichlet series with the bridge (Krein) square (RS-1)
nodes.statement: Device under test in lane c11-rs1-regular-rep-matrix-bridge (campaign round 11). Lane report of 2026-11-19, internal check by the lane itself: stage A stops; the bridge objects lie in the commutative group algebra and decompose over characters; E_a and T-NR matrix lifts keep every input. Not yet refereed independently; node status unchanged until the learn step. Object: M_q(s) = sum_n R(n) n^-s with R the regular representation of (Z/q)^*, entrywise non-negative coefficients, a matrix Euler product and a Gauss-sum functional equation; the bridge / Krein square of the square-root lane (g-spinor-square-root) is formed for the matrix symbol. The object holds Euler product, functional equation and periodicity together; Davenport-Heilbronn at q = 5 is a linear functional of M_5 that is not an eigen-direction. Closed neighbours: bridge rows Q25 (family sums, gain 0) and Q26 (single row, axis at the edge of the Euler factor). Stage A as for the other round-11 explore lanes (displayed inequality, marked steps, eleven-control table). No statement about zeros of zeta.

device.evidence: lane c11-rs1-regular-rep-matrix-bridge (round 11). CLOSED at stage A, for the displayed forms (K), (E), (Q), (H), by c12-repair-sources-statement-o-v3 (round 12) on two referee files: push/c11-rs1-regular-rep-matrix-bridge/REFEREE.md (independent; holds with six corrections) and push/c12-repair-sources-statement-o-v3/REFEREE2.md section 1 (E_a and T-NR lifts re-derived step by step). The bridge objects lie in the commutative group algebra and decompose over characters; the vector 1 is in the cone and is the chi_0 eigenvector, so every cone-quantified statement restricts to the scalar zeta statement (RH for forms K and E); the E_a lift keeps entry positivity at both levels, the Euler product, a functional equation of Gauss-sum type (squared root-number matrix, degree-two gamma factor) and periodicity; the T-NR lift keeps product-level positivity, the Euler product, the functional equation of M_q itself and periodicity. Not covered: statements mixing several bridge objects. The cell "a cone other than R_+^G" was run by lane c12-univ-pointwise-control-wcone (independent referee pass in its REFEREE.md): candidate (CW) on the cone K_F = {v >= 0, Fv >= 0} is closed (extreme rays at q = 5 with zeros off the line; the T-NR lift has every input); other F-adapted cones (non-polyhedral, or not containing v_+-) are not covered. Map rows Q28, Q29. Device type absent from the list before round 11 (no map row for matrix-valued or regular-representation objects). DH at q = 5 is a non-eigen linear functional of M_5. First controls: E_a, T-NR, EIS-w, window translate; bridge rows Q25, Q26 (family sums have gain 0; single rows have their axis at the edge of the Euler factor) are the closed neighbours

nodes.name: (Rep): asymptotic isometric representability of Weil classes iff RH
nodes.statement: lim_N c_N^{-1} P(L_N D_F)^2 = -W(F * F-check) for every real F is equivalent to RH; the tower uses Hodge index only to say the target form is definite. Along the heat flow (Rep_t) iff RH_t; all steps before (Rep) hold for the DH Weil form.

nodes.name: RES-T fixed-support Weil-positivity resolution law
nodes.statement: For Weil form W_T with test support T and an off-line quadruple at displacement delta, detectable height ceiling H_ceil(T,delta)=2 pi exp(E), E=delta^2 S(T delta)^4 T^3, S(x)=sinh(x/2)/(x/2). Fixed-T positivity follows from verified height only for T<T_X (about 3.88); doubly exponential in T.

nodes.name: Residue-averaged sign image of the seam phase ratio
nodes.statement: For a single seam window with Gram G and S = sum G_ml: <theta_C> = (p tr(G) - S)/((p-1) S) in (0,1), with tr(G)/S = (1 + eps_p)/(p-1), 0 < eps_p < (a D)_max^2/2, and <theta_C>(p-1)^2 = 1 + p eps_p. Tabulated for primes 3..3011.

nodes.name: Finite-N resolvent flux identity (complex Burgers with viscosity)
nodes.statement: Along the attractive Calogero-Moser / backward Dyson flow the Stieltjes transform m(z,s) satisfies m_s = 2 m m_z + m_zz exactly at finite N; the identity survives numerically to 0.99 of the pre-collision budget. Inviscid limit is complex Burgers; the collision is a fold with Holder-1/2 exponent.
nodes.underusedWhy: exact finite-N identity m_s = 2 m m_z + m_zz; used only for the Lambda bridge, never paired with the Cayley form S or the prime chain

nodes.name: Restricted reciprocal Mobius-delay lift (App H) and its conditioning barrier
nodes.statement: Degree-2 self-reciprocal proxy p(z) = 1 + cz + z^2 for the bridge ratio Theta_a. Bounded-real passes at a = 0.025 (Gram cond ~ 342, c = -0.0183); at a <= 0.015 the central-band Gram is near-singular (cond ~ 8.2e4 at a = 0.010, |Theta^lift| ~ 1.0031 at omega = 0.1).

nodes.name: Proven |alpha| < 1 pair correlation cannot reach the collision scale
nodes.statement: A statistic inside the proven Montgomery/Rudnick-Sarnak support is band-limited with resolution one mean spacing; the min-gap scale is s_min ~ M^(-1/3) (Ben Arous-Bourgade), below it by M^(1/3): 97x at N ~ 9.22e5, 1486x at N ~ 3.28e9. C_C is carried by |alpha| >= 1.
