nodes.name: Block-spin prime freezing: zeros are RG fixed points
nodes.statement: Octave freezing multiplies by a zero-free factor, so nontrivial zeros are exact RG fixed points; the self-dual AFE frame has an archimedean fixed point and a zero-mean tangential prime force and destroys close-pair correlations.

nodes.name: RH and simple zeros iff G = H_t + i H_t' has no zero on the closed slab
nodes.statement: RH iff G(t,x) := H_t(x) + i H_t'(x) != 0 on (0, 1/2] x R (vortex Theorem A, internal); G(0,x) = 0 exactly at real multiple zeros of H_0, so RH and SZC iff G != 0 on [0, 1/2] x R. Equivalently D_t(x) = H'^2 - H H'' > 0.

nodes.name: Bathtub joint floor for band-limited forms
nodes.statement: For psi in PW_a with unit norm, |psi|^2 <= a/pi pointwise and has unit mass, so int sigma_2^- |psi|^2 <= (a/pi) int over the deepest measure-(pi/a) sub-level set = 3065.435 at 2a = ln 3; hence c_sharp >= -3065.435. Realisable fraction about 44-51% (R = 1343.8 to ~1573).

nodes.name: Certified spherical-Bessel z^-4 tail constant for the Krein tail integral
nodes.statement: For the ground combination g(t) = v0 . Phih(t) = a^7 Sum_k d_k j_k(a t) with annihilated t^-1, t^-2, t^-3 coefficients, an interval-certified z^-4 remainder constant C = 45504.154 bounds the Rayleigh tail; Gegenbauer C_n^{13/2}-Legendre overlaps c_jk computed in exact rationals (band k <= j+6, parity j+k even).

nodes.name: Negativity set of sigma_2 is one confined well; far field positive
nodes.statement: sigma_2 < 0 only on W = [0, 3.306] u [6.945, 10.532] and its mirror (depth -4336 at t = 9.35); rigorous positivity for t >= 27 (crossing t* = 26.1023, margin 0.0616) and guarded margin +8.114 on [10.532, 27].

nodes.name: Zero crossing of lambda_min(T_a[sigma_2]) drifts down to ln 3
nodes.statement: Crossing 2a*(N): 1.13052, 1.12543, 1.12025, 1.11046, 1.10033 for N = 20, 28, 36, 44, 52 (ln 3 = 1.098612), margin +0.032 -> +0.0017 with non-shrinking steps. Just above ln 3 a p = 2 resonance eigenvalue falls from +0.47 to below -6 within 0.005 in 2a.

nodes.name: Krein concentration constant c_sharp at 2a = ln 3
nodes.statement: c_sharp = lambda_min(P_a M_{sigma_2} P_a) at 2a = ln 3: coupled N,T Rayleigh-Ritz extrapolation gives ~0.582 (range [0.5817, 0.5842]); fixed-T column 0.5811 -> 0.5786 for N = 84..164; a separate nested-basis ladder suggests ~0.45. All are upper brackets; no positive lower bound is certified.

nodes.name: Certified positive lower bound on c_sharp at ln 3
nodes.statement: Needed: P_a M_{sigma_2} P_a >= c I with c > 0 at 2a = ln 3. Rigorous floors so far are negative: bathtub -3065.435, reproducing-kernel -3200.029, well depth -4336.198. Lehmann-Maehly and de Branges coercivity both reduce to one PW_a concentration inequality against the confined negative well.

nodes.name: Fejer-Riesz square with margin exists iff c <= c_sharp
nodes.statement: (t^2+1/4)^2 = |(t - i/2)^2|^2 is a free Hermitian square reducing sigma_2-coercivity to w_1-coercivity on h = (-D^2 + 1/4) g modulo boundary terms; w_1(0) = -6.352. A truncated (Mercer) square with margin c exists iff c <= c_sharp: restatement, not a bound.

nodes.name: Standard concentration inequalities give no positive c_sharp
nodes.statement: Beurling-Selberg minorants (circular: a type-2a minorant restates truncated-Toeplitz positivity), flat prolate/Slepian eigenvalues, Donoho-Stark, Turan/Amrein-Berthier, Nazarov, weighted-PSWF decay (signed split caps at <= 0), Temple/Kato-Temple and Lehmann-Maehly (need a-priori lambda_2 bound) all fail to give c > 0 at 2a = ln 3.

nodes.name: Degree-to-v0 overlap inversion blocks the annihilating-trial certificate
nodes.statement: Exact integer degree-level annihilating trials (e.g. (33,55,27,5)) cannot be mapped back to the committed ground vector v0 through d = C^T v0 with interval enclosure; the remainder envelope is complete, the inversion step remains open.

nodes.name: Reproducing-kernel floor is linear in the band half-width
nodes.statement: floor(a) = -(a/pi) int sigma_2^-(t) dt measured across 2a <= 0.96: the scalar floor scales linearly in a because the confined well is band-independent; the scalar two-budget coupling is exhausted.

nodes.name: Pole-free Weil symbol sigma_2 and residual w_1
nodes.statement: sigma_2(t) = (t^2 + 1/4)^2 w_1(t), w_1(t) = 2 theta'(t) - sqrt2 ln2 cos(t ln 2) (archimedean phase derivative minus the p = 2 term). Pole-free Weil positivity on support 2a is T_a[sigma_2] = P_a M_{sigma_2} P_a >= 0 on PW_a.

nodes.name: Toeplitz/Weil support ladder past ln 3 (obstruction map P19)
nodes.statement: All-support positivity at damping theta is equivalent to the half-plane 1/2 + theta; finite-support rungs at theta = 0 have model margins of order 1e-30900. Finite-support Weil positivity near ln 3 uses only p = 2 (one in-band prime harmonic) and restates verified-height information.

nodes.name: Bare residual w_1 negative on [0, 3.305) and at t = ln 3
nodes.statement: w_1 is negative on the whole leading interval [0, 3.30501) and at t = ln 3; negative-to-positive mass ratio over the resolution window grows past the verified reach. No pointwise or symbol-level argument can give positivity near ln 3.

nodes.name: Well capture versus far-field cost for band-limited minimisers
nodes.statement: For the confinement family with taper g(xi) = (1 - (xi/a)^2)^2 exp(-(R xi)^2/2), the minimum of int sigma_2 |psi|^2 is 6.56 -> 7.22 tail-converged at R* ~ 3.36, about 12x the Ritz floor; far-field bias relBias(R) = 3(1/a - a R^2)(I2/I1) changes sign at R = 1/a.

nodes.name: Positive/negative symbol split loses the band-limited cancellation
nodes.statement: Bound Q(g) >= lambda_min(T_a[sigma^+]) - lambda_max(T_a[sigma^-]) crosses zero at 2a = 0.6026 < ln 2 while true lambda_min there is 1.59 to 6.42. A well-concentrated and far-field-depleted |ghat|^2 cannot be one PW_a element; only the correlation-preserving LP/Krein certificate (verified to 2a <= 0.96) keeps the cancellation.

nodes.name: Riesz series criterion
nodes.statement: RH is equivalent to sum_k (-1)^{k+1} x^k/((k-1)! zeta(2k)) = O(x^{1/4 + eps}).

nodes.name: Theorem RIG: a measure with small sawtooth discrepancy carries only zeta's zeros
nodes.statement: For a locally finite measure b >= 0 on [1, infinity) with O(Y^eps) integer-sawtooth discrepancy at every real Y, the Dirichlet transform is B* = s[...]/zeta: its singularities are zeta's zeros. Needs one measure on [1, infinity); finite-x dual points are unrelated Dirichlet polynomials.

nodes.name: Bettin-Conrey reciprocity residual does not decay along the Gauss map
nodes.statement: w_sym(a,q) = (V(a,q)+V(q,a))/q depends only on the reduced rational. After one reciprocation the residual is another cotangent sum of the same shape; along Gauss-map orbits its RMS stays ~0.026. Gauss-Kuzmin averaging isolates kappa_smooth < 1e-2 only as x -> 0.

nodes.name: Boundary cotangent sum V(1,b)
nodes.statement: V(1,b) = c_0(1/b) = Sum_{m=1}^{b-1} (m/b) cot(pi m/b) has sub-leading coefficient -pi/36 (Euler-Maclaurin with singular endpoint, digamma cross-check); boundary leg -V(1,b)/(phi(b) b) -> 0.

nodes.name: Bulk profile of the Vasyunin coefficient
nodes.statement: I(xb, b) = b f(x) + o(b), f(x) = C(1+x) + (1/2)(1-x) log x - (pi/2) w(x), w(x) = lim (V(xb,b) + V(b,xb))/b the cotangent-sum limit; curvature of f equals that of w; crossover fraction x*(eps) is b-independent to 3-4 digits.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz reduction of the absolute cotangent first moment to M2w
nodes.statement: c_1 <= sqrt(M2w): the absolute first moment over the inverse line is bounded by the a-weighted mean square; measured sqrt(M2w) ~ 0.415 < kappa_arith = 0.5705. Certification needs the Bettin-Conrey second moment transferred to the inverse line a -> b^{-1} mod a.

nodes.name: Route M conditioning-ceiling band
nodes.statement: Ordered ceiling band for the Gram conditioning: trace 2.594e7 < Frobenius-rigorous 3.748e7 < concave-tail 3.838e7 < concave-quad 4.088e7 < measured 4.109e7; exact ladder extended to N = 24000 widens the quad-to-measured margin to 0.518%.

nodes.name: Signed-to-absolute cotangent cancellation ratio 0.540
nodes.statement: |S(b)|/A(b), A(b) = Sum |c_0(h_a/a)| with h_a = b^{-1} mod a, settles in a 0.4% band around 0.5397 for 4001 <= b <= 24001; absolute downside coefficient A(b)/(phi(b) b) plateaus (measured c_1 ~ 0.29 < kappa_arith).

nodes.name: Varying-modulus Vasyunin half converges to -1/(4 pi)
nodes.statement: Sum_{a=2,(a,b)=1}^{b-1} V(b,a)/(phi(b) b) converges to -0.07958, matching -1/(4 pi) = -0.0795775 to about 5 digits past b ~ 12870; implies kappa_cot = +1/8. V(b,a) = V(b mod a, a); creep ~ C/b.

nodes.name: Sign of the signed cotangent half S(b) < 0
nodes.statement: S(b) = Sum_{a=2,(a,b)=1}^{b-1} V(b,a) is measured negative but unproved. Kernel is odd and mean-zero: c_0(h/a) = -c_0((a-h)/a). Exact residue-resonance form S(b) = Sum_{r>=1} Sum_{a|(b-r), r<a<b} c_0(r/a); small-r family dominance refuted (each family O(d(b-r) b log b)).

nodes.name: Sub-leading constant cQ of Q(b) is not determinable from the ladder
nodes.statement: sqrt(b) and log^2 b sub-leading models stay collinear on the exact Q(b) ladder to b = 16000 (checked to 1e5); three decorrelation designs fail; joint fits give s0 = 1.7871, cQ = -2.008 versus constant-model cQ ~ -13.4.

nodes.name: Uniform remainder for the coprime log sum L0(b)
nodes.statement: For L0(b) = Sum_{1<=a<b,(a,b)=1} log a: |E0(b)| <= (1/2) log b + (1/2) log 2pi + 11/8 + (1/6) sigma(b)/b for all b >= 2, with exact decomposition E0(b) = (1/2) Lambda(b) - (1/2)(Moebius-moment terms); no 2^omega(b) prefactor.

nodes.name: Per-divisor identity for the weighted coprime sum remainder E1(b)
nodes.statement: E1(b) = L1(b) - phi(b) b((1/2) log b - 1/4), L1 = Sum_{(a,b)=1} a log a, satisfies E1(b) = Sum_{d|b} mu(d) C_d exactly (Glaisher-Kinkelin collapse), with leader mu(b) b/4 plus inward correction Delta(b) = mu(b) b Sum_{e|b,e>1} mu(e) h(e).

nodes.name: w_lin from the Estermann double pole
nodes.statement: The Laurent block {A, B, C0} of the Estermann function at its s = 1 double pole reproduces the linear part of w(x): log(x)/pi from the double-pole residue and 2C/pi from the finite part, with kernel gamma factor N(s) = (2 pi)^{-s} Gamma(s).

nodes.name: Route M first moment is a mean-value statement (obstruction map P15)
nodes.statement: The first-moment programme gives F(b) >= b phi(b)/2 - 1, Int(N) >= (36K^2/pi^2) log N - O(1), K = 0.6954960511, lam_max(G_N) <= 18: mean-value statements only, nothing about lam_min, d_N or zeros; a Davenport-Heilbronn analogue exists.

nodes.name: Fixed-a asymptotic of I(a,b)
nodes.statement: For fixed a, I(a,b) = (a/2) log b + d_a + o(1) with d_a = (a/2)(2C + 1 - log a); hence I(a,b)/a = (1/2) log(b/a) + C + 1/2 + o(1) and the fixed-a moment Sum_a kappa_a^2/a^2 diverges (each term 1/4).

nodes.name: Friable Mertens sup bound sup_t |M_k(t)| = o(p_k) is false
nodes.statement: For M_k the Moebius partial sum over p_k-friable squarefree integers with dilation recursion M_k = (I - D_{p_k}) M_{k-1}: sup_t |M_k(t)| ~ 1.71^k, sup/p_k crosses 1 near k = 13. Any o(1) tail must come from signed t-integration, not a sup majorant.

nodes.name: Gap-law residual changes sign repeatedly along the prime ladder
nodes.statement: residual(omega) = gap(omega) - e^{-gamma} B_inf/log p_omega at dps 35-40 has eight sign changes on the ladder to p ~ 4.93e8; local decay exponent oscillates with a widening envelope (average ~10.2-10.6); magnitude correlates with the Mertens error delta at common heights.

nodes.name: Inverse-line second moment M2w = DIAG + OFFDIAG (Kloosterman-type)
nodes.statement: Character detection writes the inverse-line cotangent second moment exactly as M2w * Sum_a a = DIAG + OFFDIAG, DIAG = Sum_a phi(a) E_h[(c_0/a)^2]; OFFDIAG/DIAG stays about 0.86 (co-leading) to b = 1201; factorisation M2w = Rw * Mbar; oversampling OVR(b) -> ~1.25.

nodes.name: Route M arithmetic first-moment coefficient kappa_arith
nodes.statement: F_arith(b) = kappa_arith phi(b) b + E1-type remainder with kappa_arith = (3/2)C - 3/8 = 0.5704960511, C = (log 2pi - gamma)/2; arithmetic leaf of the first moment F(b) = Sum_{(a,b)=1} I(a,b) of the Vasyunin/Nyman-Beurling Gram coefficients.

nodes.name: Cusp coefficient kappa_smooth of the Bettin-Conrey period function
nodes.statement: kappa_smooth = O(x^2) Taylor coefficient of psi at the cusp = (pi/2)[P2 - L2], P2 a zeta(2) Eisenstein-period part, L2 a gamma_1 double-pole part; reflection weight W_refl is not computed. Weight-2 period polynomial has degree 0 and cannot carry z^2.

nodes.name: Route M full first-moment constant kappa -> 0.69550
nodes.statement: kappa(b) = F(b)/(phi(b) b) re-measured on primes b=101..8009 declines smoothly to 0.69550, window std 6e-5, consistent with (3/2)C - 1/4 = 0.695496, i.e. kappa_cot = 1/8. Per-part positivity fails at b=30; only the sum is robustly positive.

nodes.name: MCM bracket limit B_inf = ln A + gamma/12
nodes.statement: The Route M MCM bracket limit is B_inf = ln(Glaisher A) + gamma/12 = 0.2968557824, from lim(log p_omega - Sum_{p<=p_omega} log p/(p-1)) = gamma; gap law gap(omega) ~ e^{-gamma} B_inf / log p_omega. Verified by sieve to 5e7.

nodes.name: Multiplicative complete monotonicity (MCM) fails at omega = 11
nodes.statement: Hypothesis: every iterated multiplicative difference of h = g/m over a finite prime set is non-negative. Holds for omega <= 10 (primorial margins 1.00e-2 .. 4.78e-4), first fails at the 11-primorial (-9.62e-4). Decrement law dS = -(Pi_omega/p_{omega+1})(A_omega + c log p_{omega+1}).

nodes.name: Liouville/Moebius parity sign law of the first-moment residual
nodes.statement: r(b) = F_arith(b)/(phi(b) b) - kappa_arith is the equidistribution discrepancy of psi over coprime residues; Moebius inversion gives sign r(b) = (-1)^omega(b) at leading order (von Mangoldt coefficient 1/4); at primorials P5..P8 a subleading Moebius term takes over.

nodes.name: Mertens cap Qlog(b) <= e^{-gamma} is false
nodes.statement: Qlog(b) = prod_{p|b}(1-1/p) Sum_{p|b} log p/(p-1)-type term is unbounded: b = 5*7*11*13*17*19 gives |Qlog| = 0.780 > 0.5615; add-a-prime identity F(P u {p}) - F(P) = (prod_P/p)(log p - S(P)); over primes in (y,x] the value grows like log y.

nodes.name: b/4 ceiling |E1(b)| <= b/4 is false for general squarefree b
nodes.statement: |E1(b)| <= b/4 holds on omega(b) <= 3 (proved) and 0 violations for b <= 20000, but fails: explicit squarefree windows of primes from P0 = 379 and P0 = 101 give T(b) < -1/4 (exact segmented sieve). Does not affect kappa_arith.

nodes.name: First-moment residual magnitude governed by smallest prime factor
nodes.statement: Geometric mean |r(b)| rises about 3x from P^-(b) = 2 (1.35e-5) to the near-prime plateau; two-descriptor model log|r| ~ a0 + a_w omega + a_P log P^-(b) has in-sample R^2 0.850 and holds out of sample.

nodes.name: Arithmetic cotangent resonances at x = 1/6 and 1/5
nodes.statement: The signed deviation (I - I_lin)/I has adjacent crests at x = 1/6 and 1/5; the 1% crossing of the 1/6 crest is an alignment band set by b mod 6, not a single b.

nodes.name: Interior second moment Q = Qhat + Qcross + Qrr
nodes.statement: With Ihat = (a/2) log(b/a) + a(C+1/2) and r = I - Ihat, Q(b) splits in the 1/a^2-weighted l^2 product; leading slope s0 = lim Q(b)/b ~ 1.76-1.79; sub-leading term is log^2 b with a coefficient that is an arithmetic function of b (Moebius collapse).

nodes.name: Sign law T(b) < 0 for squarefree b
nodes.statement: T(b) = Sum_{e|b,e>=2} mu(e) J(e-1) (J the Binet remainder) satisfies T(b) = -J(p1-1) + Sum_{e|m,e>1} mu(e) D_{p1}(e). Proved negative for omega <= 4; omega = 5 reduced to two explicit inequalities with tail threshold Q0 = 7; weighted level-domination fails for large omega.

nodes.name: Small-inverse frequency is a divisor sum
nodes.statement: #{a < b, (a,b)=1 : b^{-1} mod a <= H} <= Sum_{h<=H} d(bh - 1): the count of moduli with small inverse needs no Kloosterman input. Termwise bound |c_0(h/a)| <= K (a/h) log 2a fails in the bulk h ~ a/2.

nodes.name: Vasyunin two-variable coefficient I(a,b)
nodes.statement: I(a,b) = C(a+b) + (1/2)(a-b) log(b/a) - (pi/2)(V(a,b)+V(b,a)), V(a,q) = Sum_{m=1}^{q-1} frac(ma/q) cot(pi m/q), C = (log 2pi - gamma)/2. Entries of the Nyman-Beurling/Baez-Duarte Gram form; Q(b) = Sum_{(a,b)=1} I(a,b)^2/a^2 is the interior second moment.

nodes.name: Robin margin along colossally abundant numbers is Mertens-governed
nodes.statement: e^gamma - sigma(N)/(N log log N) along 300 colossally abundant N: growth rate set by Mertens product error; carries no de Bruijn-Newman content.

nodes.name: Rouche comparison of zeta with a functional-equation-symmetrised Euler stage
nodes.statement: Stage zeta_X(s) = P_X(s) + chi(s) conj(P_X(1 - conj s)), P_X an Euler stage over the primes up to X and chi the factor of the functional equation (Gonek 2012 type; recalled, source not opened). The stage satisfies the functional equation by construction, and its zero measure on the line is the phase comb of phi(t) = -2 vartheta(t) - 2 arg P_X(1/2 + it). Proposed device: Rouche comparison of zeta with zeta_X on the boundary of a window through the approximate functional equation, so that the zero count of zeta in the window equals that of the stage. Uses all primes up to X jointly and the functional equation in the same step. Known so far: the k = 0 term of the comb is the explicit-formula density with primes up to X, and its positivity on a window is the sup bound of the truncated prime sum against (1/2) log(t/2 pi), which holds for X of order log^2 t only (round 3, lesson 2); anything further must come from the k != 0 terms or from the comparison. Not established: any Rouche margin. To be checked: the unimodular twist has the same stage theorem and no approximate functional equation; rows G10, Q10 (finite Euler stages without the functional equation are closed); Hamburger uniqueness past the Riemann-Siegel length. Closed by lane c4-fe-stage-rouche-crossing (refereed once): the stage has all zeros on the line for any non-vanishing P_X; the Rouche inequality on a box is implied only by zero-freeness of a slightly larger region.

nodes.statement: F_N=A-sum_{p<=p_N}log p/(p^s-1), nodes nu in {0.05..1.5}: lambda_min from -142.669 (N=0) to -4213.156 (N=1229), strictly monotone; -lambda_min scales like p_N^{1/2-nu_min} (R^2>=0.996). Finite Euler truncations fail reflection positivity at every N.

nodes.statement: Deterministic discrepancy at the strip y_N = sqrt(2 pi/N): D(N) = (pi C_Selberg/sqrt(2 pi)) log gamma_N / sqrt(N). Composed with the Holder-1/2 fold: |t_c(m_N) - t_c(m_inf)| <= C_W sqrt(D(N)), so r(N) = C' sqrt(log gamma_N) N^(-1/4). Consumable modulo the anchor t_c(m_inf).

nodes.name: Baker bounds for linear forms in log p
nodes.statement: Coefficient-blind: the bound concerns the frequencies log n and holds for DH, every sign twist, THIN, U, WT. For integers it is weaker than abs(log m - log n) >= 1/max(m,n) (Montgomery-Vaughan input, a mean value: P27, P29). Its non-trivial content is a polylogarithmic gap for S-units with fixed S (measured exponent 2.9 to 3.4 for 4 primes), giving window-uniform mean squares of a fixed Euler stage. The constant that Baker-Matveev proves is doubly exponential in the stage length; the measured gaps follow the pigeonhole exponent k - 1, so this is a property of the provable constant, not of the frequencies. No finite stage carries the functional equation (G10, Q10).

nodes.name: Gram positivity of truncated minimal-parabolic SL_3 Eisenstein series (rank-2 Langlands inner product; one function M at z_1, z_2, z_1 + z_2) read off the zero set of M(u) = xi(u)/xi(u+1), as a device
nodes.statement: Relative to the recalled rank-2 inner product formula (checked by the lane for M = 1; source not opened, and the range of T not checked against a source), the inequality (I2) adds one condition to rank one (row D9): a zero a of M with 0 < Re a < 1/2 forces a zero at 1 - a (Lemma R). For zeta this is the functional equation (M(1 - rho) = xi(rho)/xi(2 - rho) = 0). Lemma R gives no condition on zeros with Re a > 1/2. A second necessary condition found by the referee (E1; MEASURED, its reading ARGUED): an odd number of real inserted zeros other than a single zero at 1 fails, read as the sign M(0) = -1 together with the pole at 1. Neither condition touches non-real zeros right of 1/2. Passing at every tested T >= 0 (MEASURED: about 4,700 Gram matrices of order 1 to 5 and 5,600 descent evaluations by the lane, mpmath 30 to 50 digits; rerun on different cases by the referee; no negative value): BLS-sym (zero set closed under a -> 1 - conj a; this is zeta times a real symmetric polynomial and has f(z) = f(1 - z), Lemma S; ZQ in polynomial form is a case; T-NR with c > 2 is the infinite case, ARGUED, not run) and BLS-right restricted to non-real zeros in conjugate pairs or real zeros of even total multiplicity. Closure of (I2) under these insertions is NOT proved (lane `c17-rank2-gram-symmetric-blaschke-closure`). At a hypothetical off-line pair 1/2 +- eta + i g the form at the one point where every coefficient is known is an explicit function of M on the real segment (0, 1), positive (about 4.2 eta^2 at t_2 = 0), independent of g: the inequality holds whether or not the pair exists. Exact normalisation does not separate: zeta's form is positive on the closed chamber T >= 0 with smallest normalised Gram eigenvalue 1e-10 to 1e-12 at T = 0, the low-height BLS-sym forms have margin 1e-3; the sign pattern below the chamber is not monotone in T (E3). State of the cell: tried, not closed; the form "Gram positivity read off the zero set" is closed as MEASURED only. Not covered: the two-variable affine kernel of row D9; a read of the archimedean factor; T-NR as an infinite product and NR-q (not run). Revision, campaign round 17 (`c17-rank2-gram-symmetric-blaschke-closure`, one referee; partial result). Source of the inner product formula: Miller, math/0006058, Theorem 6.1 and (7.6); the range of the truncation parameter is not stated there, so (I2) for zeta at T = 0 is MEASURED. Lemma M (PROVED; the rank-2 form of the Maass-Selberg boundary-term fact, new to the campaign record only): d K_T/d tau_i is a rank-one Maass-Selberg Gram kernel, and positivity on the chamber reduces to positivity of the apex kernel K_0 at T = 0 under rank-one positivity for t >= 0 (classical for zeta; imported from row D9 Theorem C for conjugate pairs; MEASURED for distinct real pairs, referee E2). Theorem T (PROVED by exact rational computation; a statement about a rational model, degree 2 and degree 4 at 14 exact parameter values): negative index = number of left zeros without reflected partner. Registered search, symmetric insertions of order 2 to 20: 1,397,025 + 5,208 certified positive Gram matrices, 0 failures, 47% of the registered plan; closure for zeta neither proved nor refuted. Inertia pattern (MEASURED, 16 configurations): at most kappa negative squares observed, equal to kappa in 318 of 320 matrices, kappa = reflection defect of the left zeros plus the real-zero parity defect (referee E3: 'exactly' is not supported), for a base M with the pole at 1. **ZQ in the rational form passes** (MEASURED: 3,360 of 3,360 certified positive matrices, six instances, orders 1 to 64; M_ZQ is analytic in Re u > 0 apart from the pole at 1, the poles of the multiplier being cancelled by zeros of zeta); the entry 'ZQ (rational form) fails at S3/S4, ARGUED' of the round-16 lane's control table is wrong. **DH-base note** (referee, MEASURED, 36 certified matrices, order at most 24): with the pole-free DH base the form shows 0 negative squares with an unpaired left pair and with a single real zero, where the zeta base shows 2 and 1; the form detects neither reflection nor parity defects without the pole at 1, so the lane's test of DH at points near its own off-line zero cannot fail by the identified mechanism and is not evidence. Backward heat: passes at t = -1 (low height, non-rigorous quadrature, possibly vacuous: no off-line zero located in the tested range; base M (u-1)/(u+1), pole removed; referee E1), fails at t = -5, -10 through zeros with real part above 1 (MEASURED). Reading: the form is rank-one Maass-Selberg plus one apex kernel at T = 0, which reads the reflection a -> 1 - a of left zeros and needs the pole at 1 in the base; it does not read the critical line. Method note: a symmetric zero set built from floating-point 0.5 - eta and 0.5 + eta is symmetric to 1e-17 only and produces certified negative squares at order 40; the set must be built exactly. State of the cell U6 (g): tried, not closed (inertia law for zeta open; lane `c18-d10-inertia-law-theorem-t-lemma-d`). Addendum, campaign round 18 (`c18-d10-inertia-law-theorem-t-lemma-d`, one referee; partial result; the row is not closed). M = M_0 Xi(u)/Xi(u+1) with M_0 = (u+1)/(u-1): zeta's apex kernel is a limit of rational-model kernels of symmetric zero sets (Lemmas L1, L2; RH not used). Theorem Q (computer-assisted, exact; reproduced by the referee at 3 new parameter points and the factorisation at 6 off-grid points): in the rational model with the pole base a symmetric quartet 1/2 +- eta +- i g gives a positive semidefinite apex kernel of rank 6 for all 0 < eta < 1/2, g > 0, so a symmetric off-line quartet passes (also on the zeta base, mpmath, not certified). Theorem H with Corollary H1: 6N is the antisymmetrised Bezoutian product, so a base without the pole passes for every insertion in Re a >= 0 at every degree (a pole-free base does not detect BLS-left). Proposition L3: X(d) for all even d implies positivity of zeta's apex kernel at T = 0; only this direction is proved (referee E-3). X(d) is proved for d = 2, 4, exact at 17 configurations for d = 6 to 12, open in general (round-19 lane `c19-d10-xd-determinant-pole-term-lemma-q`: reported, addendum at the end of this cell). Zeta base: 600 of 600 symmetric insertions positive; unpaired insertions never above the predicted index (153 / 186 / 195 of 200 equal at orders 64 / 96 / 128). **The parity clause of the round-17 inertia law, restated (referee E-1).** For an odd number of inserted real zeros the rational model of M_0 Theta, Theta the Blaschke product of the round-17 lane, is b = u (u - 1) g with g = prod (u + a_j); the lane's b = (u - 1) g is the model of M_0 (-Theta), a different function. With b = u (u - 1) g the model gives, exactly, 1 negative square for a real zero right of 1/2 (inertia (2, 1) at a = 3/4, 11/20, 9/10) and 2 for a real zero left of 1/2 ((1, 2) at a = 1/4), with or without a quartet ((16, 1) and (15, 2) with the quartet (1/4, 2)): the round-17 measured law, parity clause included, in the cases tested (instances, not a theorem in a). The lane's statements that the parity clause 'does not hold in the model' and 'should be restricted to the zeta-base measurement', the rows of its table 3.5 for a single real zero (8 of 75 configurations) and its control row E1 are computations for -Theta and are withdrawn; every even-degree statement is unaffected. DH and backward heat in the model: ARGUED (finite truncations only; E-4). Reading: a kernel with base (u+1)/(u-1) reads the pole and the reflection symmetry of the zero set; symmetric off-line quartets pass, so the row cannot score whatever X(d) gives. Second referee of the round-18 lane (`c19-referee-r18-independent-sources/REFEREE2-c18-d10-inertia-law-theorem-t-lemma-d.md`; holds with corrections): Theorem Q is computer-assisted; its conclusion is confirmed by a second implementation at 29 fresh interior points and the factorisation at 12 fresh points; the grid computation itself was not repeated. Odd number of real zeros, confirmed exactly: b = (u - 1) g is the model of M_0 times (-Theta) for odd degree and b = u (u - 1) g that of M_0 Theta; one real zero a with b = (u - 1)(u + a): (1, 0) at a = 1/4, (0, 1) at a = 3/4; with b = u (u - 1)(u + a): (1, 2) at a = 1/4, (2, 1) at a = 3/4, 11/20, 9/10. Addendum, campaign round 19 (`c19-d10-xd-determinant-pole-term-lemma-q`, one referee: the partial result holds; five wording corrections W-1 to W-5; the row is not closed). X(d) is not proved for general d. PROVED (re-derived by the referee by hand and exactly with separate code): (i) the term X of the round-18 Theorem H vanishes identically, so 2N = A[L(x_1, y_1) L(x_2, y_2) b(x_12) b(y_12)]: N is one half of Q = L (x) L (tensor square of the Bezoutian of b for u -> -u) on a subspace J^- of the jet space, and the sign-free 36-term kernel N^+ is one half of Q on a subspace J^+ that is Q-orthogonal to J^-; (ii) with the pole L has inertia (d, 1) and Q has inertia (d^2 + 1, 2d): the pole enters N as a rank-2d update, and neg(N) + neg(N^+) + z <= 2d with z the radical dimension; (iii) for simple zeros with no partner pair neg(N) is the negative index of the Gram matrix of N on the 2d + 1 crossing points (1, 1), (1, -a_j), (-a_j, 1) on the two pole lines (a reduction to an explicit matrix; that the matrix has as many negative squares as unpaired left zeros is MEASURED, W-2, W-3); (iv) at symmetric sets these 2d points are null vectors of N (the direction re-derived by the referee, from g(-1 - u) = g(u)); the lane states it as 'exactly when 1 - a_j is a zero'; (v) for symmetric simple sets z >= d, so X(d) follows from NL(d): 'N^+ has at least d negative squares', and it suffices to find them for the three-term one-variable kernel on the pole line (the three-term formula is for N^+ from the 36-term sum; j^+ itself has five surviving terms there, W-1); (vi) on the pole line N + N^+ has at most one positive square. Exact instances: X(d) and NL(d) at 220 symmetric configurations of the lane, d = 6 to 16 (positive semidefinite of rank d(d-1)/2, no counterexample; the d = 16 runs come from one machine and one code path), and at 4 further configurations of the referee (two confluent); non-symmetric controls: negative index equal to the number of left zeros with multiplicity deficit in 60 of 60 (lane), and as predicted at the referee's 10 control configurations; an even-degree law; pole removed: positive in 60 of 60 (for base +1 Q is positive semidefinite, not definite, W-5). nodes.name: Sum-product / multiplicative amplification
nodes.statement: The additive-against-multiplicative pairing for zeta is Vinogradov's method (power saving N^{-c eps^2} at N = t^eps); it gives the Vinogradov-Korobov region and no fixed strip, because a size bound converts to a region of width 1/log(size). A bilinear form sum a_m b_n (mn)^{it} over a rectangle has rank one (PROVED identity: no bilinear gain); for Vaughan-type forms with the cut mn <= x the same conclusion is ARGUED, not proved. The dual pairing gives Hurwitz/Estermann series (mean values over characters). Fails for DH at the 3-4-1 step and for sign twists and THIN at the interval-sum step; THIN passes any estimate with relative slack above x^{b-1}.
nodes.mapStatus: CLASSICAL / ARGUED (rectangle identity PROVED)
nodes.defeatedBy: none passes; the conclusion is the classical region

nodes.name: Carleson / corona / interpolating-sequence criteria for S = N/D
nodes.statement: Each theorem assumes the symbol bounded analytic in Re z > 0 (this is RH) or describes the zero set of an inner function; as criteria they hold for DH, HEAT, E_a, NR. The unconditional signed member is the Balazard-Saias-Yor Poisson-Jensen identity, whose sign is free and opposite to the one needed; RH is equality (no margin: S4, Q13). Corona data (N, D) measure simplicity of zeros of F. The zeros of S at height T sit at x about 1/(alpha lam^2), lam = (1/2) log(T/2 pi): Carleson mass 1/(pi alpha lam) per unit height. A prime-side Carleson embedding is Montgomery-Vaughan (P27, P29); that it is the only one is not proved.
nodes.mapStatus: CLASSICAL / ARGUED (audit of literature statements cited from memory); MEASURED
nodes.defeatedBy: DH, HEAT, EA, NR (criterion holds)

nodes.statement: Carries an inequality to the abscissa of convergence, for local parameters: output is abs(alpha_p) = 1 (SIZE). Positivity form is P25 with Fejer's cap a_1 < 2 a_0.

nodes.name: p-adic interpolation / Iwasawa module as operator
nodes.statement: The p-adic data for all p are functions of zeta(1 - k), k >= 1. The interpolation twin zeta + c L(s, chi_-4) L(s, chi_5) (ordinary Dirichlet series, same pole, finite order; no functional equation and no Euler product) has the same values at all non-positive integers and, for complex c, a zero at any prescribed s0 with L(s0, chi_-4) L(s0, chi_5) != 0 (c = 1: zero at 0.8641 + 29.9504i, measured). p-adic zeros are compared with complex zeros only in function fields (one polynomial). Device type: exact uniqueness, no inequality. The twin is a control of DH type for devices that read values; it says nothing about devices that use the functional equation (Hamburger uniqueness).

nodes.name: Turan power sums
nodes.statement: Finite form: coefficient-blind lower bound with loss e^{-cn}, holds for every control. Limit form: Turan's equivalence 'zero-free strip iff power saving in tau for sum_{p ~ N} p^{i tau}, N >= tau^a' is a theorem for zeta (CLASSICAL, cited from memory, not re-read); its extension to other Euler products was not checked (it needs continuation of finite order to the strip, which a general sign twist does not have). It restates the target as a prime-sum bound whose proof from integer sums is the rank-one bilinear obstruction (fam-vaughan-split-landau). Not of type 'one zero forces many'.

nodes.name: Strip Dirichlet-to-Neumann identity for the phase of S (annulus DtN node with the Klein phase certificate)
nodes.statement: -theta'(y) = T_b(y) + zero sum - pole sum, all kernels positive; -theta' is the Laguerre expression; T_b is computed on Re s = 1/2 + b >= 1 and T_b > 0 is proved for zeta only (for DH, which has zeros with Re s > 1, negativity of u on the edge is measured in the windows used). It is the Poisson-Jensen formula of the strip: residue device, exact, sign of the pole sum undetermined (S1); it holds for DH with its pole terms (measured). T_b is a fraction about 1/(b alpha lam^2) of the mean phase derivative (measured 0.74 to 0.10 for T = 10^2 to 10^5). The hypothesis of the Klein phase-transport certificate is the absence of nearby poles of S (P40, G13).

nodes.name: Positivity in the Bost-Connes algebra C*(Q/Z) x N^x (isometries mu_n, phases e(r), non-commuting) joined to the Fourier duality (campaign round 12)
nodes.statement: (i) Every sigma-invariant state factors through the conditional expectation onto C*(Q/Z) = C(Z^). For the Galois-invariant KMS_beta state the measure is a product, its values on the algebraic Hecke algebra are entire in beta and built from finitely many primes; for the extremal KMS states at beta > 1 the values are combinations of L(beta, chi)/zeta(beta) (meromorphic in beta, all primes; referee E1), and positivity there is positivity of the coefficients k^-beta at real beta > 1, passed by every control with non-negative coefficients. (ii) The Weil prime side is phi_{1/2}(H_g), H_g = sum Lambda(n) g(log n) mu_n mu_n^*; Weil's criterion is an upper bound for this state value on a non-positive element (row P1). (iii) For the archimedean vector states sum f(lambda k) e_k the Mellin transform of every matrix coefficient is a periodic zeta function times an archimedean factor: read set {L(s, chi)}; the mu_n step and the Poisson step are identities and the inequality is a square. (iv) Bochner positivity of the state holds on lines sigma > 1 and is lost at the pole; a sign-reversed kernel positivity holds on every line 0 < sigma < 1 for monotone F (Muntz formula; classical) and carries no zero information (referee). (v) T-NR is beta -> Tr(D e^{-beta H}) with D >= 1 a fixed positive element of C*(Q/Z) in the centraliser, that is, the value of the KMS family on a fixed D >= 1: as a function of beta it is zeta(beta) phi_beta(D), and it is an inner perturbation of the dynamics only at each beta separately (relabel 4); it differs from zeta only in exact mu_q covariance at the one prime q. E_a is the same device on A (x) A. DEL with finite S passes the mu_n step exactly and, when the functional-equation step is read as Poisson summation on e(r) (the lane's definition), that step too (referee, control table; with the reading "s <-> 1 - s" it fails there). Closed for three classes of states: sigma-invariant states, the dual-system state, Mellin families of archimedean vector states. (vi) Non-invariant states (campaign round 17, cell U6 (e); `c17-u6e-bost-connes-non-invariant-state-twin-ladder`, two referees). For every state omega and invertible b in A, omega(b* . b)/omega(b* b) is a state in the same GNS representation (CLASSICAL: Dixmier 2.4, Bratteli-Robinson 2.3; Lemma G of the lane). T-NR in the conjugation form (the vector with the T-NR coefficients a(k) k^-s is D xi_s, that is b = D; b = D^(1/2) gives coefficients a(k)^(1/2) k^-s; both are invertible and Lemma G applies to either; second referee C1, the first referee's E4 reached independently), finite DEL and the gauge twins are of this form, so positivity of a state never separates them from zeta; the one-sided form phi(D .)/phi(D) of the cell is not positive for a state whose centraliser does not contain D and is not the twin (referee E4). The mu*-eigenstates omega(x mu_m*) = m^-s omega(x) exist for every Re s > 0 (quasi-regular representation on L^2(Z^, nu_beta), beta = 2 Re s; adjoint V_n* g = n^-s g(n .), referee E1), are classified by a KMS_beta measure on Z^, and on the algebraic Hecke algebra read n^-conj(s), m^-s and finitely many local factors, or L(beta, chi)/zeta(beta) at real beta > 1 (Lemma E); on absolutely summable elements they read absolutely convergent series with every zeta argument of real part > 1 (referee E2: the read set for general elements of the norm closure is not described). Kernels <xi_w, X xi_s> read zeta(conj(w) + s; r) with real part > 1 and are positive semidefinite iff X >= 0 (Lemma K). Two eigenstates on Re s = beta/2 are at norm distance 2 sqrt(1 - abs(zeta(beta + i tau))^2/zeta(beta)^2) for beta > 1 and at distance exactly 2 for beta <= 1 (Lemma T; Kakutani's dichotomy for product vectors), also for DEL, THIN, U, the T-NR twin and E_a: for beta <= 1 no function of tau remains. Two-point functions of bounded elements are bounded in t (Lemma S). Consequence: a twin of the form b xi can be rejected only by an exact relation, not by positivity of a state. Closed for four classes of states: sigma-invariant states, the dual-system state, Mellin families of archimedean vector states, and positivity reads of non-invariant states together with the eigenstate class on algebraic and absolutely summable elements. Not covered: weights on the cokernel of Connes' map (type II_infinity weights at beta <= 1; positivity there is the Weil form, rows P1, G21); states defined by other exact relations; normal states of the type III_1 factor beyond the three families tried; general elements of the norm closure. Whether Lemma T proves the sentence of Lemma P relabelled ARGUED was not checked against the c12 lane by the referee. Correction to ROUND_LOG round 10: KMS_beta exists for every beta > 0; the read set "finitely many local factors" is that of the Galois-invariant state, and "real beta > 1" is the correct read set of the extremal states.

nodes.name: Borel Eisenstein series on the loop group of SL_2: constant term over the affine Weyl group with shifts by the central parameter c, Maass-Selberg positivity, degenerate Whittaker coefficients (campaig
nodes.statement: Coefficients are chain products of M(u) = xi(u)/xi(u+1) at u = z + kc and kc - z (coefficient census relative to a recalled normalisation; Garland's relations and the FKP formula for affine groups not opened). In the chamber 0 < Re z < Re c every denominator argument has Re > 1; strip arguments occur only as numerator arguments (the coefficients are not holomorphic in the chamber: poles at z + kc = 1 and kc - z = 1; referee correction 1). Rank-one Maass-Selberg positivity for T >= 1 is equivalent to: N = z(1 - S)/(1 + S), S = T^(-z) M(z), is a Nevanlinna function of z^2 (Theorem B; in content the Weyl-Titchmarsh function of the truncated problem, classical). The class is closed under multiplication of S by Blaschke factors over non-real conjugate pairs of the right half-plane (Theorem C, an elementary Moebius computation; a real zero taken twice is covered, a single real factor is not, and the sign is not free: phi = -M fails), so zeros can be prescribed anywhere in Re z > 0 off the real axis. Restrictions of the second referee (`c14-referee-r13-independent`, 4 to 6): the closure is for non-real conjugate pairs or real points with even multiplicity; the lane's statement for c = -2.1 (real zero pair) and for single real factors is MEASURED only and outside the proof; the sentence "the inequality carries no constraint on numerator zeros" is proved for the rank-one inequality (I) and OPEN for the affine inequality (I_aff), since closure of (I_aff) under M -> M Theta is not proved. T-NR with c > 2 and b = arccosh(c/2)/log q < 1/2 enters as the Blaschke factor D(z)/D(z+1) (section 2 note). At c = 1 the chamber is the critical strip, the diagram automorphism is s <-> 1 - s and every non-identity coefficient is xi(z)/xi(z+n): an identity between coefficients (existence of the series for Re c <= 2 is relative to continuation results not opened). Closed for the rank-one Levi inequality: PROVED. For the two-variable affine kernel the same closure is ARGUED, not proved (BLS and T-NR are not group objects there; no formula tested). Not covered: the wall Re c -> 0; inequalities that are not truncated-norm positivity.

By Krein-Langer (recalled, source not opened) the stage kernel has infinitely many negative squares, at density theta(X)/pi per unit height, and no stage de Branges space, Pontryagin space or Hamiltonian exists. As recorded by the lane, the count goes to infinity along the stages and to zero in the limit, so no monotone or semicontinuous limit device (de Branges ordering, Krein-Langer counts) follows it. abs(theta_p)^2 - 1 has the sign of 2 cos(t log p) - p^{-sigma} - p^{sigma-1} for sigma > 1/2 (exact, also for unimodular twists): adjoining a prime is neither contractive nor expansive; K_X(w, w) is not monotone in X (MEASURED at 20 points, sign changes at 14; the same for the Liouville twist and random U). The Euler factor is lossless only about Re s = 0; the functional equation is not an input of any finite Euler stage. Not closed by this: a stage that takes the functional equation as an input (functional-equation-symmetrised stage, `c4-fe-stage-rouche-crossing`).

nodes.name: Hecke operators T_{p^2}, U_2 and the Fricke involution w_4 acting on theta restricted to the real oval of X_0(4), as a base-side loading of the arc (classical identities; bookkeeping of real against c
nodes.statement: Mellin transform along the arc turns every term into a Dirichlet polynomial in p^(-s) times Lambda(s). T_{p^2} has 2 real and p^2 + p - 2 complex isogenous points (outside a countable set of x); real points: multiplier R_p(s) = 2 p^(-3/2) cosh((s - 1/2) log p); summed complex points: C_p = 1 + 1/p - R_p, a combination of dilates of theta, positive on the arc (PROVED by a two-line argument of the second referee; was MEASURED at 9 points). R_p + C_p = 1 + 1/p is the relation c(pm) = c(m), the Euler factor: an identity. C_p Lambda is -p^(-3/2) times the T-NR twin with c = -(p^(3/2) + p^(1/2)) (c < -2, extra zeros real and outside the closed strip: Re s = 2.2423 at p = 3; "is a T-NR twin" holds only with this qualifier, relabel 7); every twin, including those with 2 < abs(c) < q^(1/2) + q^(-1/2), is (q^(-1/2) D_{q^-2} + q^(1/2) D_{q^2} + c) theta and lies in the module generated by dilations on theta, so no statement about the module separates them (referee E2). <D_l, W> acts on a W-fixed vector through the commutative quotient a + bW -> a + b. Termwise bounds lose (p - 1) p^(-1/2). Unsummed complex points: a single point has a Mellin transform with zeros off the line (measured, p = 5); the second moment over the points tau + b/p is Theta_{L+} + Theta_{L-} - theta(p^2 x)^2, row G16, with off-line zeros for the class [2,2,5] (measured). Closed for four forms: linear expressions in Hecke images of theta on the arc, dilation-covariant quadratic forms, single complex points, their second moment. Non-linear reads of the unsummed complex points (campaign round 17, cell U6 (f); `c17-u6f-isogenous-points-norm-jensen-gap`, two referees): the norm of the p^2 + p - 2 point values is theta(x)^(p^2+p)/(theta(x/p^2) theta(p^2 x)), a module identity in the dilation module of log theta (Mellin multiplier p^2 + p - p^(2u) - p^(-2u), of T-NR shape, on M[log theta]) (PROVED); the Jensen gap between trace and norm is a pointwise function of three dilates, negative on the whole arc with limit log(p/(p+2)) at the cusp, a consequence of the sum identity, the norm identity and monotonicity (PROVED); the sign of the discriminant is the parity (-1)^((p+2)(p-1)/2) of the number of conjugate pairs for every function with real coefficients (CLASSICAL discriminant sign rule; relabelled by the referee). The Epstein forms theta(x) theta(nx), n = 5, 6, pass all three reads and both identities at inert primes (PROVED; fail at split primes through the sum identity, MEASURED). The conjunction 'sum identity and norm identity at every p' is the statement that f is a Hecke eigenform with a product formula: an identification, not an inequality (that it identifies f up to a finite list of eta quotients is ARGUED). Closed for seven forms: the four above and these three reads. Not excluded: symmetric functions of degree at least 3 of the point values (ARGUED to be modular forms of level 4 p^2 outside the dilation module; no candidate inequality on file).

nodes.name: Fourier interpolation with nodes at the zeros and frequencies log n/(4 pi) (Bondarenko-Radchenko-Seip, arXiv:2005.02996), with the Radchenko-Viazovska pair (sqrt n, sqrt n) on the theta group as the c
nodes.statement: The kernel is (F*(s)/F*(w)) times A_k(w, s), with A_k a target-independent Dirichlet series of the theta group, unique by Bochner's converse theorem (relative to the source's sections 3, 4; sections 3 and 6 not re-derived). This factorisation is exact for the kernel H_- only (second referee `c14-referee-r13-independent`, restrictions 7 and 8; source display (4.6), lines 1364 to 1387 of the lane's source text): H_+ = (F*(s)/2)[A^+_(1/2)(w/2, s/2)/F*(w) - alpha^+_(1,1/2)(s/2)] with h^+_1 := 0, a subtracted term the lane's display omitted, so for H_+ the kernel built by the source's recipe and the orbit kernel differ by a multiple of 1/G(w). The target enters by division in both. Kernels built by this recipe inside one gamma class and one sign of the functional equation are related by symmetric multipliers G(s)/G(w) (Lemma M: an identity of these kernels, exact for H_- and with the additive term above for H_+, not a classification of all interpolation bases with these nodes; referee C5). In Lemma T the frequency set has one sign at m = q^2 in the H_+ family (restriction 9, as stated by the second referee; not re-derived by the map lane). The Euler product is read twice: absolute convergence of 1/F in Re w > 1 (the proof needs sum over d <= y of abs(b(d))/d << y^eps, which T-NR satisfies with unbounded coefficients; "abs(mu(d)) <= 1" over-describes the input, C9), giving the edge Re w = 1 and partial sums of size x^(1/2+eps) (inequality (I-1)); and the Ramachandra-Sankaranarayanan horizontal lower bound (function class only). For multiplier controls (T-NR: factor P(1/2 + iz), real, of one sign, modulus in [abs(c) - 2, abs(c) + 2]) off-line nodes change no sign or decay of the basis functions in z; for a general target nothing is established about signs (no basis function was computed; C7). Off-line nodes move the exponent of the partial sums in the frequency index from 1/4 to beta/2 < 1/2. For s outside a countable set, partial sums of size x^kappa imply that no zero has Re rho > 2 kappa (PROVED-rel); the converse, that the exponent equals half the supremum of Re rho, is ARGUED (C1, C2): a restatement of Littlewood type. The pivot (Weil functional in the basis, W U_n = Lambda(m)/(pi sqrt m) for n = m^2) is the explicit formula in coordinates (positivity rows of section 3.1). Closed at stage A. Not covered: the kernel for the gamma factor Gamma_R(s+a) Gamma_R(s-a) (E_a, EIS-w); signs of DH basis functions; stage B (the functions U_n, V_rho) was not run.

nodes.name: Luo-Rudnick-Sarnak mechanism (Rankin-Selberg positivity, even twists in the conductor aspect, gamma pole at the non-tempered parameter) applied to E*(z, rho/2) and to Borel Eisenstein objects at regul
nodes.statement: At xi(rho) = 0 the completed Rankin-Selberg function G(w) = xi(w + beta - 1) xi(w + 1 - beta) xi(w + i gamma) xi(w - i gamma) has exactly one simple pole pair, at w = 2 - beta and beta - 1 (six of the eight residues carry xi at rho or a reflection of rho; the pair that survives uses the functional equation at rho; for beta = 1/2 the statement is the regularity of G at 1/2 at a zero of any multiplicity). This is the pole count of a cusp form, at P = 2 - beta instead of 1. The gamma pole of the even twists is at beta_0 = 1 - beta, so P - beta_0 = 1 for every parameter: for Borel (GL_1-induced) data of any rank at regular parameters, and for any Hecke eigen-object with these Satake parameters, the statement follows from the Hecke eigenvalues alone (referee defect 2; walls excluded). The vanishing forced at the gamma pole is the trivial zero L(0, chi) = 0 of even chi, an identity in the parameter. The inequality of the mechanism beta_0 <= w*(P, d) reads beta <= 7/4, relative to the reconstructed threshold of the lane's section 3.1 (LRS 1995 not opened; restriction 10 of `c14-referee-r13-independent`); it is the one displayed inequality the device yields only in that relative sense. The mechanism needs P = 1 independent of the parameter (square-integrability), available only for zeros outside the closed strip (row G12). Lemma 1 is a corollary of the classical Rankin-Selberg transform of a product of two Eisenstein series (Zagier 1981, not opened); not a new theorem. Not covered: non-Borel objects (residual or cuspidal data on a larger group with Rankin-Selberg pole left of 2 - beta; no candidate on file); a level-q object for T-NR.
nodes.mapStatus: PROVED (Lemmas 1, 2, 3; Lemma 4 relative to Gindikin-Karpelevich), re-derived by two independent referees (contour residues at zeros 3 and 5 and two generic parameters; the second, `c14-referee-r13-independent`, at zeros 1, 2, 5 and the generic parameter (0.62, 9.3)); LRS exponent count ARGUED (reconstructed; reproduces 1 - 2/(n^2+1); LRS 1995 not opened; the verdict does not depend on it); numerics MEASURED; five wording defects

nodes.statement: MEASURED, finite search; closed as a device class on the registered grid and draws only, with the conventions of the lane's PREREG section 2. Of 12,994,697 functionals evaluated on 290 objects, 629,432 are one-signed on the 24 positives (459,547 of them from the adaptive stage, not independent draws); none has the opposite sign on a member of every control class (0 at every tier; 841,651 cases not decided by float64 resolved in balls). 0 of the 629,432 give the battery Davenport-Heilbronn function the opposite sign; 400 reject a backward-heat member. The positive condition is a fitted condition on 24 objects and does not hold out: held-out L-functions of conductor 14 to 40 take the opposite sign at a mean rate 0.287, higher than held-out DH members of real-part type (0.193), so the DH count is not a sensitivity of D to the Euler product (referee finding 1). By family: minors of the kernel with polar terms never reject backward heat or theta^w; minors of the kernel without polar terms never reject E_a, backward heat or EIS-w (the sign depends on the order alone). With zeta as the only positive: five functionals reject a battery member of every class, none meets the held-out rule, and each separates zeta from the L-functions as well. Registered prediction "T-NR passes the minors with polar terms" is false (pass fraction 0.646); "E_a passes" holds on the registered positives. Lemma H (heat passes the order-2 part of one family) is the only proved statement; its consequence is relative to the classical log-concavity of the Riemann-Polya kernel (source not opened; restriction 13 of `c14-referee-r13-independent`). Not run, and not covered: Hermitian forms for complex kernels; orders above 4; more than three real parameters or nodes outside [-2.6, 2.6]; functionals reading two kernels at once (lane `c14-joint-zeta-twist-noncone-search`); other kernels or normalisations.

nodes.name: Hecke-built norms outside weighted L2 on Lax-Phillips resonance states f_rho (residues of the Eisenstein series at rho/2): solid norms, the Hecke-sup norm, L^q with q < 2, and the Hecke-invariant spac
nodes.statement: Closed for four named families, not for norms in general (referee item 4). (a) Solid norms: a solid space X containing f_rho contains the constants, so the operator norm of T_p^k on the whole of X is at least (p^(1/2) + p^(-1/2))^k and reads 0 <= beta <= 1 only (Theorem L); on the mean-zero subspace X_0 (which contains f_rho and is T_p-invariant, and on which Theorem L says nothing) the referee's repair gives: X contains 1 + ht^(Re w), hence every E(., w') with 1/2 < Re w' <= Re w, these lie in X_0 and are T_p-eigenfunctions, so the eigenvalue bound is implied by admissibility, by EIS-w; invariant subspaces smaller than X_0 are not classified. (b) Hecke-sup norm sup_n N_0(T_n f)/lambda_theta(n): N(T_m f) <= lambda_theta(m) N(f) by the Hecke multiplication rule (H1); finite on an eigenvector iff abs(Re mu) <= theta, which is the conclusion (H2); dominated by a two-sided wave-growth norm sup_t e^(-theta abs(t)) N_0(cosh(t sqrt(L)) f), L = Delta + 1/4, defined for every Lax-Phillips triple (Lemma Q after the referee's typing repair: stated on functions with T_n = sum over dd' = n of cosh(log(d/d') sqrt(L)), one-directional, on the Eisenstein channel); commutation transfers growth bounds and produces none (H3). (c) L^q, 1 <= q < 2: admissibility q < 1/(1/2 + a) implies the bound; off-resonance Eisenstein series fill the spectrum (Lemma E). (d) The space with zero mode O(y^(1/2+delta)) as y -> 0 reads phi(w) = 0 and is Hecke-invariant; the device on it is Zagier's horocycle criterion with T_n acting by dilations (Lemma O; criterion CLASSICAL, recalled). Multiplicativity enters in H1 only, as an identity that the wave group satisfies without Hecke operators. The sentence on interpolation for L^q_0 (lane section 5) is not derived: OPEN, not used. Not covered: non-solid norms that are not of Hecke-sup, translation-covariant or model-functorial type; part (iii) of the lane's decisive test (general gauges) is ARGUED. Second independent referee pass (`c15-referee-r14-independent-checkpoint`; holds with a scope line; `LABEL_RESTRICTIONS.md` items 18 to 22): Corollary L1 holds as an operator norm on X, and on the mean-zero subspace the bound is implied by admissibility (18; already in this row); decisive test (iii) and the "not covered" list are ARGUED statements about classes of constructions (19); Lemma Q is PROVED-rel c4 Lemma 1 and the wave evolution of non-L^2 data (20); the lane's H2 figure 4.1e10 is a product of local suprema at k <= 60, and on one prime the supremum is 1.000 for k <= 30 (21); Zagier's criterion, Sarnak's exponent and Kim-Sarnak are recalled, not opened, and "BLS" in the lane is the lane's reading (22).

nodes.name: Joint functionals of the pair (zeta, L(s, chi)): the ratio Q_chi = L(s, chi)/zeta(s) (winding, Littlewood and Nevanlinna quantities; vortex charges of both signs), the cross bridge Gram form of (S_zet
nodes.statement: J1, ratio: every winding quantity is the signed difference of the member counts; a multiplier common to both members cancels, so T-NR at a prime p0 = 1 mod q has identical ratios for any finite set of characters (Lemma C). With all moduli (Lemma A, relative to the conductor-aspect density theorem as recalled, source not opened): a comparison COMP, N_zeta(W) <= N_chi(W') for q^theta' characters mod q and infinitely many q, with theta' > 3(1 - sigma)/(2 - sigma) for sigma in [1/2, 4/5] (referee E1: for sigma > 4/5 the second range of the theorem or monotonicity N(sigma) <= N(4/5) is used), implies no zero of zeta right of sigma in W; COMP is equivalent to the target. For T-NR at a split prime COMP is the same statement as for zeta plus a common term (not "holds with equality"; E2); for E_a the corresponding line is ARGUED. J2, cross Gram: rank min(m, n) for finite simple pole sets, vanishes iff one member is causal; identities for any pair of unitary symbols. J3, twist-transfer: for narrow bumps at log m the prime sides of W_chi(g_c) and W_zeta(g_(c chi)) are equal (identity TW; the width condition is used: referee rerun, defect 1.4e-8 inside and 0.02 to 0.05 outside it); the difference is archimedean with leading term (log q) times the squared norms; it holds for every F whose twist has a functional equation. The general form "every pair functional that consumes the twist relation cancels the prime side" is ARGUED (E3); the closure of J3 uses TW only. DH twists (MEASURED, float64 winding numbers, 141 and 192 twists, no interval certificate): no enhancement of off-line zeros of the twists at the off-line zero of DH; background rate 0.07 to 0.10 per twist per box of height 2, so the q^theta' form of COMP is expected to hold for DH (ARGUED) and the comparison link has no content for a control with a positive density of off-line zeros (E4). The pair lift of DH keeps a functional equation only for q = +-1 mod 5. Not covered: functionals not homogeneous in each kernel and triples with the group law (lane `c15-nonhomogeneous-pair-triple-kernel-search`, row G41); infinite pole sets in J2. Second independent referee pass (`c15-referee-r14-independent-checkpoint`; holds with a scope line; `LABEL_RESTRICTIONS.md` items 8 to 12): Lemma A has the exponent 3(1 - sigma)/(2 - sigma) for 1/2 < sigma_0 <= 4/5, and above 4/5 it is 2(1 - sigma)/sigma or 1/2 (8); Lemmas A and B are PROVED-rel Montgomery, Theorem 12.1, recalled, not opened (two searches) (9); identity TW: the second display is for chi even, the whole identity for chi primitive and c supported on (m, q) = 1 (10); Lemma C is for a finite set of characters, p0 depends on the set, and the pair lift is coefficientwise (11); the E_a and DH rows of link 1 (lane section 2.6) are ARGUED / undecided (12).

nodes.name: Weight-1/2 Eisenstein series on Gamma_0(4) at s_rho = 1/4 + rho/2 (square-index coefficients vanish; T_(p^2) eigenvalue p^(rho-1/2) + p^(1/2-rho)); Luo-Rudnick-Sarnak exponent count with theta-orthogo
nodes.statement: Coefficient formula derived from the definition: A(n^2, s) = W(s) zeta(2s - 1/2)/((1 + 2^(1/2-2s)) zeta(4s - 1)) times a finite Dirichlet polynomial; constant term y^s + phi y^(1-s) with phi proportional to zeta(4s - 2)/zeta(4s - 1). The whole square-index row vanishes at zeros of zeta (Lemma 1': every A(n^2, s) carries zeta(u)/zeta(2u), u = 2s - 1/2; confirmed at zeros 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 20 for even and odd n). The vanishing is NOT the single condition b(1) = 0 propagated by the Hecke relation at squares (referee correction 1): that relation is for odd p and gives odd squares only; at u_0 = 1 + i pi/ln 2 one has b(1) = b(9) = 0 with abs(zeta(u_0)) = 0.7295 and abs(A(4)) = 0.2162, abs(A(16)) = 0.3243; the condition is b(1) = 0 and b(4^j) = 0, or Lemma 1' directly. The vanishing row annihilates the first-moment (Shimura) series and removes no polar term of the second-moment series, whose poles are at 1/2 + beta, 3/2 - beta, 1 +- i gamma (positions relative to the regularised Rankin-Selberg method, Zagier 1981, not opened; exponent rule 1 + abs(2 sigma - 1) measured at five parameters). Rightmost pole P = 1 + abs(beta - 1/2), gamma pole beta_0 = abs(beta - 1/2): P - beta_0 = 1, and the count returns an inequality true for every beta. Lemma E: (i), (ii) an eigenfunction of moderate growth with non-real eigenvalue on a finite-volume rank-one quotient (any weight, cover, vector) has a non-zero dominant constant-term coefficient at some cusp (otherwise it is square-integrable and the eigenvalue is real; classical, not new); (iii) P - beta_0 = 1 for it, relative to the same unopened method. "Other rows do not vanish" is MEASURED at the listed m and zeros; in general it is L(rho, chi_t) != 0, not proved (correction 4). The second object (residue at (1 + rho)/4) is the Shimura preimage of the object of row G35. Not covered: rank >= 2 non-Borel or metaplectic objects (no candidate on file). Second independent referee pass (`c15-referee-r14-independent-checkpoint`; holds with a scope line; `LABEL_RESTRICTIONS.md` items 13 to 17): "one linear condition b(1) = 0, propagated to the whole row by the Hecke relation at squares" is false as written; every A(n^2, s) carries zeta(u) (Lemma 1') and b(1) = 0 gives the odd squares only (13; already in this row); in Lemma V the phrase "times non-zero local functionals" is wrong at the prime 2 on Re u = 1 (14); the definition of f_q is the repaired one, with level and multiplier relative to Shimura 1973, not opened (15); Lemma 3 and Lemma E (iii) are PROVED-rel the regularised Rankin-Selberg method, not opened, with exponents MEASURED (16); Lemma E closes the LRS-type count in rank one, not every inequality on a rank-one object (17).

nodes.name: Catalogue of twelve inequalities of the literature that consume a Hecke eigen-relation or exact local factor at every prime (Rankin; Rankin-Selberg-Serre with Landau; Langlands-Deligne tensor powers;
nodes.statement: No entry has all hypotheses met by a zero-indexed object at a zero in the open strip. Lemma T: for a torus parameter every L(s, Pi, r x chi) is a product of shifted Dirichlet L-functions and the rightmost pole minus the rightmost local or gamma pole equals 1 for every parameter and every r; the forced vanishing sits on the line Re w = P - 1 (real only when the minimising weight is real; referee error 4). The position part of the hypothesis "pole at 1" (rightmost pole on Re s = 1) is equivalent to the conclusion with exponent 0; the pole is never simple for a torus object with n >= 2 (error 1). Proposition E: the Eisenstein-series proof of zeta(1 + it) != 0 is the one entry met in full with a hypothesis specific to zeros, at Re rho = 1 (the known proof, CLASSICAL); in the strip the single missing hypothesis is xi(2 - rho) = 0, false by the Euler product. For the weight-1/2 object only the Jacquet-Shalika entry has all hypotheses met exactly when beta = 1/2 (unitarity and genericity); the six entries needing cuspidality or square-integrability fail at every parameter (error 2: the shadow E(z, rho) at beta = 1/2 is on the unitary axis and not square-integrable); theta-orthogonality is a hypothesis of no entry. nodes.name: Hecke amplification of the truncated norm of E*(z, rho/2) at a zero rho = 1 - delta + i gamma (edge argument for a strip width; family 31 of `campaign/STRATEGY.md` section 3.1; campaign rounds 15 and
nodes.statement: At a zero the truncated norm is exactly abs(xi(2 - rho))^2 T^delta/delta, and at T = 1 the device inequality is the identity M = L + S. On the truncated series T_m acts as a combination of truncations at dilated heights: T_m Lambda^T f = lambda(m) f minus pseudo-Eisenstein series cut at heights T d/a. T >= N: the amplified norm is M(T) x*Kx with K depending on (gamma, delta) only, the gain is at most N^delta, and the amplified inequality is implied by the unamplified one (PROVED; two referees). T < N (round 16): closed Gram formula for all T >= 1, N, sigma != 1 (PROVED; agrees with quadrature to 7e-14, Hecke relations to 1e-82); R2 = 1 for T >= N; R2 <= M/L (a validity statement, not a structural cap on the amplifier; item 5.3 of the independent referee). **Family 31 item "T < N": measured obstruction on T <= 4, N <= 128** (gamma <= 541): G_opt < N^delta at on-line zeros in every computed row, crossing factor in [0.987, 1.0094] (MEASURED, arb balls); 463 formal rows with delta >= 0.01. Not a proved closure: G_opt <= N^delta for all N with T < N, the large-height small-delta regime and boundedness of M/L are OPEN. The registered prediction R2 <= 1 failed for T < N (sup R2 between 1.04 and 1.46 for N <= 8 only, float64, local optimiser, lower bounds), also at EIS-w points: below the truncation height Hecke operators stop acting by dilation, and the effect is a bounded constant shared by the control. Disposition of the fired clause S2 of the lane's pre-registration (planner, round 17): set aside; the clause had no control comparison; EIS-w shares the excess; no follow-up lane. Width obtainable from the device: c/log^5 gamma (ARGUED), weaker than classical. Correction of the second referee to the c15 lane: for unimodular parameters alpha_p = i one has tau(p) = 0; for alpha_p = i p^(-delta/2) it is -i (p^(delta/2) - p^(-delta/2)).

nodes.statement: The Fejer-weighted form (C-F) of 3 + 4 cos + cos 2 holds for every sigma, t, U with every term finite in 1/2 < sigma < 1 (identity E; truncation defect 1e-7 to 3e-6 at non-prime-power X with 600 to 800 zeros, 1e-4 to 1e-3 at prime-power X: a truncation figure, not a precision of the identity; referee E7). No relation between primes is read. Theorem T: a pointwise lower bound with positive weights and a locally bounded right side holds on an open set iff the set is zero-free (for fixed translates as stated; for the triple sigma + ikt by the same computation with the referee's two repairs, E2; sentence to use, both referees: for the triple sigma + ikt a lower bound with B locally bounded in (sigma, t) on a strip holds if and only if the strip is zero-free): the pointwise forms left of 1 are zero-freeness itself. Lemma S (with the local boundedness hypothesis, E3): sign control of the zero terms up to abscissa theta forces v(u) e^(-sigma u) <= v(0+) e^(-theta u); for the Fejer weight the sign region is exactly Re z <= 0 (proved by the referee), so sign control forces a test at abscissa >= 1. Lemma V (sentence of the second referee, C3): a simple zero at distance delta from Re s = 1 can exceed the pole term in the 3-4-1 mechanism only if the mean log-length of the test is below log 2/delta (log(m a_1/a_0)/delta for order m; E5). nodes.statement: Stage A stopped the lane; no server run. Lemma N: non-negative coefficients of F^(k)/F (with the sign (-1)^k) for one k force a(n) >= 0, so log-derivative positivity of any degree with the functional equation and the pole clause lies in the identification class of Theorem P (row P56); a bookkeeping statement. Candidate (J), cross-prime positivity of the pair form (the part of Lambda_2 supported on products p^j q^k, p != q): true for zeta, trivially. Its multiplicative step is a sign relation between atoms at different primes, and this is the failing step for T-NR and for sign chains (the first such step on file). **Correction E1 of the referee (the lane had the Liouville twist passing): for Liouville Lambda(p^j) Lambda(q^k) = (-1)^(j+k) log p log q is negative when j + k is odd; it fails at the cross atom p q^2, first at n = 12 (coefficient -2 log 2 log 3 = -1.523; also 18, 20, 28), and passes only for P <= 12. nodes.statement: Holds exactly for T-NR with c >= 2 (c > 0; the zeros of the twin leave the line only for c > 2, so at c = 2 the condition holds with every zero on the line: second referee `c14-referee-r13-independent`, restriction 1) and for E_a (exact arithmetic), and fails for the tempered twin with abs(c) < 2, for L(s, chi) at primes with chi(p) = -1 and for tempered degree-2 factors: the condition is ordered against the target (it selects real non-negative local parameters, not unimodular ones). It says nothing about dilation minors of the kernel: the registered prediction that T-NR passes the minors of row G36 because its local sequence is totally positive was refuted (pass fraction 0.646). nodes.name: Dirac / dilation identity on the Mayer operator
nodes.statement: The Lagrange identity holds for every g (no eigen-equation, three-term relation or Hecke input); Re(rho) - 1/2 comes from the weight u^(1/2). For the Eisenstein eigenfunction the boundary term is unbounded (coefficient zeta(rho-1) != 0, zero on the Maass channel), so the form is not finite on the critical line. The only channel-restricted object, [(1-L_b)^(-1) 1](0) = 2 zeta(2b-1)/zeta(2b), restates RH; sup-norm sigma_min(1-L_b) -> 0 on Re b < 1/2 unconditionally.

nodes.statement: Coefficients >= residue plus zeta's exact FE force the integers (1.1). So no such control exists, and the direction yields identification, not an inequality. Limited to zeta's own FE.

nodes.statement: Euler product iff w in {1,2,4,8}; Hecke-eigen set {1..8}. The on-line window around w = 1 shrinks on both sides with height (to (0.99482, 1.00876) at 2000). w = 4 is multiplicative with 44 of 202 zeros on the line. Non-emptiness of the window restates RH plus simplicity to height T. abs(w-1) log T = const is rejected for first departure.

nodes.statement: No Euler product for 0 < w < 1. Zeros leave the line Re s = w/2 and return (29 departures, 29 returns below height 205; event counts are lower bounds; independent check at height 39 only); departures mix zeros of different births, so no pairing of zeta zeros with w = 0 pairs.

nodes.statement: Genus 2: interval structure of I_C proved; lower endpoint is a zero collision u_d = 2 sqrt(h) - N_1 - 1. Genus-2 median log-length of the component containing q is about 2.7/q (q <= 19); at q = 3 it falls by 2.1-2.4 per unit of genus (g <= 5, conditional on an unverified class-count formula). The q^{-g/2} law for g >= 3 and any transfer to zeta are not established.

A multiple-Dirichlet-series route must derive the functional equation of the theta-dual m-series (MS (5.3)) or it is closed by Theorem T. Open: Bochner hull of the estimate-supplied region.

Unmarked norm << Z^M (log Z)^4 for M >= 2N + eps is the classical trivial range. K-loss removal follows from a flat Gram spectrum (converse false). No property invariant under M -> -M (W D factorisation, Krein form, norm, normality defect) forces the circle; the radius is Weil's bound. Over Z the eigenvalue branch leaves Re s = 1/4 at first order under phase rotation (rates 0.244, 0.222).

nodes.name: Spin of prime ideals (cyclic cubic fields) as an order-2 row
nodes.statement: Cocycle is the quadratic symbol of K times a rational Jacobi symbol times a 2-adic Hilbert symbol; -1 on half of pairs of split primes of distinct residue characteristic. (alpha/sigma(b)) is a relabelling of (alpha/b): same singular values and Poisson dual class. Spin times a non-vanishing multiplicative function is never mu times a Hecke character. A {+-1} symbol with bicharacter cocycle absorbs mu only if the cocycle is trivial.

nodes.name: Borel Eisenstein coefficients on the double cover of GL(3) as absorbing rows
nodes.statement: Row-linear coefficients are +chi_d(p) for squarefree d coprime to p, -chi_{d0}(p) only at d = d0 p^2, else 0 (Whittaker normalisation). The Moebius-times-symbol term lies on the slice d = d0 m^2 with generating function d0^-w / L(s+2w, chi_d0). With mu inserted only sigma_2 survives: region inf Re s = 1. Untested: theta representation, cuspidal and maximal-parabolic objects.

One-prime model C*/p^Z gives only Re s = 0. Non-holomorphy of the scaling action is Connes-Consani's own statement (section 7); their W-coefficient Frobenius (section 7.1) was not examined. Global lift formula formal (OPEN).

nodes.name: Kuenneth / Kurokawa multiple Euler series
nodes.statement: Symmetrised prime-pair sum = -int_c^{s-c} Psi_X(w) Psi_X(s-w) dw for arbitrary weights (integer spacing unused). No form converges absolutely for Re s < 2 (>= k for k factors, also pole-removed). Pole-removed series converges conditionally for Re s > 1 + Theta, the input itself. Zero sums lie behind log branch points at c + rho; poles of residue -1/+1 at 2 rho on the two sides of the cut. Landau with positivity returns Theta <= 1.

At a simple zeta zero there is no off-line zero of F near the anchor, but the neighbourhood has no uniform size (jump curve 0.011 from rho_3, boundary point 8.5e-5 from the D = -43 anchor): the stability radius is a zero-gap quantity.

Any zero-free sequence on Re s > 1/2 converging to 1/zeta on an open set is unbounded, with unbounded inverse, on every Jordan curve around s = 1 meeting that set. log abs(Theta_S zeta) = -Re Ei((1-s) log x) + O_K(1) + O(abs(s) x^{1-sigma} e^{-c sqrt(log x)}); a pure O(1) remainder is equivalent to RH. Line invariants are archimedean (Maslov index theta(T)/pi + O(1)) or endpoint signs. Shifted pair is Hermite-Biehler iff zeta is zero-free in Re s >= 1/2 + a. A partner with count theta(T)/pi + O(1) cannot interlace the zeros of Xi.

nodes.name: Partial Euler products sampled at the zeros (R_S; A_S = sum over zeros in a window of abs(zeta_S(1/2 + i gamma))^2)
nodes.statement: The lower inequality R_S >= 0 is the target (P10). The upper (depletion) inequality is the Landau-Gonek diagonal term: mean ratio A_S/(N M_P) = 1 - 2 c_P/L to first order, c_P = sum_{p <= P} log p/(p - 1), L = log(T/2 pi); it is a function of x = (log P - gamma_E)/L only (1 - 2x for x <= 0.25; about x^{-3} for x >= 0.6), tends to 1 at fixed P as T grows, and needs only the prime-power coefficients of -F'/F. In windows of 500 / 2000 zeros at heights 1e3 to 1e8, P = 10 to 1e5, the ratio stays below 0.904 / 0.782; against one-spacing shifts it exceeds 1 in some windows (max 1.172). The DH formal product at DH zeros (on-line and off-line; float64 zeros, not certified) and the Liouville twist at rho/2 show the same suppression; E_a and heat tau = -0.5 satisfy the depletion inequality. Partial Euler multipliers damp off-line pairs. R_S -> 0 as P grows. Surviving identity: the S-periodised explicit formula (Lemma B: positivity range support < log(2 N_S) at the price of residues of zeta'/zeta at 1 + 2 pi i k/log p); it holds for every control with the functional equation. Closed as a restatement in round 3: row P43.
nodes.mapStatus: PROVED (Lemma B, Cor. B1; refereed once); MEASURED (two independent lanes, each refereed once with corrections; rows T0 = 1e3, P = 10 and 100 of the zeta table reproduced in ball arithmetic by `c3-repair-map-theorem-a`)

nodes.name: Window-local projection domination (off-line pair against its on-line projection) with the smoothed Landau-Gonek identity as arithmetic partner
nodes.statement: The smoothed identity is the Weil explicit formula with a band-limited window: S_w(log n_0) = -(H w^(0)/2 pi) Lambda(n_0)/sqrt(n_0) for n_0 + 1 < H, with a remainder about H (8H/T)^7 log T (so H = o(T^{7/8}) is needed; the lane's "exact, no error term" does not hold). The lower bound forced by an off-line pair, 2 abs(W) sinh(delta log N) - M_on, is below the trivial sqrt(N) bound on short twisted prime sums for every H, N and delta < 1/2; closing that gap is the zero-free statement. Only the support and size of Lambda enter; a multiplicative weight gives no gain.

nodes.name: Pole-lattice test multipliers (Lemma B: the S-periodised explicit formula; theta-family and shifted forms) as a route to an inequality
nodes.statement: By Poisson summation in k the residue sum over the poles 1 + 2 pi i k/log p equals Weil's pole term minus the prime sum for the test Z_S w, truncated together: Lemma B is the Weil explicit formula for a non-compactly supported test, regularised. It has no sign of its own; the enlarged support threshold log(2 N_S) is bookkeeping, not a gain; the only inequality step is the classical zero-free region (Littlewood / Vinogradov-Korobov form). Proved for abs(S) = 1 (finite-smoothness profiles included); for abs(S) >= 2 for C_c^inf tests, with absolute convergence from a Baker-type bound whose constant was not checked against the source. Shifted form (multiplier zeta_S(s - 1 + sigma_0), poles on Re s = sigma_0; `c3-lemmab-halfplane-growing-s`): a correct identity; with the residues bounded in absolute value through sup bounds of zeta'/zeta on the line, positivity is certified only for support T_w <= f(sigma_0) log log T, f = (sigma_0 - Theta)/((1 - Theta)(sigma_0 - 1/2)), f(1) = 2 for every Theta including RH (the Littlewood scale X = (log T)^2). Support c log T is not reached and the 7/8 half-plane adds no range. This is an obstruction of the bounding method, not a proof that positivity fails beyond 2 log log T; a signed treatment of the lattice sum is the target (P10).
nodes.mapStatus: PROVED (abs(S) = 1; refereed once, seven corrections); abs(S) >= 2 PROVED-rel the Baker-type bound (Proposition P and the constant: referee debt); DH check MEASURED (14 cases, two codes, off-line pairs up to 61% of the zero side; relative residual about 2.2e-11 in float64 once the quadrature step of the archimedean term is converged: -2.256e-11 and -2.170e-11 in the two cases rerun at step 0.001 and 0.0005 by `c12-control-battery-harness`, replay D3. The figure "at most 5.4e-12" recorded earlier belongs to the single step size 0.002, where all eight residuals are +3.9e-12 to +4.6e-12; it is a partial cancellation, not the converged value. The origin of the remaining 2e-11 was not isolated); shifted identity MEASURED (30 cases, at most 2.0e-10); range bound PROVED for the method (refereed once)

nodes.name: Functional-equation-symmetrised Euler stage (Gonek 2012: G_X = P_X + chi conj(P_X)) with Rouche or Hurwitz comparison; stage collisions as carriers of zero information
nodes.statement: The on-line theorem is P-independent: G_X = 0 forces abs(chi(s)) = 1 because abs(conj P_X) = abs(P_X) != 0, so every zero with 0 <= sigma <= 1, t >= C_0 lies on the line for every X and for any non-vanishing P (Gonek Thm 6.2, Lemma 6.1, opened). It holds verbatim for every unimodular twist, the Liouville twist, E_a-type products and Beurling products; it contains no arithmetic. The stage is not analytic; the analytic stage P_X(s) + chi(s) P_X(1 - s) has off-line zeros outside the range where the phase F_X is monotone (X < L^2/16 sharp cut; about (L log L)^2/16 Fejer; L = log(t/2 pi); row Q11). The degree (Poincare-Bohl) form of Rouche on a box: zeta/G_X avoids (-inf, 0] on the boundary. It implies the box is zero-free, so no statement strictly weaker than zero-freeness of the boxes implies it; at fixed X it fails at arbitrarily large height for sigma_0 < 1 (Montgomery omega theorem, recalled, not opened). The boundary quantity is a sum over all zeros (Gonek Thm 3.1, trapezoid weight). The functional-equation term has modulus (t/2 pi)^(-d) at distance d from the line: for fixed d the device is the Hurwitz statement of Q19. Collisions: stage zeros leave the line only through double zeros, an event of the primes alone, invariant under torus rotation, with positive height-independent rate at fixed log X/log T (measured to T = 1e9, torus model to 1e20); the Rouche margin fails at a height-independent 0.1 to 1% of sampled points near the line and DH passes at comparable rates.
nodes.mapStatus: PROVED / CLASSICAL (refereed once, corrections E1-E7: the "any height" non-locality claim, the shifted form of Gonek Thm 5.1 and the approximate-functional-equation remark are ARGUED, not proved); collision law MEASURED (refereed once, two wording errors); one box at T = 1e6 certified in ball arithmetic, below verified height
