nodes.name: Fejer-weighted stage: positivity of the k = 0 term of the phase comb on every window
nodes.statement: For the Fejer weight (1 - log n/log Y)_+, F_Y'(t) = 2 log Y sum over zeros of Re kappa((rho - s) log Y) - 2 Re[Y^(1-s)/((1-s)^2 log Y)] + O(1/t), kappa(w) = (e^w - 1 - w)/w^2, s = 1/2 + it. On-line zeros contribute (1 - cos u)/u^2 >= 0. Positivity on every window is the Weil functional on the translated Fejer tests g * g~, g = e^(itx) 1_[0, log Y]: under RH F_Y' >= -2 sqrt(Y)/(t^2 log Y) - O(1/t) for Y up to a power of t; without RH it is the target in one-sided form (rows P10, P1; eq48). The classical explicit formula with kernel Y^z/(z^2 log Y); a rewriting, not new (referee E6). Addendum, campaign round 16 (`c16-ctheta-proposition5-power-sum`; detail in row Q30): with the stage coupled to height, Y = t^theta, the positivity statement reads only frequencies up to theta log t of the zero measure; its reach grows linearly with the local number of off-line pairs (PROVED given Turan, recalled; attained on synthetic sets, MEASURED) and lattice rows of spacing 2 pi/(theta log 2T) are invisible on the window (PROVED): not a zero-free region. Round 17: the reach statements of this row are assembled in row Q31 (window information law). Round 18: the second referee of that lane reported (holds with corrections), so the reach statements of this row are superseded by row Q31 as it now stands; the text here is kept as the record of rounds 15 and 16.
nodes.mapStatus: PROVED from the classical explicit formula (refereed once); checked to 1e-7 at low height and 6e-5 at T = 2.5e5; "without RH it is the target" rests on an ARGUED off-line estimate for one pair

nodes.name: Power-saving discrepancy of a completely multiplicative unimodular chi (sum_{n<=x} chi(n) = c x + O(x^theta), c != 0, theta < 1) as a source of a zero-free region for F = sum chi(n) n^-s (Helson follo
nodes.statement: Relative theorem: H = F F*/zeta^2 = exp(-2A) on Re s > 1, A a Dirichlet series with coefficients (1 - Re chi(p)^k)/k >= 0 on prime powers. With sigma_0 the largest real zero of F in (theta, 1) (theta if none), Landau's theorem gives convergence of A on Re s > sigma_0, hence ord_F(s) + ord_F(conj s) = 2 ord_zeta(s) there and sum_{p<=x} abs(1 - chi(p))^2 << x^(sigma_0+eps). A zero-free statement for F right of sigma_0 is the same statement for zeta: the implication is circular. If F has a real zero in (theta, 1) the abscissa of A equals sigma_0 exactly. The proof uses the Euler product with unimodular local parameters and never the additive spacing of the integers: it transfers to Beurling systems (F_B against zeta_B). Thin sign twists have a real zero at b with measured discrepancy exponent near b/2 (greedy sets, b = 0.5 to 0.9, x <= 1e8), so sigma_0 cannot be replaced by theta on the evidence. Second check and a complement (`c5-repair-engine-map-r4`; author and two referee passes): for sum_{d<=y} abs((chi * mu)(d)) << y^beta, beta < 1, one has sum_{3<=p<=X^(2(1-beta)/5)} abs(1 - chi(p))^2 <= (4 pi^2/abs(c)^2)(5 sup_{x<=X} abs(E(x))^2 + O(1)); hence the largest real zero b of F in (theta, 1) satisfies b(1 - b) <= 10 theta (nothing is proved for a smaller real zero below it), and a chi with E(x) << x^eps for every eps > 0 has no real zero in (0, 1) (r(0) = 0 for the exponent-zero class; zeros near 1 for small theta > 0 are not excluded).
nodes.mapStatus: Theorem 1 PROVED (author, one referee, and an independent second check: three passes); novelty not established: four generic searches and the text of Klurman-Mangerel-Pohoata-Teravainen (arXiv 1911.06265) contain no power-saving statement of this form; treated as a routine Landau argument. Complement PROVED (author; REFEREE.md and REFEREE2.md of `c5-repair-engine-map-r4`), numerically checked on sign twists and two complex chi. Thin-twist exponents MEASURED

nodes.name: Bandwidth 1 < alpha < 2 in the Gabor / inertia chain (row P27) through averaged Hardy-Littlewood
nodes.statement: F(alpha) <= C corresponds to abs((1/H) sum_{h<=H} (1 - h/H) E(h)) << X^(1/alpha) log X with H = X^(1-1/alpha): a power saving of exponent 1 - 1/alpha over the sieve bound. Proved in the literature: a saving of an arbitrary power of log X, for almost all shifts, for X^(8/33+eps) <= H <= X^(1-eps) (Matomaki-Radziwill-Tao, arXiv 1707.01315, abstract opened), i.e. alpha >= 33/25. Gap in the exponent: 1 - 1/alpha against 0; for 1 < alpha < 1.32 no averaged asymptotic is proved. Ramare's identity is not available for Lambda. The output would still be a proportion (P27 item 2).

nodes.name: Ramare factorisation of Dirichlet polynomials (Matomaki-Radziwill short intervals; averaged Chowla / Elliott) as a pointwise or every-window input
nodes.statement: Outputs are mean squares on Re s = 1 with savings of a power of log (Theorem 1 of arXiv 1501.04585: exceptional set of relative size (log h)^(-1/100) at tolerance (log h)^(-1/200)). The t-range is split into sets T_j where a prime polynomial is below e^(-alpha_j v/H_j), alpha_j = 1/4 - eta(1 + 1/(2j)) < 1/4, and a set U of large values. Large-value count (their Lemma 8, opened): for P(s) = sum_{P<=p<=2P} a_p p^-s, abs(a_p) <= 1, well-spaced t in [-T, T] with abs(P(1+it)) >= V^-1 number at most T^(2 log V/log P) V^2 exp(2 (log T/log P) log log T); at V = P^a this is T^(2a) P^(2a) up to the last factor. An isolated zero at sigma lies in the large-value set at threshold a = 1 - sigma at every scale (single-scale explicit formula, checked to 8e-7 for zeta); excluding it needs exponent <= 0, available 2(1 - sigma): gap 1 at sigma = 1/2, 1/4 at sigma = 7/8. The one sup bound in the method is Halasz with Vinogradov-Korobov (classical region). The conclusion class is closed under linear combination.
nodes.mapStatus: PROVED (count, single-scale formula; refereed once); Lemma 8, the sets T_j / U and Theorem 1 read from the ar5iv text; sharpness of the exponent 2a ARGUED; MEASURED checks

nodes.statement: D(1, n^(it); x)^2 = log log x - log abs(zeta(1 + 1/log x + it)) + O(1) moves by O_beta(1) for a zero with beta < 1; zero terms have relative size x^(beta-1) (1/log x in log averages) against tolerances at least (log x)^-A; the hypotheses are invariant under finite modification up to 2 sum_{p in S} 1/p and under n^(ia) rotation: tail type (round-3 lesson 5). The averaged Chowla / Elliott theorems hold for H -> infinity with o(H^k X) (arXiv 1503.05121, abstract opened; the two-function Elliott form is not in the abstract and is not needed for the DH pass).

nodes.name: Degree-2 positive forms with automorphic companions: log-level squares, products of log-level forms, coefficient squares sum abs(b(n))^2 n^-s (Ingham / Rankin-Selberg), pointwise outputs
nodes.statement: Log-level squares are linear in -L'/L (row P25; Fejer-Riesz: the zeta part is the classical cone). A product of two log-level forms has non-negative coefficients only if both factors are admissible linear forms up to a common sign (Lemma Q, with X the closure of the phase points and every point a limit of others, referee correction C2; with companions relative to a cited density statement). A coefficient square is non-negative for every sequence b and invariant under every unimodular twist of b (elementary); with DH coefficients it stays non-negative (exact, n <= 10^4). For b = lambda_Pi, tempered and unramified, it equals L(s, Pi x Pi~) H(s) with log H bounded on Re s >= 1, and its Landau abscissa is 1 - 2 min Re z_j for every zero configuration: the leading pole is met only by factors evaluated on Re s >= 1, so Landau on a coefficient square reaches Re s = 1 and no further. Multiplicativity enters only through the factorisation. Density (family) outputs not run: MV-CAP (P29) and the even-moment row apply. Not covered: quadratic objects that are not Dirichlet series (periods, triple products, theta lifts).
nodes.mapStatus: PROVED (Lemmas Q, H, Edge; Lemma U elementary; relative to classical non-vanishing on Re s = 1); coefficients MEASURED exactly; refereed once (five corrections, none changes the verdict)

nodes.statement: Strict form (no main term at q > 1), any theta < 1, under limsup abs(S(x))/x > 0: chi(n) = n^(-i alpha) (the sum over a mod p of the twists equals p chi(p) S(x/p)); an identification, and the hypothesis is then classical with theta = 0+. In the branch S(x) = o(x) (Liouville and relatives) the strict form is not an identification: it is equivalent to the strip statement for all L(s, psi) and is closed by circularity (row P14). General form: THIN passes (error O(q x^(b+eps)); measured twisted exponents about 0.45 at b = 0.9 with a zero at 0.9, order of magnitude only). Zeros of sum chi psi(n) n^-s right of the q = 1 abscissa are those of L(s, psi) for real chi; for complex chi only the product statement of Theorem 1' holds (zeros of each factor are zeros of L(s, psi)). Greedy THIN at b = 0.9: discrepancy exponent 0.42 on x <= 4e10.

nodes.name: Unit spectral window with non-negative central values and a long Moebius polynomial (lead 4), and its reopening by spectral reciprocity over signed moduli
nodes.statement: Window positivity (L(1/2, phi_j) >= 0, Katok-Sarnak) isolates the Eisenstein member, and an off-line zero would force S(T, X) large if the mollifier length X = T^A had A > 1 (detector P2: ARGUED, not proved; no region of convergence in t for a comparison). The long-polynomial off-diagonal needs Moebius cancellation against characters of conductor at least the length, summed with signs over the moduli: coefficient-blind tools give A = 1/2 (A = 1 under Lindelof for the family, or with GRH for Dirichlet L-functions termwise), so the output abscissa 1/2 + 1/(2A) is >= 1 (`n4-spectral-window-moebius`, unrefereed ledger). Round 10: the exact reciprocity dual of sum_c S(n, l; c)/c (Poisson in n, additive reciprocity, Poisson in the modulus; Lemma R, CLASSICAL, re-derived, checked to 1e-13) is a coprime-lattice sum over (m, c) whose second dual is a Kloosterman sum to the moduli m. Both steps act on (n, c); the twist l, which carries A, is a parameter and is not moved: ledger map A -> A, dual side T^(2A-1) terms per l against T (equal at A = 1, longer beyond). The statement "the composite is the functional equation of L(s, phi_j)" is supported by matching of ranges only (referee C3). Variants with a second family on the dual side (Motohashi type cubic weight; Blomer-Khan level reciprocity; Humphries-Khan, Kwan) are a ledger over RECALLED formulas, not derived: lengths (T, X^2) -> (T, X^2) or a dual family of size >= X^2; known range A <= 1/4 for the long-window mollified fourth moment (recalled). No A > 1/2 obtained. Reopen only with a reciprocity that acts on the Moebius variable l (lane `c11-rs1-twist-modulus-reciprocity`).

nodes.name: de Branges shift positivity (entire-function form with structure function xi(1/2 + a - iz) and shift 2a; weight form with any (a, h); bridge-symbol weight; conductor family)
nodes.statement: The condition implies a zero-free statement and a phase-balance condition at scale h at every zero (Conrey-Li Theorems 1, 2, opened by the lane and its referee): Delta_h in [-pi/2, pi/2] mod 2 pi in the entire-function form; Delta_h = 0 in the weight form (boundary expansion at a zero). False for zeta: zero 34 at h = 1 (-5.389e-69, reproduced); Re{xi(s)/xi(s + 1)} = -0.000131957 at 1 + 282i (reproduced three times); weight form fails next to the first zero for h = 1, 0.25, 0.1. The two-parameter weight family is false for every conclusion half-plane sigma_0 <= 1, relative to Bohr 1916, Satz A (opened by the second referee: log zeta on a fixed line 1/2 < sigma_0 <= 1 is dense, with the branch continued from the right). Variants V1a = row T3 and V2 = row G6 are restatements. The converse directions ("equals") are not established. No step uses the Euler product. Not established: failure for every fixed h < 1 in the entire-function form. Correction of "none found below 1e4 for h <= 0.5" (`c12-control-battery-harness`, ball-certified signs over all 1517 zeros below 2000): (N2_h) fails at h = 1/2 at zeros 922, 996, 1308, 1496 (q = -0.054, -0.122, -0.041, -0.278); none at h = 0.1, 0.25 (least q_0.25 = 0.132); DH on its 1861 on-line zeros below 2000 fails at h = 1/2 eleven times and at h = 0.1 once (zero 1249, t = 1400.5328). Corrected record of the screen (`c13-repair-map-engine-battery-records/records_corrected/screen.corrected.json`, 320-bit balls, ordinates with certified sign changes): the lane's DH and gamma-only windows were computed at unconverged ordinates (mpmath root finder stopping on absolute size); 31 of 54 recorded minima change (by at most 1.3e-2), the zeta windows and every DH fail count are unchanged, and the two recorded failure counts of the gamma-only fake at h = 2 (12 of 32 near 1000, 31 of 35 near 1e4) become 0 (least q_2 = 0.0043 and 0.00045: positive, tending to the boundary value 0). nodes.name: Height-uniform pointwise or windowed inequality in the values of finitely many Dirichlet L-functions in 1/2 < Re s < 1, as a step claimed to carry arithmetic (filter UNIV)
nodes.statement: Relative to joint (and hybrid) universality: a sup-norm-closed condition with height-independent constants on a fixed compact window with connected complement, holding outside a set of heights of upper density zero, holds for every non-vanishing analytic tuple on the window (Lemma U1); a continuous inequality in finitely many values and derivatives at fixed offsets then holds on the whole jet space (no content). Three classes: T (true for every analytic tuple), N (true for every non-vanishing tuple; automatic on zero-free windows and able to fail only on a window containing a zero; the sentence "equal in content to a zero statement" holds in that sense only, referee E2), F (false on a set of heights of positive lower density). Linear combinations of two or more of the L-functions with non-vanishing Dirichlet-polynomial coefficients have at least cT zeros in every sub-strip (Kaczorowski-Kulas, as printed in the survey). Not covered: Re s <= 1/2; Re s > 1 (control U); statements non-local in height (t with 2t, positive-definiteness in t, mean values, sums over zeros); families growing with T and the conductor aspect; inequalities using s together with 1 - conj s or the completed function; height-dependent constants or regions; existence in short intervals; companions that are not Dirichlet L-functions. Not numerically checkable (heights not located; a sample to height 8000 shows 58 of 256 sign patterns). Against 34 device rows: decides 1 (device 7, a restatement by Bagchi), part of 4 (1, 4, 14, 25), restates 2 (12, 32), out of scope for 27.

nodes.name: Pre-filter for T-NR (Lemma P) and census of inequality types not preserved by cone endomorphisms, as candidates for a step that fails both T-NR and E_a (campaign round 13; combine)
nodes.statement: Lemma P (section 2 note): T-NR with c > 0 passes every device whose hypotheses are linear identities or linear-class memberships, dilation-invariant cone conditions on objects linear in F, and conditions away from p0; exclusions X1 to X5. Use rule (restriction 3): all hypotheses of a device are typed in one normalisation (the Laurent form or the D form of the multiplier) before the lemma is applied. Scope restrictions needed for 0 disagreements with the record: the log level, c < 0 and mollified mean values are outside. Lemma L: for c > 0 the weight sequence (p0^(-1/2), c, p0^(1/2)) of T-NR is totally positive iff c >= 2 (zeros off the line iff c > 2; referee R-4); by Cauchy-Binet T-NR with c >= 2 inherits the sign of every minor of a dilation matrix of zeta's kernel with row nodes on one p0^2-lattice, given constant sign of zeta's minors on that lattice (MEASURED at orders 2 to 5, not proved). Lemma E: the xi-kernel of E_a is the convolution of Phi e^(au) and Phi e^(-au) and inherits every Polya-frequency order of Phi. Both lemmas are applications of classical theorems (Aissen-Schoenberg-Whitney-Edrei; Schoenberg, Karlin), not new (R-5). Census of twelve non-cone types (determinantal, hyperbolicity, norm equalities, entropy and others), each with the T-NR and E_a verdict at a named step: no entry fails both controls at a step that is an unconditional property of zeta, reads the functional equation and is not passed by another control. Where both fail the condition is a consequence of the target for zeta (Laguerre expression on the line, all-order criteria), or the size of local parameters (empty for zeta, no functional equation), or order-4 minors of the theta kernel with its constant term on generic nodes, where theta^w passes for w = 1/3, 1/2, 3 (and fails from w = 3.5; R-2), zeta's sign is measured and differs from that of primitive characters, and the T-NR failure is rare outside p0 = 2, 3 (R-3). T-NR and E_a are separated by complementary kernels: xi-kernel translation determinants cannot fail E_a; theta-kernel conditions of orders 1 and 2 with the constant term cannot fail T-NR. Not covered: 23 device types with no T-NR record by name; functionals of two objects.

nodes.name: Lemma POS-FE: zeta's functional equation, the pole clause and a non-negative coefficient measure (cell U2-POS of the checkpoint; campaign round 16; deepen)
nodes.statement: Theorem P: if G(s) = integral over [1, inf) of x^(-s) dN(x) in some half-plane with N a non-negative measure, (s - 1) G(s) is entire of finite order and G has zeta's functional equation, then G = r zeta, r the residue at 1. POS-FE (the same conclusion from nu >= 0 for -G'/G) follows, since nu >= 0 implies N >= 0. Decisive step: the trace identity integral of abs(phihat)^2 dN = (r/2)(norm(phi)^2 - abs(integral phi)^2), from the theta relation, proved for smooth phi supported in the open interval (-1/2, 1/2) and used with Fatou (referee E3); it places N on the zeros of the sinc function, the positive integers. This is Poisson-summation rigidity: the equality case of the one-dimensional linear-programming bound (test function with transform sinc^2) applied to the self-dual measure of G. The proof uses no multiplicativity and no Euler product. Necessity is shown for three clauses, each by a member G = zeta m on file with zeros off the line: N signed (ZQ, SG); coefficient mass below frequency 1 (T-NR in symmetric form); extra poles (G_+ of the c15 referee). Necessity of the finite-order clause is not addressed (E3 of the logic referee). So U2-POS is an identification class, a cell of U3: {zeta's functional equation, pole at 1 only, finite order, N >= 0 on [1, inf)}, which contains {FE, pole, Lambda_G >= 0}. It is not a statement about zeros. The registered quantitative form ("nu >= -eps mu forces every zero within f(eps) of the line, f -> 0") implies RH when applied to G = zeta: target-level. For signed members the proof gives an exact balance law (Proposition T) about coefficient mass. Server screen (MEASURED, float64): with one off-line quartet forced at integer multiplicity the mixed-integer incumbent is the two-zero swap ZQ in 40 of 40 cells, which are 35 distinct programs; it is an incumbent on the listed columns, not an optimum of the family (shifting neighbouring zeros lowers the defect by 2.5 to 3.5 percent in 5 of 5 cells tried by a referee). Fully fractional relaxations fall like 1/K and carry no information. Not surviving: the remark on Hecke's groups G(lambda), lambda > 2 (frequency inverted; not used by Theorem P).
nodes.mapStatus: PROVED (Theorem P; three referee files hold); CLASSICAL in content (uniqueness of the Dirac comb among non-negative self-dual measures with no mass in 0 < abs x < 1; Bochner's relation; sources recalled, not opened), new to the campaign record only; MEASURED (screen, float64, column-restricted)
nodes.defeatedBy: identification: no control lies in the class (members with off-line zeros exist only when a clause is relaxed; they are named in the previous cells). The registered quantitative form is not obtained (it would imply RH)

nodes.name: Cell U3 read as an inequality: a quantitative identification 'defect delta in one clause of the identification class {zeta's functional equation, pole at 1 only, integer frequencies, N >= 0} forces ev
nodes.statement: Target-level in all three directions: any inequality 'zeros within f(defect), f(0) = 0' on a class that contains zeta at defect 0 is the Riemann hypothesis at defect 0 (Proposition TL, one line). What is provable without the target is stability of the identification, which reads the functional equation and integrality, not multiplicativity. (a) Defect term of Theorem P: for a signed member with the exact functional equation, integral over [1, inf) of sinc^2 dN_off = 0, and N_off >= -eps' dx gives integral of sinc^2 dN_off^+ <= 0.0485883 eps'; the step is Lipschitz in the defect, with no square root (PROVED). (b) Proposition W (PROVED): zeta(s)(q^(s-1/2) + c + q^(1/2-s))/(2 + c), q = 1 + delta, c = q^b + q^(-b), has zeta's functional equation exactly, the pole at 1 only, a non-negative coefficient measure with atoms within delta of log n, and zeros on Re s = 1/2 +- b at heights (2k+1) pi/log(1 + delta), for every b > 0 and every delta > 0; it violates only the support clause of Theorem P (atom at 1/q). So frequencies within delta give no reach f(delta) -> 0; inside a window abs(t) <= T the member needs delta >= about pi/T. (c) Weights multiplicative up to delta with integer frequencies and the exact functional equation: the class is {r zeta} (Hamburger; relative to Statement O), so the relaxation is empty. (d) Lemma LR (PROVED): the zeros of conj(z) q^(s-1/2) + c + z q^(1/2-s) lie on Re s = 1/2 +- arccosh(abs(c)/2)/log q for every unimodular z, so a bound abs(alpha) <= q^(1/2+delta) on the local root is the statement that the factor's own zeros lie within delta of the line. NR-q note: NR-q is multiplicative on its own semigroup (generated by the rational primes, q and q^(-1); 'Euler product' in the generalised sense only, the factor at q is a polynomial in q^(-s)), so no functional excludes it through multiplicativity; it fails through integrality (frequencies log n + j log q) and the size of the local root; only the lift z = +-1 has the exact functional equation and real coefficients (referee E4). (e) Functional equation up to delta, integer frequencies (MEASURED, float64, symmetrised model functional, N on integers up to X = 300 to 4000, nine pairs below height 131): the smallest defect that admits a model quartet is at least 0.047, grows by kappa eta^2 (kappa 0.24 to 0.51) for eta <= 0.2, and is the same with and without multiplicativity on coprime pairs up to a factor 1.0004 to 1.23, the larger factors partly a bound effect (referee E2: the lane's ratio column up to 1.40 measures multiplicativity plus bounds); the dependence of the threshold on the gap d is not established (E3). The square-root law (distance eta against defect) belongs to the mechanism 'pair born on the line at a double zero' (ZQ; reality on the line), not to the arrival from large height of Proposition W (E1); 'reach 0 at delta <= 1e-2' holds in the symmetrised model only: for the true continuation the shift n^alpha gives zeros at distance alpha at defect 1.14 alpha to 1.42 alpha in both classes (E5). Phi_1 >= c sqrt(eps) on ZQ is ARGUED (MEASURED 0.077 to 0.086 on 8 members). Not done: the unconstrained LP at X = 4000 (a bracket only). State of the cell: U3 as an inequality is closed as target-level; multiplicativity enters no proved step.
nodes.mapStatus: PROVED (defect term with the constant 0.0485883; Proposition W; Lemma LR; Proposition TL; each re-derived by the referee); RELATIVE to Statement O (direction (c)); MEASURED (float64, symmetrised model; no certificate); ARGUED (Phi_1 lower bound); two referee passes, both hold with corrections (first: E1 to E5; second, `REFEREE2.md` by `c18-referee-r17-independent-sources`, scope Proposition W, Lemma LR, kappa_0 = 1/2 - Si(2 pi)/pi = 0.0485883332: wording corrections W1 (the factor at q is a polynomial local factor with a unit shift, not an inverse local factor) and W2 (the clusters {n/q, n, nq} overlap as point sets once n >= 1/delta, so 'the same total weight in every cluster' holds for the labelled decomposition only and cannot be read from the measure N alone); Lemma S6 relative to the self-duality step of c16 Proposition T for signed N; Lemma R, Phi_1, Phi_2 and the server LP not re-derived by the second pass), no verdict change

nodes.name: One-sided bound N(theta) on the band operator T_Z for 1/2 < theta' = u/log(t/2 pi) <= 1, completed by the reflected half of the approximate functional equation (campaign round 18; combine and heavy co
nodes.statement: Exact first lemma (Theorem A; PROVED, classical in content: the explicit formula of the exponential polynomial D_P composed with the fact that truncated shifts kill every term n >= P): for a_1 = 1, a_P != 0, D_P(s) = sum over n <= P of a_n n^-s, u = log P, h in H^1_0[0, u]: -2 Re <h, A_P h> = -u norm(h)^2 + sum over zeros beta of D_P of the forms with kernel e^((beta - 1/2) abs(xi)) (left zeros positive, right zeros indefinite), truncation tail (u - 2 log abs(a_P))/(pi T) norm(h)^2 (1 + o(1)); the mean of Re beta is log abs(a_P)/u (second referee). The constant is -u for every a_P != 0 (D_P'/D_P(s) = -(log P)/2 + lim sum over abs(Im beta) < T of 1/(s - beta), with no further constant): the term log abs(a_P) printed in display (A) of the lane is spurious (referee E1; hand check on 1 + a 2^-s; residuals 1.0986, 1.3863, 0.6931, 0.6931 = log abs(a_P) with the printed constant on four series with a_P != 1; for DH the cut P must not be a multiple of 5). The identity holds for every Dirichlet series with a_1 = 1, multiplicative or not: N(theta) is a statement about the zeros of the partial sum D_P at P = (t/2 pi)^theta'. Pole term at most 2 u P^(1/2) abs(1/2 + it)^(-2k) norm(h_0^(k))^2. The reflected half has frequencies >= u and is not seen by a band-u form (classical: compact support of the test; the lane's frequency sentence is ARGUED, E3). Explicit completions: the zero measure (positive when the zeros in the window are real: the target in the window) or a phase symbol of a splitting (needs Hermite-Biehler; false for D_P: 27 to 35 percent of its zeros lie right of the line at P <= 8, height <= 300, complete lists by winding number, E6; 31 to 33 percent at P = 12 and 37 to 41 percent at P = 20 with certified complete lists, heights to 2400, second referee). Proposition Z (PROVED in the lattice model only, E7): ZQ passes the band-u device for theta' < 1 at M = 0 whenever mu(eta, u) <= Lg (1 - theta' - sin(pi theta')/pi), a sufficient bound and not the threshold (in the model the lowest eigenvalue closes about linearly, 2 Lg (1 - theta'), and ZQ passes for eta about ten times the root of the bound at theta' = 0.9; E4); the model has no margin at theta' = 1. Server lane (MEASURED; signs certified relative to a hand-derived radius; 96 Fourier modes; heights 1e6 to 1e12, 40 windows; 44,600 cells, 229 undecided): (c) the registered linear reflected completion (atoms n -> t/(2 pi n), weights Lambda(n)(Lg - log n)/(sqrt(n) log n)) is not a positive extension of zeta's data: zeta fails it in 600 of 600 cells, and at 3e6 for every global phase of the reflected part (referee, float64); the reflected atoms have shifts above u/2, so their operator is nilpotent of order 2 and its Hermitian part is indefinite (ARGUED in the lane, confirmed by the referee). (b) N(theta) on 96 modes: zeta positive in 640 of 640 cells at theta <= 0.85 (margins down to 0.004 Lg) and 0 within the radius at theta >= 0.95; ZQ with eta = 0.05 passes at M = 1 up to theta = 0.75; E_0.1 and DH pass at low theta; multiplicative sign chains pass at theta = 0.55 in a typical 96-mode window and fail in 94 to 98 percent of cells at theta >= 0.95. The passes of the chains and zeta's margins are properties of 96 modes (referee E1, E3): at theta = 0.65 the chain pass rate falls from 99 to 57 percent at M = 1 and from 79 to 1 percent at M = 0 between 96 and 1536 modes while zeta stays positive (float64); the mode-count dependence of ZQ, E_0.1 and DH was not tested. Liouville carries no information separate from zeta (its form is 2 Lg minus zeta's upper frame bound). Reading: below the Nyquist band N(theta) is an open condition that ZQ satisfies (no R3) and a statement about zeros of a partial sum (no R1); at theta' = 1 it is the target in a window (no R4); the linear reflected completion is not a positive extension. Second referee of the server lane (30-cell independent rerun at 48, 96 and 192 modes; sentences 10 to 14 of `campaign/CORRECTIONS_R18.md`): zeta's smallest eigenvalue on 96 modes has median 0.22 to 0.26 Lg at theta = 0.55 and 0.012 to 0.025 Lg at 0.85; on 192 modes with the same centres it is 0.28 to 1.0 times the 96-mode value (median 0.75): the margin is a property of the window space and decreases with the number of modes. Form C: zeta fails at M = 0 and M = 1 in 600 of 600 cells with a reflected atom on 96 modes; in the rerun the smallest eigenvalue is negative at 48, 96 and 192 modes in every cell, between -1.42 and -0.19 times Lg, more negative with more modes; at (1e6, 0.85) 40 of 40 at 96 modes, and at 192 modes one of two sampled windows is negative at M = 0. At (1e10, 0.75) the boundary integer 31622777 is prime and is included; it changes lam_min of Form C by up to 1.4e-3 and no sign. Addendum, campaign round 19 (`c19-rs-real-zero-completion-band-server`; heavy server lane; one referee: does not hold as written, holds after E1 to E4; the obstruction verdict stands): the one continuation on file was run. Completion measure sigma = unit masses at the sign changes of the Riemann-Siegel main sum in the window plus (Arch density minus its chord). **Lemma P as repaired by the referee (E1):** the lemma (for sigma >= 0, <h, T_sigma h> = int abs(g)^2 d sigma >= 0, and Q_D = T_sigma + E) is correct under its hypothesis, but the constructed sigma is a signed measure: the Arch density rho(x) = (Re psi(1/4 + ix/2) - log pi)/(2 pi) is negative for abs(x) < 6.2898 (rho(0) = -0.8550; negative mass 2.2479), so 'T_sigma >= 0 on every band' and 'sigma >= 0 for every point set' are false (counterexample U = 10, h = sin(pi s/10): <h, T_sigma h> < -4.5 norm(h)^2). Repaired statement: T_sigma >= -2.248 sup over abs(x) <= 6.29 of abs(g(x))^2; on m Fourier modes centred at t_w this is at most 2.248 * 4m/(u t_w^2) (3e-10 absolute, 3e-11 Lg, at 1e6 with m = 384), and the runs enclose lambda_min(T_sigma) >= 2.4e-6 Lg in every zeta cell (2.4e-6, 2.3e-3, 4.5e-3 Lg at the three heights), so no number and no control verdict changes. The statement holds on the mode spaces m = 96, 192, 384, not on every band. MEASURED (prime side, signs relative to a hand-derived radius; 1e6, 1e9, 1e12; 8 windows; theta = 0.75, 0.80, 0.85; 216 zeta cells): zeta's defect -lambda_min(E)/Lg is 0.036 to 0.137, 0.008 to 0.020, 0.0016 to 0.0052; scaled by (t/2 pi)^(1/4) the medians over m are 1.3 to 2.1 and the cells 0.7 to 3.3 (E2); at most 5e-4 Lg with the first correction term C0. The one-sided statistic changes under a ZQ exchange only by the pair form, of size at most mu = u (sinh(u eta)/(u eta) - 1) (PROVED, row Q31 source lane, re-derived), so at tolerance tau Lg it cannot exclude an off-line pair with (u eta)^2 below about 6 tau Lg/u, a set that is non-empty for every tau > 0 at every height; at the registered tolerance 0.05 this includes eta = 0.01 at 1e9 and 1e12, not at heights above about 1e31 and not at the C0 tolerance, and at 1e12 the defect of ZQ at eta = 0.01 is 1.5 to 4.2 times zeta's (E3: 'ZQ has the same defect as zeta' is false there). Exchange threshold eta* > 0 in 432 of 432 cells (422 certified in balls, E4). Chains, Liouville, DH (1e6, 1e9), E_a, T-NR, HQ2 fail by missing functional equation, zero or pole location, or size; no step reads multiplicativity. Registered outcome (b): the completion gives only N(theta) with tolerance; the two-sided version is the target in the window (ARGUED). State: device type closed (`engine/curated/devices.json`): three refereed lanes of the device type (`c18-tz-one-sided-bound-fe-reserve-bridge` and `c18-tz-band-completion-controls-server`, two referee files each; `c19-rs-real-zero-completion-band-server`, one), 'four refereed lanes' in `ROUND_LOG.md` round 19, which does not name its lanes (the fourth is presumably the window-law lane `c17-window-information-law-ctheta-u5` behind row Q31) (referee E1 of the record lane: the device entry names three lanes); no continuation on file.

nodes.statement: Theorem R: for real eta != 0 with sum abs(eta(n)) n^{-1/2} < inf, L - sum eta(n) n^{-1/2-z} has a non-PSD finite Pick matrix on every interval. All-order positivity has zero tolerance in each prime weight, so no property stable under Lambda -> Lambda + eta implies it. It identifies the function and does not locate zeros.

nodes.statement: Q(e^{-zt}) = Re L(z)/Re z; Q >= 0 on Re z >= c iff no zeros with Re s > 1/2 + c. An off-line pair gives a negative value only inside the disk of radius delta about its foot. Positivity region = zero-free region.

nodes.name: Prime chain as sections; sectionwise passivity
nodes.statement: S = T_{M(alpha G) prod_p M(-alpha u_p)}[1] for Re s > 1; a section is J-contractive iff Re Z >= 0. Summed J-defect is bounded iff Re s > 1 and square-summable on the Bohr torus iff Re s > 1/2, variance 1/(8x^2) + O(1) at Re s = 1/2 + x: the gap between the l^1 and l^2 thresholds of (p^{-sigma} log p). nodes.name: Splitting L into positive-real prime pieces; single-delay and multi-delay section extraction
nodes.statement: If L - sum_p h_p is positive-real with prime-periodic h_p, every h_p is an imaginary constant. No Blaschke-Potapov single-delay factor at interior or boundary nodes. Multi-delay, finite P: for H holomorphic with Re H >= 0 on the polydisc and h = H((p^{-z})_p) lossless, sum over poles gamma_j <= T of r_j zeta(1/2 + i gamma_j) = (T/2 pi)(H(0) + conj h(1/2)) + O(T^{1/2+eps}), real part at least (T/2 pi) Re H(0); so if L - h is positive-real then h is an imaginary constant (hypothesis implies RH; proof does not assume it). No bounded multi-delay factor divides S. Round 2 (`c2-jinner-multidelay-lft`, Theorem A' refereed twice): for every positive-real Dirichlet series h = H((p^{-z})_p) of Bohr-lift type with atomic boundary measure, any prime set, sum_{gamma_j > t_0} r_j zeta(1/2 + i gamma_j) e^{-delta gamma_j} = (a_1 + conj h(1/2))/(2 pi delta) + O(delta^{-1/2-eps}), Re(a_1 + conj h(1/2)) >= (4 - 2 sqrt 2) Re a_1; so the non-unipotent normalisation and infinite P give no section (row Q22). DH analogue: the same formula with bracket a_1 + c_1 conj H(w') + c_2 conj H(w''), w'_p = conj chi(p) p^{-1/2}, real part >= 1.0597 Re a_1 (conductor-5 derivation written line by line in the second referee pass; main and second-order terms checked in ball arithmetic for zeta and DH, remainder bounded as delta -> 0). The first-moment no-go therefore holds for DH and does not use multiplicativity; the earlier sentence "multiplicativity is used at the point evaluation" is withdrawn. CLOSED 2026-11-18 for sections holomorphic on the full polydisc with Schur termination or termination depending on the other primes. Not covered (no lane): boundary nodes of R_a for a >= 1/2; sections on a Reinhardt shell; sections containing the gamma term. The last two were treated in round 7: rows Q23 (shell) and Q24 (gamma-coupled).

nodes.name: Lee-Yang stages to a Krein-space limit (rank Gamma_- semicontinuity)
nodes.statement: Rank Gamma_- is lower semicontinuous under bounded weak-* convergence. In the self-dual conductor normalisation every stage symbol is inner and tends to -1 on Re z > 0, for zeta and every unimodular twist: the chain carries no information. With gamma factor and pole renormalisation, zero-free in Re s > theta iff the stages are locally bounded on {Re s > theta, s != 1} (Hurwitz + von Koch; no novelty). The Lee-Yang inequality gives a stage bound with exponent of order P, weaker than trivial.

nodes.name: Global trace identities

nodes.name: Heat-monotone functionals of the anticausal Hankel block or of zero configurations
nodes.statement: No unitarily invariant norm of Gamma_-(t) is monotone in t (through the one-pair collision; 50-digit witnesses between collisions). The sum of Re p over right-half-plane zeros of D_t = F_t + alpha F_t' is continuous and strictly decreasing while positive. A non-negative functional vanishing on axis configurations and monotone along the flow is non-increasing, so it bounds t = 0 only by values at t < 0, where the conclusion is false.

nodes.name: Rotation-invariant stage tools as a size bound for Euler stages (polydisc stability, multi-affine Lee-Yang property, Grace-Walsh-Szego, Asano contraction, Borcea-Branden closure, Ruelle radius)
nodes.statement: Sharp bound from stability on a polydisc of polyradius (R_p): prod (1 - abs(z_p)/R_p)^{d_p} <= abs(F(z)) <= prod (1 + abs(z_p)/R_p)^{d_p}, attained in the class. For the Euler stage this is abs(E_P(s)) <= E_P(sigma), the trivial bound with its exact constant; with the Lee-Yang radius p^{-1/2} the bound is weaker than trivial by a power of P. A bound that may depend on the point but must hold for every member of a class closed under torus rotations is at least the maximum over the torus; a unimodular twist is a torus rotation. For zeta with the pole renormaliser, sup over t of abs(G_P(sigma + it)) >= E_P(sigma) for every P and 0 < sigma < 1: height-uniform and below-trivial cannot both hold at fixed P. At fixed P the stage of U is a limit of height translates of zeta's stage (Bohr). Remaining: a bound at fixed t with P growing, or P coupled to height, which is c1 Thm. D(b) (row Q19), equivalent to the zero-free statement.
nodes.mapStatus: PROVED (refereed once, statement of Thm. 2 corrected to the pointwise form; content classical: Bohr, Kronecker, Dirichlet); table MEASURED
nodes.defeatedBy: U (same class member up to rotation); every control with product stages (TW+, TW-, EA); DH, HEAT by citation

nodes.name: J-contractive linear-fractional sections of the prime chain in several delays (non-unipotent normalisation Theta(0) = M(c_0) U_0; infinite prime sets)
nodes.statement: A holomorphic J-contractive matrix function of the delays on the full polydisc (finite P, or D^inf intersected with c_0) whose image discs reach -1 along x -> +infinity is M(H(w)) V_0 with V_0 constant J-unitary and Re H >= 0: the joint defect is rank one and additive, rank 2 does not occur (maximum principle for the Potapov-Ginzburg transform; uses only S(x) -> -1, the gamma growth; holds for every control with a gamma factor). With Theorem A' (row Q12): if S = T_Theta[S_1] on Re z > 0 with S_1 Schur, Theta is a constant J-unitary matrix. Limit step: sharp sections converge on 1/2 < sigma < 1 in L^2 of the Bohr torus and almost everywhere, not at zeta's orbit point, and J-contractivity is not closed there; tapered sections converge locally uniformly on Re s > theta iff they are locally bounded iff no zeros with Re s > theta. Not covered: sections holomorphic only on a Reinhardt shell around the tori; sections containing the gamma term; J-expansive sections (for these the stage statement is equivalent to RH by removal of Euler factors). Both treated in round 7: rows Q23 (shell) and Q24 (gamma-coupled). Still not covered: P(t) growing like a power of t; J-expansive sections.

nodes.name: Sections of the prime chain holomorphic only on a Reinhardt shell around the tori (Laurent class; left open by Q12, Q22)
nodes.statement: For a positive-real lossless h whose boundary measure is the pullback of a positive measure mu on T^P carried by a hypersurface crossed by the orbit t -> (p^{-it}), the Bohr series of h runs over the half-space k . log p > 0, not the orthant, and the first moment of F over the poles is (2 int F_P dmu)/(2 pi delta) + O(delta^{-1/2-eps}), F_P the P-part of F on the torus (Lemma 1; in coefficients a_1 + conj((Pi_int h)(1/2)), Pi_int the projection onto integer frequencies). Proved for trigonometric-polynomial densities on a coordinate hyperplane; measured for Poisson densities. Sign rule: the real part is forced non-negative over the class iff Re F_P >= 0 on T^P; for zeta iff sum_{p in P} arcsin(p^{-1/2}) <= pi/2 (true for {2}, {2,3}, {2,3,p} with p >= 37; false for {2,3,7} and richer sets); for DH forced on {2,3} (min Re D_P = 0.0387) and not on {2,3,7} (min -0.62). So the Harnack sign of Theorem A' (polydisc) does not survive non-integral frequencies, for zeta and DH alike. Closure: if every pole is a zero of F, all twisted first moments vanish and mu = 0 (zeta: E_P has no zero on the torus; DH: relative to the unproved statement that the zero set of D_P has codimension 2). Limit step: in measure form the class is locally dense in all lossless positive-real functions (the statement "alpha L is a limit of sections" is RH restated); in formula form see Q24. Not covered: P growing like a power of t.
nodes.mapStatus: PROVED (Lemma 1, restricted class; one referee, independent run for zeta and DH); MEASURED (Poisson densities); Corollary 1 direction "sign forced" needs Lemma 1 for general measures; the constant-density case is a mean value of zeta on an arithmetic progression (literature not cited by the lane)

nodes.name: Sections containing the gamma one-port: poles at X_F(1/2 + it) m((p^{-it})_p) = 1, m unimodular on T^P (left open by Q22)
nodes.statement: Normalised first moment of F over the poles -> 1 + conj(int_{T^P} F_P m dHaar) (Lemma 2). Monomial m = c w^kappa (these are all unimodular trigonometric polynomials): the poles are shifted Gram-type points 2 theta(t) + t log q = a mod 2 pi, the mean is 1 + conj(c) n^{-1/2} if 1/q = n is an integer and 1 otherwise; proved for zeta by the Gram-point method (Riemann-Siegel formula and Kusmin-Landau), second referee. m = 1: Titchmarsh's mean 2. Holomorphic inner m: 1 + conj(m(0)) (first referee's correction of the lane's value), sign forced. m = -conj(F_P)/F_P (reflected Euler stage): 0. m = -conj(F_P)/abs(F_P): 1 - norm(F_P)_{L^1} < 0 when F_P has no zero on the torus (argued and measured: -0.298 / -0.340 for zeta on {2,3}, {2,3,7}; -0.168 for DH on {2,3}); for DH with three or more primes this m is not continuous. So no forced sign with the gamma term, for zeta or DH; this conclusion rests on a non-monomial m and is not proved. Closure by twists: a prime q outside P has twisted mean f_q q^{-1/2}, so every prime with f_q != 0 must lie in P, and inside the module of P the only candidate is the reflected stage (rows G10, Q10). Limit step in formula form: contractivity abs(U_P) < 1 of the reflected stage on a shell holds at height t only while log(t/2 pi) > 2 sum_{p <= P} log p/(sqrt p - 1); this is the height-coupled reserve bound Q*(t) of `g-passive-cascade` ({2,3} from t = 3590), not uniform in height.
nodes.mapStatus: PROVED for monomial m and zeta (second referee's proof, itself unrefereed); ARGUED + MEASURED otherwise (uniformity in k of the expansion sum U^k not established); Proposition 3 ARGUED

nodes.name: Anticausal Hankel block or Krein index of the bridge form summed over a twist family, with the 7/8 theorem as input
nodes.statement: The single-cutoff trace tr Gamma_-^* Gamma_- does not depend on c; the gapped block has weights e^{-(beta_j - 1/2)c} and its decay rate in c is twice the least real part of a pole. The prime-side value of every member block is zero before any family sum; a family sum with positive weights is a positive form in the off-line data of all members and equals the bridge form of the product prod F_chi^{c_chi}; its negative index is the number of distinct off-line zeros of the union. The 7/8 input bounds the pole farthest from the line (Re z < 3/8) with the same constant for one member and for the family: gain 0; the family sum reads the pole nearest the line. Every-window form: the tilted block vanishes at tilt >= 3/8 member by member (row G20 restated). Below 3/8 a family bound controls a member only when it is below one unit of the index (MV-CAP, row P23); for unimodular twists n^{-i alpha_k} the family sum is a sum over height translates of one member. A bridge formed from a single completed probe row: row Q26.

nodes.name: Bridge (spinor square-root) form built from one completed probe row B_m of the 7/8 mechanism (left open by Q25)
nodes.statement: One theta row is T_m = L0 D with L0 = L(3s - 1/2, psi). The row's functional equation has its reflection axis at Re s = 1/2, which is Re w = 1 for the Euler factor L0; the critical line of L0 is Re s = 1/3, at distance 1/6. Gamma_-(T_m) is blind to zeros of L0 (classical non-vanishing on Re w >= 1), apart from the poles of T and the pole of L0 at w = 1 when psi is principal. Zeros of L0 are poles of D (measured, five zeros) and are read by Gamma_-(D) at every height as an identity; about Re w = 1/2 the form is H(T) - H(D), with no sign. The target enters as an L-function only after the sum over rows (row Q25: family sums, gain 0). With Q25 the bridge / 7/8 junction has no open member.

nodes.name: Sum rule with positive terms on the prime stub chain, crossing from summable (Re s > 1) to square-summable (Re s > 1/2) coefficients: Szego-Verblunsky, Killip-Simon, Simon-Zlatos, H^2 point evaluation
nodes.statement: (i) Littlewood window functional: int_W log abs(F_P) = Phi_P(T) - Phi_P(T+H) for every unimodular chain and every sigma > 0 (Lemma 1); the coefficient side is 0 at every stage and the bound-state term B_W is a tail invariant (Lemma 3). It is Jensen's zero count: zeta at sigma = 0.3 on [10, 20] gives 0.2 = 1/2 - 0.3; DH at sigma = 0.7 on [82, 89] gives 0.1085171825, its off-line zero. (ii) Mean form: E + 4 pi delta = log zeta(2 sigma) with three non-negative terms; this is M_log = 4 pi delta (Littlewood) rewritten, the classical density identity. (iii) Any stage functional continuous in the phases has the same distribution over heights for zeta and for every unimodular twist (Kronecker-Weyl; row Q21). (iv) Difference condition of Simon-Zlatos type on the coefficients in delay order: holds for zeta on Re s > 0 and for THIN on Re s > b/2 with its zero at b (Lemma 5). It is a coefficient condition only (no theorem of this family is stated for a product over incommensurable delays) and is compatible with a zero right of the line; for random U the sum is infinite almost surely for sigma <= 1/2 (three-series step added by the referee). (v) H^2 of the infinite torus: point evaluation at depth delta has norm zeta(2 delta)^(1/2), so the step reaches Re s > sigma_0 + 1/2 only (Hedenmalm-Lindqvist-Seip; restated, row Q10). A positive-term sum rule gives "no bound states" only if its coefficient side vanishes, and then its limit step is the target. Closed for these five forms, not for every sum rule. Not covered: a sum rule whose coefficient side vanishes identically with a limit step semicontinuous in the direction "bound states of the limit <= liminf of the stages" (that limit step is the R4 statement); the semicontinuity remark of Lemma 3 is conditional on weak convergence of the stage weights, not established for 1/2 < sigma <= 1.

nodes.name: Regular-representation matrix series M_q(s) = sum R(n) n^-s over (Z/q)^* with the bridge square; cone R_+^G
nodes.statement: Every bridge object built from M_q with primitive completions lies in the commutative algebra C[G] tensor operators and is the direct sum over chi of the scalar bridge objects (Lemma S). The vector 1 is in the cone and is the chi_0 eigenvector, so every statement quantified over cone vectors restricts at v = 1 to a statement about the scalar zeta object in which G no longer appears; for copositivity (K) and positive definiteness in chi (E) that statement is H_c^zeta >= 0, which is RH (Lemma P). The uniform entry bound at threshold o(1/phi) is a restatement (Lemma Q). Entry positivity is character orthogonality at log level (rows P25, P50), holds for coefficients and kernels and ends in values at s = 1 (measured at q = 5, 7, 8); the functional-equation matrix W has negative entries. (E) fails on nodes at q = 5 and q = 8 in the stated normalisations and passes after rescaling one direction. Cone functionals include Hurwitz entries with zeros on both sides of the line. Wording of the first referee: "the cone can enter only as (K) or (E)" is an enumeration, not a theorem. Second referee: the E_a lift has functional equation with E^2 and a degree-two gamma factor; the T-NR lift has its zero in the strip only for c < p0^(1/2) + p0^(-1/2); no single control keeps log-level positivity and M_q's own functional equation, and that pair is an identification in degree one (rel. Kaczorowski-Perelli, opened). Not covered: a cone other than R_+^G; statements mixing several bridge objects.

nodes.name: Cone adapted to the functional-equation matrix: K_F = {v >= 0, Fv >= 0} on even functions on Z/q with the dilations as cone automorphisms; candidate (CW) (the cell "a cone other than R_+^G" left open
nodes.statement: Linear inequalities of K_F are the entrywise ones at x and 1/x (Lemma C). Every dilation-invariant pointed cone meets the dilation eigenvectors only in the trivial slice (Lemma P', with the one-line step supplied by the referee, E3); that a copositive form over such a cone contains the scalar zeta inequality with the cone inert is ARGUED. At q = 5 the F-fixed extreme rays give zeta(s)(1 + 5^(1/2-s)) +- L(s, chi_5): positive kernel, zeta's functional equation, at least cT zeros in every sub-strip (relative to the survey's Theorem 31) and measured zeros off the line (0.7796 + 61.1685i and five more below 120). The T-NR lift has every input of (CW) (kernel in K_F with the same F, coefficient matrices cone endomorphisms); its zeros are inside the strip only for 2 < c < 2.1213 at p_0 = 2 (the lane's 2.5 corrected, E1). The E_a lift fails only at the polar terms of the theta-normalised kernel (E*(i, 0.7) = -2.331). Automorphism at every prime is an input that no cone inequality consumes (cone inequalities are preserved by cone endomorphisms); projective contraction is void (two Perron vectors). No value-side cone in the open strip (row P54). Closed: candidate (CW) on K_F. Not covered: other F-adapted cones (non-polyhedral, or not containing v_+-).

nodes.statement: I(u) = residue sum over right-half-plane poles + remainder; RH iff abs(I(u)) <= sqrt(2 pi) Dl exp(-u^2 Dl^2/2) for all u < 0. The identity holds for any pole configuration. Measured ratio at u = -6: zeta 0.33, DH 1.2e7: zero detection at a height where zeros are known.

nodes.name: Sections of the prime chain with P = t^theta on the gamma one-port; J-expansive (sharp) sections (class U7 of the checkpoint; left open by rows Q22 to Q24; campaign round 15; deepen; R4 direct; the la
nodes.statement: Fejer-tapered section L_F = sum over zeros of K_u(s - rho), u = log P, Re K_u >= 0 on Re w >= 0: J-contractive on Re s > 1/2 + eta_0 for every P if and only if zeta has no zero there. The limit step from finite stages is sound (Harnack, Vitali), and the stage inequality at unbounded P is row P45 (the Weil functional on translated Fejer tests), the target. In content this is the Fejer-smoothed form of the known criterion Re xi'/xi > 0 on Re s > 1/2 (Hinkkanen 1997, Lagarias 1999; recalled, not opened): CLASSICAL in content, with a proof written in the lane (referee E5). Coupled to height, statement C(theta) (Re L_F(1/2 + it; t^theta) >= -M for t >= t_0) is implied by RH and is proved by the lane only for P up to about ((1/4) log t log log t)^2, a range in which every sign twist satisfies it; its band-bound consequence (Proposition 4: arbitrary coefficients, constant not explicit) is met by random sign chains. Windowed anticausal block: bounded by the tail in sup norm under absolute summability or a zero-free hypothesis; square-summability gives most windows only. Sharp sections are J-expansive for zeta on the line at theta >= 1/2 (MEASURED). Proposition 5 (zeros within c_theta/log gamma of the line from C(theta)) is ARGUED for a single off-line pair; its constant is of order-of-magnitude value only and is not recorded here (E4). Addendum, campaign round 16 (`c16-ctheta-proposition5-power-sum`, one independent referee pass, corrections E1 to E6; no statement about zeros of zeta): Proposition 5 is not a two-sided correspondence. C(theta) reads the off-line part of a zero set only through its local Fourier transform at frequencies up to theta log t. PROVED in window form (Theorem B as restricted by E1): for each T a lattice row of pairs with spacing 2 pi/(theta log 2T) contributes a constant on the window for every offset b <= 1/2, so it is invisible to every section with u <= theta log 2T (inside the Riemann-von Mangoldt density only for theta < 1/2; a row of fixed spacing does not satisfy the all-heights statement). PROVED given Turan's second main theorem (recalled, not opened; Lemma T): if the off-line pairs form one isolated cluster of n pairs, C(theta) gives b_max <= (c n + O(log log gamma))/(theta log gamma), linear in n. MEASURED (ball arithmetic on grids; synthetic point sets, not candidates for zeta): linear growth in n is attained; clusters of 3 to 40 quadruples added to zeta's ordinates at heights 1e6 to 1e9 pass with the deepest pair at 1.6 to 3.4 times the one-pair region for theta = 1. Reverse direction (Lemma R of that lane): the region gives C(theta') only with M replaced by C log^2 t on a synthetic class (E5). So the reach of a P = t^theta device is not a zero-free region of width c/log gamma; the all-heights form is measured, not proved. No step uses multiplicativity. The measured positivity for zeta (14 cells up to P = 1e8) is implied by verified height (E3: the lane's 1e-21 is per zero; summed over zeros above 3e12 the bound is below 1e-9). No proved step uses multiplicativity. Round 17: the reach statements of this row are assembled in row Q31 (window information law). Round 18: the second referee of that lane reported (holds with corrections), so the reach statements of this row are superseded by row Q31 as it now stands; the text here is kept as the record of rounds 15 and 16.

nodes.name: Window information law: what a height-coupled band-limited positivity device can read (tests of band u = log P, tolerance M, window of length L; classes U5 and U7; proposed in place of the reach state
nodes.statement: Frame (CLASSICAL: Weil's quadratic functional on tests g * g~ with g supported on an interval of length u; Weil 1952, Yoshida, Bombieri, Connes-Consani; the repository's Route I Toeplitz form; referee E6): every band-u positivity device is the quadratic form of one operator T_Z on L^2 of an interval of length u, tested on some set of vectors; the complete device with tolerance M is T_Z + 2M >= 0, read as a quadratic form on C_c^infinity of the interval (T_Z is unbounded when the local density grows like a logarithm; second referee, domain correction); statement C(theta) of row Q30 is the same form on modulated indicator functions. PROVED (re-derived by the referee): a cluster of n off-line pairs contributes exactly n negative directions; one pair against a tight on-line background alpha is invisible exactly up to sinh(ub)/(ub) = 1 + (alpha + 2M)/u (alpha = log(t/2 pi) for u <= log(t/2 pi)); in the lattice model above the Nyquist band u = log(t/2 pi) the exact device (M = 0) excludes every finite cluster, and with tolerance M one pair passes below the root of mu(b, u) = 2M and is excluded above the root of (sin^2 + sinh^2) mu(b, u - Lg) = 2M (order sqrt(M) u^(-3/2) for fixed theta' = u/Lg > 1 away from lattice points; the two bounds differ by an unbounded factor as theta' -> 1+ and at lattice points, referee E3); infinite rows of spacing <= 2 pi/u pass with any offset (Theorem 6, Poisson); for one cluster u b_max <= 5.85 n + logarithms (relative to Turan's second main theorem in the form of Montgomery-Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory III (draft), Theorem K.3: factor 2 and constant 8e as printed there, proof read by a referee; Montgomery's Ten Lectures, chapter 5, not opened). MEASURED (ball arithmetic, exact criterion; reproduced by the referee on new cases): tapered half-Nyquist rows pass up to u b_max = 0.445 n + 2.1 (n = 40 to 60; slope 0.44 per pair), shape-optimised clusters up to 1.7 n (n = 3); on zeta's ordinates near 1e6, 1e9, 1e12 the one-pair threshold is 0.90 to 0.99 of the lattice law at theta = 1/2; clusters placed on the ordinates do not grow with n in the two offset profiles tested (E7). Two structural bands: P = sqrt(t/2 pi) (count-preserving replacement: rows pass for theta' <= 1/2, PROVED; excluded at offsets tending to 0 above it, MEASURED with an ARGUED count) and P = t/2 pi (exactness: above it only the exact device M = 0 has full power, and that inequality is the target restricted to the window). Reading: the reach of a band-u device is not a zero-free region; no band u = theta log t gives a region shrinking faster than a power of log t. Lemma E (PROVED): the truncated Euler product identity holds exactly in the algebra of truncated shifts for every completely multiplicative chain, and no step uses it; sign chains have the factorisation. The input that would enlarge the unconditional band from a power of log t to a power of t is a one-sided operator bound N(theta) on T_Z for 1/2 < theta <= 1 tied to the functional-equation reserve (round 18: no such bound is on file after two lanes; row P58). NOT established (both referees): the density form W4 ('only when off-line pairs have local density of order u/2 pi over a length of order b_max') is ARGUED; its proved replacement is the count form W4c (relative to Turan): a single cluster of radius r that passes the Fejer-modulated sub-device has at least (u b_max - 1.2 log((M + 2 pi D')(r + 1/2)) - O(1))/5.85 pairs, and the one-pair regime needs no density. The sequence form W5 (infinitely many isolated pairs with b (log gamma)^(3/2) -> 0 pass) is ARGUED: the cited theorems treat one pair and 'u = theta log gamma' has a meaning only for a windowed device, for which no theorem is proved; its proved replacement at one band is W5c (second referee of the window lane; refereed once in round 19, `c19-referee-r18-independent-sources/REFEREE-W5c-and-TURAN-SOURCE.md`: holds with corrections; PROVED, the Plancherel-Polya step proved inline by the sub-mean-value property on disjoint discs): pairs x_j +- ib with equal offset b and abscissae separated by at least D (all abscissae carrying a pair, with multiplicity one); for every h in L^2 of an interval of length u (centred without loss, f being translation invariant), sum_j -[f(z_j) + f(conj z_j)] <= 4 pi C(u, D) sinh^2(ub/2) norm(h)^2 with C(u, D) = (2 e^2/pi) max(2/D, u/2); hence the family passes the complete band-u device with tolerance M against any on-line set when 4 pi C(u, D) sinh^2(ub/2) <= 2M, in particular for ub <= 1 and b <= 0.499 sqrt(M) u^(-3/2)/sqrt(max(1, 4/(uD))). One band, equal offsets. Remark K (Krein extension) holds for the unwindowed device only (the distribution form of Krein's theorem recalled, not opened); for the windowed N(theta) the equivalence with a positive completion is ARGUED, and N(theta) must be given a definition before use (N_all or a named sub-device N_K; `c18-referee-r17-independent-sources/GATE.md`). The DH and zeta(s+a) zeta(s-a) rows of the lane's control table as written do not stand (E1, E2; defeated-by cell). The constant 0.36 per window of row S12b was not matched to the count uL/2 pi.
nodes.mapStatus: PROVED (Theorems 1 to 6, Lemma P, Lemma E; uniform in the lattice model only; nothing is established for zeta at any band); PROVED relative to Turan's second main theorem in the form of Montgomery-Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory III (draft), Theorem K.3 (Corollary T'; the statement and the start of the proof read in the extracted text by the round-19 referee lane and by its referee; Turan's own text and Montgomery's Ten Lectures not opened); MEASURED (ball arithmetic; scale-free and on zeta's ordinates as synthetic sets); ARGUED (W4, W5, the count for W4'); two referee passes, both hold with corrections (first: E1 to E8; second: three labels to ARGUED (W4 density form, W5 second bullet, the Remark K sentence for the windowed N(theta)), two control rows rewritten, W4c and W5c supplied), no verdict change. Sources at secondary level only: Turan's second main theorem (constant 8e supported by van der Poorten; the factor 2 is printed by one of three secondary sources: without it 0.29 delta becomes 0.146 delta and 5.85 is unchanged; 'relative to' stays; round 19: the theorem with the factor 2 and the constant 8e is Theorem K.3 of Montgomery-Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory III (draft), found with proof; Corollary K.5 follows from K.4 with M = L; 2,000 random instances, no violation; Montgomery's Ten Lectures not opened; `c19-referee-r18-independent-sources`, one referee); Akhiezer's factorisation for Fejer-Riesz of exponential type (needed only for 'passes the complete device'); the explicit formula re-derived in the operator normalisation (signs correct; the pole-term bound e^(u/2)/t^2 is for indicator vectors only)
nodes.defeatedBy: zeta(s+a) zeta(s-a): in the lattice model the pairs gamma +- ia are a row of spacing 2 pi/Lg and pass the complete device with any offset a for every u <= Lg (first referee, E1; the lane's entry 'fails in a window' cites a measurement of another configuration). On its own configuration on zeta's ordinates at T = 1e6 (second referee; ball arithmetic, 512-bit, window model; reproduced by the referee of that pass with a Nystrom discretisation, float64): passes at every tested a <= 0.22 and fails at every tested a >= 0.24 at theta = 1/2, M = 0 (same bracket for window half-lengths 30 and 45; crossing near 0.229 to 0.231, float64); passes at a <= 0.02 and fails at a >= 0.05 at theta = 0.8, M = 0 (crossing between 0.04 and 0.05; the counts at theta = 0.8 include directions within 5 of the zeta / lattice junction). T-NR passes for P <= q. ZQ rows pass. DH: not run; not established (nothing bounds the number of its off-line zeros per window near the line); outcome through zero location only (E2; second referee). Sign chains and every completely multiplicative chain have the factorisation (Lemma E) and are not separated by any step; they fail N(theta) at theta >= 1 (MEASURED in the round-15 and round-16 lanes). Target: the exact device above the Nyquist band

nodes.name: Prime side by Cayley expansion
nodes.statement: S = -1 + 2 sum_m alpha^m P^m/(1 + alpha G)^{m+1} in Re z > sigma_0(alpha); its transform is supported on u >= 0, so the prime-side anticausal kernel is identically zero, for every sign twist. The two sides share no hypothesis; their difference is the residue sum. sigma_0 <= 0.78, 1.26, 2.60 for alpha = 0.3, 1, 10. Differentiating the Hankel data along the heat flow does not change this row (`e1-burgers-cascade-anticausal`, refereed once): the prime-side flux is zero for every twist (argued), and the difference is the residue sum over zeros.

nodes.statement: Negative index of H_c = rank Gamma_- = kappa = number of distinct zeros in Re z > 0 (not with multiplicity), in {0, 1, ..., inf}; S = S_0/B. An exact count valid for every control; carries no arithmetic constraint.

nodes.statement: The real-node Pick matrix is linear in the zero measure; on-line pairs add PSD terms; a quartet is 2 P_t + R with R of order sigma^2; the LMI never contains the primes. Joint SDP = explicit-formula LP for T in 1e2..1e6, K in {6, 12, 24} on five node families (grid-certified; product 0.32 at (100, 24), below 1.1e-5 for T >= 1000). DH is accepted at its true quartet.

nodes.name: Window functional-equation rigidity with a fixed number of windows (rotation lemma of Q21 with the window-translate lemma of control WT)
nodes.statement: For fixed m, H, eta there is an integer alpha != 0 such that zeta(s + i alpha) passes all m window tests above a height T_0(m, H, eta) (phase identity, defect 2 abs(sin(Psi/2)); Dirichlet simultaneous approximation): no statement "defect at most eta in m windows implies chi(p) = 1" holds with m and eta independent of T. In the finite model (smoothed approximate functional equation, windows of length 2, all primes p <= N = 3.2 sqrt(T/2 pi) free as unimodular phases) unimodular Euler products with window defect below 1e-9 and a simple off-line zero of the model function exist for m below a crossover m* of order pi(N)/30 (within a factor about 2); beyond it local search found none, with no certificate of infeasibility. Past the crossover the conclusion is "F = zeta on the window", which holds for bounded non-multiplicative sequences as well (Hamburger). The test reads the conductor, one phase and about 30 reals per window, not the Euler product. Rigidity needs a window count of Riemann-Siegel size, about sqrt(T)/log T (correction of round 15, row S12b: that count is for the free-prime family on separated windows; on contiguous windows near one height the family meets about 24 + 0.36 K conditions).

At tolerance eta it passes K contiguous unit windows for K up to K_tr(T, eta) = max(eta T log(T/2 pi)/pi, sqrt(8 eta T))(1 + o(1)) over all real alpha; the second term is the reflection translate alpha = -2c found by the referee (E1), whose defect is (L + 2 abs(delta))^2/(8T) with abs(delta) <= pi/(2 log(T/2 pi)) depending on T, so that sqrt(8 eta T) is an upper bound for the reflection branch and the comparison with the k = 1 translate depends on the origin for L within 2 pi/log(T/2 pi) of 8 pi/log(T/2 pi) (second referee `c16-referee-r15-j1prime-u8-screening`, row 1.3, with E1 of its REFEREE.md; it matters only for K at most 2; the lane's word "sharp" holds for abs(alpha) <= T/2 only). K_tr is above T^a for every a < 1 at fixed eta. Free-prime unimodular Euler products with an off-line zero of the finite model (primes up to N = 3.2 sqrt(T/2 pi) free): about 24 + 0.36 K real conditions on K contiguous windows; largest K passed at tolerance 1e-6: 0, 16 to 32, 128 at T = 1e4, 1e5, 1e6 (2.0e-6 at K = 256, one seed; K = 512 not run), against sqrt(T)/log T = 10.9, 27.5, 72.4 (MEASURED, float64, no certificate; N and the crossover are properties of the test design, referee minor (iii)). The combination (zeta(s) + zeta(s + i alpha))/2 has the same absolute defect and no Euler product, with one off-line zero found at T = 1e6; it passes an absolute-tolerance version of the test only (E3), and the minus combination has a(1) = 0 (E2). No rigidity inequality was found. Scope (E4): every translate has all its zeros on the line, so the closure is established for identification-type conclusions ("F = zeta on the window"); for conclusions about the location of zeros it is MEASURED in a finite model only. Not covered: window heights whose ratio differs from 1 by more than eta log(T/2 pi)/pi read together with more than pi(N) prime conditions (every statement found there is "F = zeta on the window", row S12). Round 17: the reach statements of this row are assembled in row Q31 (window information law). Round 18: the second referee of that lane reported (holds with corrections), so the reach statements of this row are superseded by row Q31 as it now stands; the text here is kept as the record of rounds 15 and 16.

nodes.name: Stepanov-Bombieri transplant
nodes.statement: Closure half transplants: RH iff abs(R_x(l)) <= R_x(0) iff a one-sided polynomial bound R_x(l) >= -C(1 + l)^m (a reformulation of the classical psi criterion). The stop is the 2x2 shift minor of one row: Lambda >= 0 alone and the upper-bound sieve certify size e^{l/2} (parity factor 2), the classical region e^{l/2} exp(-c l^{3/5} ...), 7/8 gives e^{3l/8}. No regime found where the minor is both non-trivial and certified. Multiplicity step needs f(s)^k = f(ks), false in characteristic 0. Twisted fixed-s form (`c3-fixedt-growingp-onesided`, refereed once, corrections E1-E5): for fixed s = sigma + it, 1/2 < sigma < 1, t != 0, put G(P; s) = sum_{p <= P} p^{-s} + E_1((s - 1) log P). Its Laplace transform in log P is (1/w)[log((s + w - 1) zeta(s + w)) - log(s - 1) - H(s + w)], H analytic in Re(s + w) > 1/2, with singular points w = 0 and w = rho - s for every zero rho at every height. A lower bound Re G(P; s) >= -C P^alpha for all large P at that one point gives Theta <= sigma + alpha (no exceptional ordinate for this sign: referee E3); an upper bound Re G(P; s) <= C P^alpha gives beta <= max(sigma + alpha, beta_t) for every zero, beta_t the largest real part of a zero with ordinate +-t; conversely Theta <= sigma + alpha gives the two-sided bound O(P^{alpha + eps}). The statement is global, not a window statement: a zero at distance Delta from s enters with weight P^{beta - sigma}/(Delta log P), so a test with P <= Pmax does not separate zeta from a control whose zero is farther than about Pmax^{beta - sigma}/log Pmax (MEASURED, float64, P <= 1e7, on U, RZ_b and DH; referee rerun to 4e6 at other points). The criterion holds verbatim for U, RZ_b and DH. For the Liouville twist G_lambda = -G_zeta identically, so a derivation of a one-sided bound that uses only complete multiplicativity, real unimodular local parameters and meromorphy gives the two-sided bound; this does not cover derivations that use the functional equation, which the Liouville twist lacks (referee E1). That no unconditional input gives the one-sided bound without the two-sided one is ARGUED (a survey of four input types), not a theorem. The step from fixed P to all P is the statement to be proved.

nodes.name: Exact-relation rigidity: the exact relations on the lane's reading list (functional equation, integrality, pole clause, multiplicativity, mu_p*-eigen relation, lattice Hecke relations, seam identity,
nodes.statement: Ordinary multiplicativity added to {FE, INT, N >= 0} does not replace the pole clause, and added to {INT, N >= 0, POLE} does not replace FE. FE deleted: TN1 = zeta(s)(1 + q^(3/4 - s)) (integer frequencies, multiplicative coefficients 1 or 1 + q^(3/4), single pole at 1, zeros on Re s = 3/4). Pole clause deleted: control HQ2 (section 2), which has zeta's functional equation exactly, integer frequencies, multiplicative coefficients >= 1 and four zeros near each pole at distance eps^(1/4)/(sqrt 2 log q)(1 + O(sqrt eps)) from the line. Lemma Q: a pole-free symmetric one-base Dirichlet multiplier is rational in u = q^(1/2 - s) and equal to 1 (Liouville; no multiplicativity; any real q > 1); it gives number of zeros = number of poles on the u-sphere and places neither (referee E4). Proposition F: the members G_q = zeta(s)(1 + (c_q + 2) u/(1 - u)^2), c_q = q^(1/4) + q^(-1/4), have zeta's coefficients for all n < q, the exact functional equation, multiplicative non-negative coefficients, converge to zeta uniformly on Re s >= sigma for each sigma > 3/4 as q grows, and vanish on Re s = 3/4: nothing about zeros follows from an exact relation at a finite stage, and zeros do not move continuously in the coefficient topology inside {FE, INT, MULT, N >= 0}; what completes the identification is analyticity of (s - 1)G on the critical line, the one clause not stated right of 1. Proposition D: (a) in the coefficient topology the hold sets of INT, MULT, CMULT are closed and strip zeros are not continuous; (b) in the strip topology off-line zeros persist (Hurwitz) and the hold set of FE is closed; (c) as corrected by the referee (E1): non-closedness of the hold sets of INT and MULT in the strip topology is CLASSICAL (Voronin, recalled) on the right half-strip only after the lane's witnesses (2 zeta and DH 'on a rectangle', which need non-vanishing on the whole half-strip: RH for 2 zeta, false for DH) are replaced by targets non-vanishing on the whole half-strip, for example f = 1 + 2^-s/4 + 3^-s/4 for MULT and f = 2 for a(1); inside the functional-equation class it is OPEN (d). The statements 'ZQ, NR-q and the Proposition W twin pass multiplicativity' hold by convention only (E2): these twins leave the class at integrality or support before multiplicativity of integer coefficients is defined. Of the relations listed, only a(pn) = a(n) (the definition) and J = 1 (the target) exclude every control. Reading: rigidity on file is linear algebra in the coefficient measure (FE, integrality, pole clause); multiplicativity is linear in log G and is never needed. Closed (one referee in round 18; a second referee file is on record after round 19): do not look for a control failing through multiplicativity inside an exact relation. Screen of HQ2 over the device table: row X2

nodes.name: HQ2 as a screen for devices reading functional equation + integer frequencies + multiplicativity + positivity (campaign round 19; combine; registered expectation: no device rejects HQ2 by a step other
nodes.statement: Twenty device rows classified by the step at which HQ2 fails. Pole clause only: Hamburger, Theorem P and its trace identity, Weil-type explicit-formula positivity, the band devices W, C(theta), N(theta) in the limit, spinor causal S, the rank-2 apex kernel of row D10 (the last two ARGUED). Passes every step: identities (seam, Krein factorisation, lattice Hecke relations), Bost-Connes state positivity (ARGUED, device row 12), and each band device at a fixed finite stage below a measured eps. Another step read first: (a) the sign of nu at powers of q (POS-FE, Lemma L): removed by the new control HQ3, and by Lemma N the poles then sit on the real axis; (b) the local shape at q (Lee-Yang stage property, size of local parameters, Selberg's Euler axiom, the 7/8 size inputs (ARGUED, device row 18); total positivity is removed by HQ4); (c) complete multiplicativity at q (Bost-Connes eigenstates, Hecke eigen-relations, Helson classes). For finitely many modified primes with rational local factors and zeta's functional equation, (b) and (c) are forced: the multiplier splits into one-prime factors symmetric up to sign (Lemma F); a one-prime symmetric factor with no pole in abs(u) <= 1 is 1 (Lemma S in the form strengthened by the referee, E1; zero-freeness is not needed); geometric local factors at finitely many primes and zeta's elsewhere force G = zeta (Lemma C). Referee E1 (the main correction): inside this class the local-shape step is not independent of the pole clause: every such twin other than zeta has a lattice of poles of a local factor on a line Re s = sigma_0 >= 1/2, so the twins rejected by (b), (c) are those already rejected by the pole clause (for sigma_0 > 1/2 by the density estimate N(sigma, T) = o(T); on sigma_0 = 1/2 relative to a Putnam-type theorem on arithmetic progressions of zeros, CLASSICAL, recalled, not opened). 'Another step' therefore describes which hypothesis a device reads first, not a rejection mechanism beyond the pole clause. Lemmas S, F, C are elementary and of a known type (the lattice-of-poles argument behind strong multiplicity one in the Selberg class; novelty not established, E3); the Ramanujan-size case of device row 17 follows from the argument of E1 and is not in the lane file (E2). Numerics (finite stages; certified cells at heights 1e4, 1e5, 1e6, 96 and 192 modes; counts recomputed by the referee from the record files): the prime-side forms of HQ2 equal zeta's form plus the quartets minus 4 times the pole lattice (identity re-derived and rechecked on new cases); HQ2 with factor zeros at distance <= 0.10 passes N(theta) at M = 1 in 384 of 384 object-cells with theta <= 0.85; 801 certified pairs at M = 0 fail through the pole lattice alone; zeta is never certified negative (268 zeta records at M = 0 are undecided, E6). Reading: nothing on file reads multiplicativity jointly with the functional equation inside the strip. Open: infinitely many modified primes (section 6, item 23). Not a statement about zeros of zeta

nodes.statement: The reflection of the target variable is MS Prop. 5.1 (already used; it produces M + l <= 1 as "dual length <= number of rows"). The signal constant c is an invariant of the probe (Lemma U): two high comparisons of one J in the Prop. 2.1 format have the same c, so no identity (row functional equation, Voronoi, approximate functional equation, target functional equation under the integral) changes h; the same holds for a change of the probe below the comparison error, and for a change of slope outside one degenerate configuration (second referee). A probe changed by as much as the top size of the signal is a different probe and is not covered. Ledger with height w = 4 tau and side choice, source geometry: 13/15 at w = 0; reflected >= 13/15 + w/15; unreflected (MS Lemma 9.1, polar term kept) >= 1; empty dual >= 11/12; 5/6 floor of Z15 unchanged. s <-> 1-s cannot act on 1/L (Lemma V). Free geometry (first referee's correction): with the polar term b/12 kept, vertices with h > 1 occur only at lx < l with a hypothetical optimal unreflected sieve or with the K- and P-losses deleted, and those runs fall below 1/2 at the search bound (the reduced system is inconsistent there). With the polar term deleted (G = 0) they also occur for Lemma 9.1 as stated (1/3 at h = 4; 2/3 at h = 2 in geometry M >= 2l) and for the reflected branch with the K-loss alone deleted: 7/9 at (lx, ly, l) = (0, 5/3, 1/3), h = 4/3, not below 1/2. These are MODEL vertices with hypothetical deletions; no lemma supplying the deleted inputs is stated.

nodes.name: Probe quadratic or of higher degree in the target (pair probe; functional-equation pair from the bridge)
nodes.statement: A bilinear probe has signal f(Z1) f'(Z2). Same-side pair with factorised H: the pair hypotheses are equivalent, with changed constants, to the linear hypotheses of Prop. 2.1 with halved exponents; the estimate system is homogeneous of degree one in the target-row length and equals the single-probe system at (lx/2, ly/2, (l1+l2)/2) (36,000 exact comparisons, 0 mismatches); h_pair = 1 + (l1+l2-lx)/2 <= 1 under lx >= l1 + l2; ledger 13/15, 31/36, 5/6 unchanged. With the full source ledger the least value at h_pair >= 1 is 52/57 (8/9 with the polar G), so no such point reaches 13/15. Points with h_pair > 1 at or below a tier value exist only for lx < l1 + l2 (no construction) and need at least one deleted input: the K-loss alone (tie at 31/36, h_pair = 49/48) or the Gram excess alone (69/80 at h_pair = 21/20) (referee correction of the lane's classification). Functional-equation pair (rho, 1 - conj rho): its product has size Z for every beta, so it carries sign information only and cannot feed a size comparison. Shifted product zeta(s) zeta(s - d): the E_a scaling.

nodes.statement: Mollifier + convexity count: e(sigma) = 1 + 2A(theta - sigma), so f(theta) = theta. Pointwise detector: contradiction only at beta >= theta. Density channel carries no theta-dependence for the Halasz-Montgomery-Huxley channel (t-aspect); binding bins at real part 0.694 and 0.7347, below 3/4. Explicit-formula positivity with concentrated tests: f(theta) = theta. Composed map f(theta) = min(theta, sigma_sc), sigma_sc = 0.8749572 / 0.8748866 (imported, not re-run).

nodes.statement: A Moebius sign on a quadratic symbol and centring on the unitary axis did not occur together in any computed case: the symbol enters Hecke relations as a Gauss sum over p, so the reciprocal sits at shift 1/2 and cancels the gain h/r = 1/2. Model abscissa 1, or detection only for beta >= 1. Not computed: genuine cusp forms on the double cover of GL(3).
