nodes.name: Order-2 rows from group families: angular characters lambda^(6k) of Q(sqrt(-3)), ring-class / anticyclotomic characters
nodes.statement: The transform in the family variable is Fourier inversion on a compact group; its kernel depends only on the class of sc and contains no Gauss sum. Root number +1 (Hecke theta inversion for lambda^(6k); Froehlich-Queyrut 1973 Theorem 2, opened and read, for finite-order characters of a quadratic extension trivial on the ideles of the base field). mu is not absorbed: every row is a combination of Moebius sums of the family. Below K = Y^(1/2 - eps) the probe equals its k = 0 row for arbitrary coefficients; in the ray regime the on-ray sum carries the weight N(c*)^(-1/2) (c* = c without its rational part; first referee's correction) and is at most the Cauchy-Schwarz level; the Cauchy-Schwarz ledger gives abscissa >= 1 for all K, Y (log factor in the large-sieve line). The model ledger (1 + kappa)/2 contains its conclusion: a mean-square low estimate over a row set contains the pointwise Moebius bound for the target's row with the same exponent (positivity of a sum of squares; PROVED). The statement for an abstract family "whose epsilon factor is a character of the family parameter" (Theorem 7 (iv)) is ARGUED: its set of admissible derivations is not defined. Reading, not used in a proof: mu enters a family only through a nontrivial Jacobi-sum cocycle of the epsilon factor (order >= 3; Weil 1952 recalled, not opened).
nodes.mapStatus: PROVED for the two families (one referee; second pass on Lemma 2 and Theorem 7 (iv)); abstract row ARGUED

nodes.name: Double covers as a source of a weight-0 (shift 0) epsilon cocycle: Gelfand-Tsetlin weights on the double cover of GL(n); twist families of a GL(n) form
nodes.statement: Narrowed wording (the referee does not hold the lane's claim as worded). Given the recalled Gelfand-Tsetlin recipe for the double cover, at an unramified odd place with chi(-1) = +1, in unitary normalisation every pattern weight is a product of 1, 1 - 1/q, -1/q and T q^(-1/2): the quadratic symbol T occurs only together with q^(-1/2) and every minus sign only together with q^(-1), in every rank (Lemma L; rechecked in rank 2 on new shapes and in rank 3). No local term (sign depending on T) x (unit) occurs at order q^0. For l1 = 0, l2 even the numerator of the row series is the displayed product and its only U-dependent term above order 1/q is -T Yu q^(-1/2) U; this is a reading of one local factor, not a statement about a global Dirichlet series. Epsilon factors of quadratic twists of any GL(n) form are a character times a periodic root of unity (no Jacobi-type value). Not established: the numerator for other labels; any global Euler-product statement; chi(-1) = -1 (q = 3 mod 4); the normalisation convention that turns Lemma 1 (exponent group Z/2) into an obstruction; the global Whittaker constants of a genuine cusp form (section 6 item 18 stays open there). Sources recalled, not opened (Brubaker-Bump-Friedberg / McNamara).

nodes.defeatedBy: none run (local algebraic statement; no control is separated)

nodes.name: Normaliser of the Prop. 2.1 probe: cap at abscissa 2/3 for sextic rows
nodes.statement: At the principal residue point (w, z) = (1, 1/6) the normaliser of MS (10.1) is H_eta(s) = zeta_F^S(2)^-1 L^S(6s - 3, psi_eta) E_eta(s) on Re s > 1/2, psi_eta = (alpha eta)^6 of infinite order, E_eta absolutely convergent and non-vanishing there; second form with L^S(6s-3)/L^S(6s-2) on Re s > 3/7 (Lemma H: local factor (1 - q^2)(1 - D(1-q) - Rq)/((1-R)(1-D)), three referee passes, see the status cell). H_eta has infinitely many zeros in 7/12 <= Re s < 2/3 and none with Re s >= 2/3. MS hypothesis (2.2) (sup over Re s > sigma_0 of abs(H_eta - 1) <= 1/2) holds, for suitable S, if and only if sigma_0 > 2/3: for every sigma_0 <= 2/3 the half-plane contains Re s > 2/3, where sup abs(H_eta) is infinite for every finite S (Kronecker on the logs of rational primes; sum over split l of abs(c_l) l^{-sigma} is unbounded as sigma -> 1+, c_l = psi(p) + psi(pbar)). This uses no zero of L(w, psi_eta). The zeros of H_eta in 7/12 <= Re s < 2/3 matter for a different statement, the holomorphy of H_eta / L^S(s, eta) on Re s > B (Lemma S), whose binding abscissa lies in [7/12, 2/3]. The two statements are separate (referee of `c7-repair-engine-map-r6`, E1). Round 9: what the format uses of (2.2), and the ladder over levels, are in row Z24b. Without (2.2) the exact statement is Lemma S: f_eta(Z) << Z^(C(B)+eps) iff H_eta / L^S(s, eta) is holomorphic on Re s > B. Consequence for the format: with the sextic probe the unconditional conclusion stops at abscissa 2/3 (h = 2, effective order 3). A probe aimed at h = r/2 needs a normaliser without zeros in Re s > 1/2, or the family enlarged to contain psi_eta with common zeros excluded. The formula was first recorded in Z18 as non-binding for the present design.
nodes.mapStatus: PROVED-rel MS Lemma 7.1. Lemma H: three referee passes (sum of table (7.16); (7.11) against the table; series (7.10) with (7.8) and the lift formula, `c8-repair-engine-map-r7/c6-marks-bc-manuscript-check/REFEREE3.md`; the lane directory holds two of the files); the derivation of (7.8) from (7.1)-(7.7) read, not replayed; Hecke L-function facts CLASSICAL

The global statements (continuation of L(w, psi_eta), zeros in 7/12 <= Re s < 2/3, symmetry about 7/12, Lemma S) need (alpha eta)^6 to be a Hecke character and are not available for a general unimodular completely multiplicative weight (E4)

nodes.name: Normaliser cap with the family enlarged along the normaliser character (ladder over levels alpha^f chi)
nodes.statement: What MS Prop. 2.1 uses of (2.2): H_eta holomorphic on Re s > sigma_0, bounded on Re s >= 2, and ord_rho H_eta < ord_rho L at one zero within eps* of the supremum (Lemma U1; one direction of Lemma S of row Z24). So the format fails only by exact resonance at a zero, not by size. (2.2b) holds automatically if beta* > (3 + beta_1)/6 or if beta* < (4 - beta_1)/6; inside that strip nothing is known ("if", not "iff": referee E1). Ladder: G_f = {alpha^f chi}, f_0 = 0, f_{j+1} = 6 f_j + 6, with the format ASSUMED on levels 0..k-1 (hypotheses (F_j)): beta(0) <= max(sigma_0, 3/5 + (2/5) 6^-k) (Theorem A); over all levels the supremum B is <= sigma_0 or lies in [4/7, 3/5] (fixed points of 6b - 3 and of its reflection 4 - 6b). The value 3/5 is the limit of this argument, not a proved limit of the format: no configuration with B in the window is exhibited (E6). With the sourced level only (k = 1) the ceiling stays 2/3 (row Z24). (F_j) for j >= 1 concerns targets of infinite order and has NO SOURCE. Inside the window the needed input is a non-resonance statement (no top-layer zero rho with L(6 rho - 3, psi_eta) = 0), a common-zero statement; "not reachable by counting" is ARGUED. Second normaliser through eta^sigma: the two L-functions coincide iff eta^6 = (eta^sigma)^6, which holds for every chi with chi^6 = 1 (all cubic and sextic residue characters) and others, not only for eta = 1 and chi o N (E2); at levels j >= 1 it needs the format on the levels of frequency -f_j as well. The ladder does not reach 1/2.

nodes.name: Which half of Proposition D fails for THIN: row moments and the probe (6.1) by enumeration
nodes.statement: Not decided. Row moments (Z <= 2^21): every sign weight, multiplicative or not (16 weights, plus two non-multiplicative weights added by the referee), carries a common row component with amplitude linear in its Mertens-type sum (energy exponent 0.13 to 0.20, staircase); for thin weights it is under 2 percent of the mean square in range. The lane's control claim "multiplicativity produces the signal" is refuted by its referee. A large row moment does not decide Proposition D (it leaves abs(I_eps) free). Probe (6.1) (14 sign weights, Z = 2^10 .. 2^18): I_w = principal row + remainder, principal coefficient 1 for Liouville, THIN and the non-multiplicative control, remainder about Z^(-0.24) for all; the range is pre-asymptotic (one sixth-power frequency; the second enters at Z >= 2^36), pre-registered thresholds undecided, condition (N) not seen. First failing hypothesis in the manuscript replay is Lemma 5.8 (periodicity of every twist in the conductor aspect). The question is now a paper question (LIOU-HIGH: high comparison for the Liouville weight through 1/L(x, liou chi) = L(x, chi)/L(2x, chi^2)).

nodes.name: Long prime marks with l - lx = 2 (h = 3 vertex) as the route to abscissa 1/2
nodes.statement: Inside the transcribed reduced system: no geometry with l >= M has abscissa <= 1; B = 1/2 is LP-feasible only at tall h = 3 points ((5,5,7), (5/2,5,9/2), (3,5,5) uncompensated; (4,8,6), (6,12,8) compensated with TRO6 G). Every h > 1 geometry has lx < l and lies outside the hypothesis lx > l of every proved low estimate (MS Prop. 15.3, Liu II Prop. 13.4). Against the manuscript text: of 12 lines of the reduced system 5 agree with a numbered statement, 4 are transcribed differently, 3 have no source. The c5 sentence "low input at h = 3 is equivalent to GRH for the family" is replaced by the chain GRH => (N) => (R), where (N) is the low input, (R) is: beta* <= 2/3 and every top-layer zero of the family in 1/2 < Re s <= 2/3 is a common zero of L(s, eta) and L(6s - 3, psi_eta); (R) => GRH is OPEN (Z24). Each implication is relative to an exact identity and a high side that have no source at the vertex. (N) is not weaker than its conclusion, so the branch gives no independent input. Theorem B (criticality at h > 3) survives with a slack hypothesis; Theorem C holds for sigma <= 1/3 and is resonant above. One sentence of claim A of the c5 lane was false (section 7).

nodes.name: Cap of the Prop. 2.1 format without the hypothesis lx >= l; which low estimates can pass 1 - 1/r
nodes.statement: With h = 1 + l - lx, M = lx + ly: the three inputs B >= 1 - h/r (square-root level), B >= 1 - h/r + (M + l - 1)/2 (K-branch), B >= 1/2 - ly/2 + h(1 - 1/r) - l/2 (floor-class high bound H0) give B >= 1 - 1/r + lx/(2r) for all lx, ly, l >= 0, by the identity with weights (r-2)/r, 1/r, 1/r (2lx/(3r) with the uncompensated high bound); attained on the segment l = lx/2, ly = 1 - 3lx/2, which contains the 13/15 point. The K-branch of Liu II Lemma 2.4 (checked against its text) is the Hilbert-Schmidt lower bound max(Q, D) of the reflected row matrix: no l2-l2 operator bound of that matrix is below it, whether applied to the whole matrix or blockwise on a partition of rows and columns (blocks with a positive proportion of unimodular entries; reflected coefficients without a large entry). The cap contains no target data and holds for U, DH, THIN. Not covered: estimates specific to the coefficient vector of the probe ((E-K): sum_m abs(B_m)^2 << Q^{1+eps} Z^{max(0, k_J, k_P)} for Q P > Z; in the form with all range losses removed it contradicts the consistency bound h <= r/2 for long marks, so it is restricted to lx >= l) or to the vector A; mixed norms; cancellation over non-principal rows below H0 ((E-H)) (rows Z30, Z31 for the state of (E-K) and (E-H) after rounds 8 and 9). Model values (first referee): with the polar term kept, K-loss removed gives 31/36 at h = 5/6 and no vertex with h > 1; H0 removed gives 13/15 (4/5 with G = 0); 1 - 2/r only in the three-input system. "h <= 1" is not a consequence of the format: the format bounds h by r/2 only (given the high comparison and a true low estimate at exponent lx/2). Phase-blind (unreflected) low estimates have B >= 1 by alignment with the Liouville-twisted target (ARGUED: the high identity (7.5), the principal residue and H_lambda(1) != 0 are checked for the twisted target; the bound for its non-principal rows is not written); with G = 0 this is violated, and keeping the polar term b/(2r) suffices for r >= 3. Outside lx >= l the signal exponent and H0 have no numbered source.

nodes.name: Periodicity used as lattice-translation invariance (the 7/8 mechanism)
nodes.statement: Every sextic twist of the target is periodic in the row variable, with a Poisson dual uniform in the modulus (MS Lemma 5.8, Prop. 5.1). In the low half this appears as the absence of one coherent term kappa abs(m_w)^2 in the row second moment: for Liouville rows in one ray class, sum_m w(m) abs(B_m)^2 = D + P + Rem with P >= 0 of order M^{5/6} X^{1/3} (exponent 7/6 at M = X = Z against 1 + eps for a periodic weight); P is proportional to the squared smoothed Mertens sum of the weight and is present for non-multiplicative weights as well. So the periodicity input separates THIN and the Liouville twist (R3 of the mechanism) but is a Hermitian form in the weight: the low half carries neither R1 nor R4. It acts in the conductor aspect of the row family at every height of the target. Floor of the device: row Z15 / Z27 (1 - 1/r), normaliser row Z24 (2/3). For THIN the statement is conditional on conductor-uniform bounds (T1, T2). Round 8 (`c8-liou-row-bound-theorem`, Theorem A, one referee): Liouville rows N = D + P + Rem, P >= 0 of exact order M^(5/6) X^(1/3), abs(Rem) <= C X^(1+eps) relative to a fixed-twist form of Blomer-Goldmakher-Louvel Cor. 1.4; the Liouville analogue of MS (5.36) fails for 7m/8 < n < 5m/4; THIN conditional on a zero-free half-plane for twists of zeta_F.
nodes.mapStatus: PROVED (principal term; one referee); remainder ARGUED-rel a recalled second-moment bound and a contour step (referee: label "PROVED-rel (H2)" lowered); MEASURED Z = 2^7 .. 2^14
nodes.defeatedBy: Liouville twist fails the periodic row bound by Z^{1/6} (averaged over the characters mod f_0); THIN conditional; U not separated in the height aspect

nodes.name: Periodicity used as reciprocity (the 2026 Landau-Siegel device)
nodes.statement: A real primitive character is the Frobenius of a quadratic field: for chi mod q the Frobenius class of every prime H < p <= q^A in Gal(Q(sqrt d, sqrt 2)/Q) is determined by chi(p) and (2/p), and an interpolation determinant over a box in Z[sqrt d, sqrt 2] is divisible by the primes of the relevant Frobenius classes (the divisibility holds for the classes {1, sigma, sigma tau}; referee correction of the lane's statement about split primes). The zero enters only through the classical prime bias of a real zero at s = 1 + 1/log X. Floor: real zeros with 1 - beta <= c/log q; the device is empty to the left and has no height-aspect form (n^{-it} has no field: control U). A completely multiplicative sign function that is not periodic (THIN, Liouville) has no field, and the congruence theta^p = Frob_p(theta) mod p has no object: these controls fail at the field step. The statement itself is a corollary of the compiled Dirichlet 7/8 theorem ((1 - beta) log q >= (log 3)/8). The two uses differ: Z28 uses invariance of the coefficients under translation of the argument and acts at every height; Z29 uses the reciprocity law that turns chi(p) into a splitting condition and acts only in the conductor aspect at height 0. Neither supplies R4.

nodes.defeatedBy: THIN, Liouville twist: fail at the field step (conductor aspect only); U: fails, which is why there is no height-aspect form; DH, heat, E_a, T-NR, Beurling not run. No control on file passes every step of this device (`c11-del-device-read-confirm` section 2: with the floored 7/8 mechanism it is one of the two mechanisms with that property, and both read periodicity in the conductor aspect); it is closed for the height aspect by the absence of a height-aspect form, not by a passing control

nodes.name: (E-K): mean square of the completed cubic-theta rows for the probe vector, dual longer than the row set (left open by Z27; working label Z15d of rounds 8 and 9)
nodes.statement: Round 8. Over Z[omega] (exact unfolding: Poisson in the row variable; theta coefficient times Gauss sum = Moebius times a ray character): Sum_m g_X(m) abs(B_m)^2 = X D + X Sum_{k != 0} F_k, F_k bilinear in smooth partial sums of 1/L(1 + u, eta theta chi_k^{-1}) over the order-6 twist family of the target. (E-K) is a mean value of 1/L over a family containing the target; it is not an operator-norm statement and not an independent input. Under GRH for the family it holds for X >= Z P (proof in outline). The excess form is positive semidefinite of rank 6 (two referee passes; not of signature (2,2)). The Dunn-Radziwill extremal vector is not the probe's configuration. In F_q[T] (q = 7, 13; squarefree unreflected marked rows; exact integers): row energy = diagonal + squared signal; energy / diagonal >= B_0 at dual length 0 (proved), so a diagonal-level row bound implies the Moebius bound of the weight; Weil targets sit at the diagonal in the bulk; failure for targets beyond h = 3 argued from 5 cases. Compensated probe (12.5): h > 1 survives, low input unchanged. Round 9, the window Z/P < X < Z P. Over Z[omega] (`c9-mv6-window-statement`): the displayed statement (MV6-W) is equivalent to (E-K) at each X (Lemma 0, a display of the round-8 Lemma 1 and Corollary 1). With more dual frequencies K than columns N the 1/L frequency form has its own diagonal of size (K/N) D (Proposition 1; this is the duality principle of the large sieve), and the two named absolute-value techniques (family GRH pointwise; the second-moment step of `c8-liou-row-bound-theorem`) return N^(1+eps). This is an obstruction for those two techniques, ARGUED + MEASURED; no lower bound is proved for the Moebius vector, and a method that keeps the signs of the dual sum or works on the row side is not excluded. Slot decomposition of the marked row (Lemmas S1, S2; checked to 1e-15); the upper half-window reduces to a named unproved signed cross term (CROSS). Float screen: theta ratio at most 1.007; aligned +7 to +40 percent and Liouville +2 to +22 percent from Z = 4000 (the slot changes with Z; values within 5 percent of 1 carry no information below Z = 4000). In F_q[T] (`c9-mv6-ff-window-exact`; exact integers, rule fixed before the runs): squarefree marked rows at N = 2 (equal to the completed rows by Lemma P, relative to the model definition), window N - lam < d < N + lam, rmax > 3N, sharp degree classes: the probe vector of a quadratic target of prime conductor has row energy 1.19 to 20.6 times the diagonal at q = 7 (nine active configurations, r* = 6 to 12) and 2.17 to 18.1 at q = 13 (three active configurations), rising in steps (two at q = 7, one at q = 13) and not monotone between steps; in inactive classes the same vectors are below the diagonal. The pre-registered rule returns FAILS. Not established: an exponent of growth; any statement for a bound restricted to inactive classes or with weights that remove the sixth-power frequencies; N = 3 (cube-term rule UNDECIDED on 4 configurations, completion formula untested for twisted vectors); reflected dual sums were not built ("dual length above 3N" is nominal). Round 10, slot split of the exact F_q[T] row energy (`c10-ff-slot-cross-decomposition`; one referee, four corrections): long marks (lam > N, lam > d), q = 7 (N + lam <= 14, one run at 15) and q = 13 (<= 10), N = 2, 3, d <= 3, 58 configurations, exact integers, rules fixed before the runs. R = sum over marked primes P of R^P, the block of P being chi_P(m) times the unmarked row twisted by a cubic character. The slot-diagonal part equals the diagonal up to O(N q^(N - lam/2)) (prime sum of a non-principal cubic character; measured within 2.4e-3 for lam >= 7), so the excess over the diagonal is the cross term over pairs of distinct marked primes, and random signs on the marked primes return every vector to the diagonal in the mean (per-seed scatter about 0.4 at d = 1). The exact squared signal B on the Gauss-sum rows is carried by pairs of distinct primes; with n = (E - B)/D: n <= 1.5 in 583 of 596 vector-configurations, the registered statistic c_perp in [-1.05, 1.5] in 593 of 596, and n = 5.3 for the second target at (2, 12, 1), so the registered rule "excess = coherent cross" is not awarded. Post hoc: a second squared signal in the vector's own character u(m), supported for non-invariant vectors at d = 1 only (7 rows, one q); for the translation-invariant vectors (one, mu) at d = 2 the vanishing remainder is a dimension count (referee). The target is not separated from random multiplicative signs (50 of 51). Reconciliation with the Z[omega] screen (sizes, not a disagreement): at short marks the model has no target excess for the six interior target values at N >= 4 (ratio 0.975 to 0.997; at the window edge and at N = 3 the target values 1.12 to 1.17 lie outside the control ranges, small samples), and in Z[omega] the predicted coherent cross is 1.5e-4 to 3.2e-4 of the diagonal at Z = 2000 to 16000 against resolution 0.01 to 0.02; visibility would need of the order of 1e10 columns with P >= Z^2 (ARGUED estimate from a float proxy, extrapolated over 13 to 15 orders of magnitude). The completed-row run (6, 9, 2) at q = 7 was made by `c10-ff-completed-rows-692` (no row text proposed by that lane; outcome in `campaign/ROUND_LOG.md`, round 10: the literal band is met through offsetting deviations and the completed-row law fails with exact inputs).

nodes.name: (E-H): cancellation over the non-principal rows of the Prop. 2.1 probe beyond the trivial count (left open by Z27; working label Z15d of rounds 8 and 9)
nodes.statement: Round 8. NP = I - I_1 exactly (MS (10.5)). Given the low estimate, a bound on NP is necessary and sufficient for the conclusion of Prop. 2.1 at the corresponding abscissa. This is necessity, and it holds for every proved high-side input of the manuscript as well; it does not make (E-H) circular and does not close it (referee). Closed: the termwise treatment (model floor 13/15; (E-H) never binds with the source ledger) and the norm treatment (31/36 with (E-K); with the K-branch B >= 1 - 1/r + lx/r + l(1/2 - 1/r)). F_q[T], exact dual decomposition at r <= 4: cancellation over rows appears for every weight; it is a property of Poisson duality. Round 9 (wording of its referee). NP is a linear functional of the weight with a kernel that does not depend on the target (Lemma D; confirmed rowwise in 15 blocks); for independent random signs and for random completely multiplicative signs alike, E abs(NP(W))^2 = norm(K_NP)^2. F_q[T], q = 7, (k, N') = (6, 6), r = 3, 4, 5 and (5, 5), r = 3, 4 (referee), exact: cancellation exponent of targets 0.26 to 0.46, of random multiplicative signs 0.34 to 0.45, of random non-multiplicative signs 0.37 to 0.42; the pre-registered excess of the targets over the two seeded control classes is not detected at r <= 5 (24 seeds per class at r = 5; resolution 0.05 to 0.07 in the exponent). "Not detected", not "absent": the power of the test against a true target mechanism is unknown, and an excess below about 0.05 or setting in at r >= 6 is not excluded. Linearity does not imply that the cancellation is of norm type; the measurement supports it (targets inside the range of random vectors). Lemma A (phase-blind low estimates have B >= 1): in the model a sketch for q -> infinity, measured at q = 7 only inside r < (k + N')/2; the number-field sub-step (non-principal rows of the twisted target) is open. State: closed in the model as a source of a target-specific input (second obstruction of the same kind); not a theorem that no proof of (E-H) from the rows exists. Reopened only by a relation among the reciprocals 1/L(s, eta conj chi_u) across u that is not a norm bound.

nodes.name: TRO6 through the signed c-sum, stratified by the squarefull part of the row index (lead 17; inter-stratum cancellation left open by `e2-tro6-signed-csum-stratified`)
nodes.statement: Lemma I: each squarefull stratum B_kappa is a signed sum, signs mu(d) mu(e), of sublattice sums Phi(j) with j squarefull, at most 4^omega(j) terms; the net coefficient is 1 at j = 1 and 0 elsewhere (inclusion-exclusion). Proposition E, one direction: a power saving of abs(B) against the sum over kappa of abs(B_kappa) requires a squarefull j != 1, of norm up to Q, with N(j)^(1/2+eps) abs(Phi(j)) >= c Q^delta abs(Phi(1)); the converse is not proved. Both hold for arbitrary row values. So stratification by a divisibility label recombines sublattice copies of the total and has no saving of its own. Measured (finite trilinear estimator, class-cell mean square, X = 1e6 and 1e7, Q <= 37,150): the exponent in Q of the ratio signed sum / root sum of squares is -0.005 / +0.001 against the pre-registered threshold -0.02, equal within the null scatter 0.003 to random-phase, conjugated, Liouville, THIN, random multiplicative and cubic rows. Limits of the measurement (referee): the two halves of the estimator correlate at 0.14 / 0.23, so the statistic is not a measurement on the true theta coefficients; the squarefree energy share of 94 to 97 percent is the row-count share (93 percent) and carries no arithmetic information; x2 at 1e6 is -0.045 (se 0.034) and "no saving" for x2 rests on the 1e7 fit. Closed for squarefull stratification only. Not covered: the dual c-sum restricted to squarefree n; Type I on average over the level (lane `c10-tro6-dual-squarefree-type1-level`).

nodes.name: Squared signal of the Prop. 2.1 probe as an intersection-form square, as the crossing device of the function-field model (generator ranks 17, 26; neighbours T3, Z26, Z30)
nodes.statement: F_q[T], prime cubic conductor, N <= 3, exact (q = 7; referee reruns at q = 5, 11). The Moebius sum of the probe is S_cop(k) = sum_j c_j t_j with c = c(q, N, lam, k) independent of the curve (Lemma 1, proved; uses "sums over primes of the character are Frobenius traces"). For every vector c and every real quadratic 1 - a u + q u^2, with roots on or off the circle, (sum_j c_j t_j)^2 = -D.D/(2 q^N) with D = sum_j c_j (P_(N+j) + q^j P_(N-j)); the equality is deg[m] = m^2 on an elliptic curve, uses no index theorem and carries no positivity (it holds for genus-1 fakes with off-line zeros; the counts 3444 of 3444 and 9408 of 9408 test nothing beyond Lemma 1). B_coh of the round-8 law is a non-negative combination of such numbers. In genus 2 the equality fails (0 of 80 at q = 7; 0 of 624 at q = 5) and becomes l^2 = (g/2)(-D.D)/q^N - sum (phi_m - phi_n)^2 for trace-linear signals; the probe signal M_N = h_N is not trace-linear for g >= 2, N >= 2. The Riemann hypothesis of the target enters only as the Weil upper bound on the signal. Corrections of the referee: the sentence "the squared signal is (P_0 . D)^2" is false (P_0 . D carries the extra factor t_N; the correct form is S = -(1/2) P_0 . P_[m]); "h > 1 comes from the sixth-power count of the probe rows" holds only within the round-8 law (measured for r <= 5, extrapolated). No new input is named. Not covered: the probe J_k itself for r >= 6 on conductor degree >= 5 (genus >= 2 targets; lane `c11-ff-genus2-probe-jk`).

nodes.name: Twist-modulus reciprocity for twisted second moments of Dirichlet L-functions, applied to the family-positivity mollifier device J_p(s; a) = 1 - sum_{chi mod p} abs(F(s, chi) A_chi(s) - 1)^2 (lead 4;
nodes.statement: J_p > 0 implies F(s, chi) != 0 for all chi mod p (one line). At s = 1 over odd characters, for distinct odd primes, the twisted second moment is a Dedekind sum (classical) and Rademacher's three-term law moves the Moebius variable into the modulus: (modulus p; twists l1, l2) -> (modulus l1; twists l2, p) + (modulus l2; twists p, l1), remainder (l1^2 + l2^2 + p^2)/(12 l1 l2 p) - 1/4; for composite moduli the moment form needs a divisor sum (first referee). The dual carries Moebius signs on the moduli and characters of conductor >= length (the wall of row P52 in the same words). For twist length X >= p - 1 and free weights, sup_a J_p = 1 - #{chi: F(s, chi) = 0} (finite Fourier inversion): no margin. The target's functional equation is not read; the device joins periodicity with the functional equation of the twists (the read set of the 7/8 mechanism), so RS-1 is not reached. At the centre (source opened by the second referee: Bettin, arXiv:1607.05595): exact reciprocity is stated at s = 1/2 with integer shifts, for distinct primes in the moment form and for coprime integers in the Estermann-function form; no exact reciprocity for abs(L(1/2 + it, chi))^2 with t != 0 is in the text. Withdrawn by the first referee: "E_a passes candidate (C)" (it is a fourth moment; the proved statement concerns the linear form); "for X < p the candidate forces sigma > 1" (false at p <= 101).
nodes.mapStatus: PROVED (one-line implication, zero-one law, s = 1 identities; nine-term identity for the twin at every s); CLASSICAL inputs; centre: relative to Bettin (opened), t = 0 only; two referee files

DEL, THIN, U, sign twists fail at the reciprocity step (no periodicity). DH and the interpolation twin: argued only. Backward heat, Beurling: not formulable

nodes.name: Depth-aspect termwise exchange: replace the height twist n^(-it) by a character mod p^k on n <= N, so that a zero at height t is posed in a periodic family with the functional equation of the target u
nodes.statement: The termwise exchange step (E) is false: no character mod p^k is within 0.479/s of c n^(-it) on n <= N once N >= C_r p (p^k abs(t))^(1/r) and abs(t) >= t_r, for each r >= 2 (Lemma X; s = r for r <= 5; thresholds t_r = 40.3, 3.4e5, 7.7e7, 2.3e10 for r = 2..5). For an r-datum, prod (m + a_i H) = prod (m + b_i H) mod H^r (Lemma P) while the real ratio is 1 +- kappa (H/m)^r (1 + o(1)): integers below N supply multiplicative relations that are trivial p-adically and non-trivial at the real place. Covers N >= sqrt(q)(sqrt(t) + 1) for even k and t >= 41 (r = 2; odd k: sqrt(pq)(sqrt(t/1.12) + 1)), and N >= max(sqrt(q), sqrt(t/2 pi)) for abs(t) >= 2.27e10, p^k abs(t) >= (9p)^20 (r = 5). What is refuted is sup-norm termwise agreement of the twists, a sufficient condition for the transfer; a transfer through weighted sums special to the coefficients of zeta is neither found nor excluded (referee G1). Bounded heights with k -> infinity are covered by the written lemma only for r = 2 and abs(t) >= 41; at t = 14.134725 the conclusion holds in the cases tried (exact check at q = 3^30, 5^21, 2^60 by the referee; not a written proof, G2). An exchange is measured to exist only up to N of about 11 to 17 at log q between 6.4 and 12.1 for abs(t) >= 14; non-existence is proved for N >= q^delta and abs(t) >= t_r, and is measured, not proved, between log q and q^delta (relabel 6). Lemma D gives existence without rate; for small abs(t) the principal character is an exchange at every N (G3; the bound N/abs(t) + O(1) of the lane's section 3.5, first bullet, is ARGUED, not CLASSICAL: its error term is misstated and it is not load-bearing, relabel 5). In the 7/8 format the depth characters are already targets (no slot stores a height) and as a row family they are a full dual group (Parseval, circular). Height and depth are independent coordinates of the dual of R_{>0} x Z_p^x; the analytic conductor p^k (1 + abs(t)) is a product. The depth aspect as an analogue of the t-aspect is standard (Postnikov, Gallagher, Milicevic, Blomer-Milicevic; not cited by the lane); Lemma X is a correct elementary lemma, not presented as new (G6).

nodes.name: Bilinear twist-modulus reciprocity at height t (Bettin 2016, arXiv:1607.05595, Theorem 5 with the Estermann reciprocity, case z = 0, complex s) read as a J-form over characters (campaign round 13; com
nodes.statement: Entries R_chi(t) = rotated L(s, chi) L(s, chi-bar), s = 1/2 + it: real, R_chi = R_chi-bar, R_chi(t) = const Z_chi(t) Z_chi(-t). J = complex conjugation on the character group, J = 1 exactly on real characters. For L(1/2, chi) != 0 (hypothesis added by restriction 12 of `c14-referee-r13-independent`), the sign of R_chi(t) is (-1)^(number of zeros of L(s, chi) in the strip with ordinate in (-t, t)): off-line zeros come in pairs with the same ordinate, so the sign is fixed by the argument principle and is the same for every function with this functional equation and real pair entry, whether or not its zeros are on the line (referee addition). Inertia of the group matrix: twice the number of complex pairs with odd parity and non-zero real part of the weight transform, plus the sign of the zeta entry 2 sqrt(q) cos(t log q) - 2 (index count as corrected, E3). The reciprocity at height t, truncated at any J >= 1 with the remainder as one contour integral (integrand of order abs(v)^(-(J + 3/2 + c)) with -1 < c < -1/2, E1 and restriction 11 of `c14-referee-r13-independent`; a finite form with remainder is already in the source, E2), is the period relation z -> -1/z of the Eichler-integral series of E(z, 1/2 + it) at the central point of its additive twists (this reading is ARGUED): the height is the spectral parameter, the target's functional equation enters only through the archimedean kernel, and the two L-arguments are tied at (s + j, s - j), j integer, so no kernel in two independent heights is reached. No one-sided statement that is not an identity follows. With row Z34 exact reciprocity is closed as a height-reading device in the Hermitian and the bilinear form. Not covered: an exact law for the Estermann function off its central point (none known).
nodes.mapStatus: PROVED (Lemma 1 for J >= 1, Proposition 3, Lemma 5), re-derived by one independent referee; the second independent referee (`c14-referee-r13-independent`) reproduced Lemma 1 numerically at two new instances and at one of the lane's (a/q, b) with a different J (defect below 1e-17) and did not re-prove it, and confirmed the sign rule on 160 of 160 new cases (two characters of conductor 17 and 19); RELATIVE TO Bettin Theorem 5 (source opened as text); sign changes of R_chi established by direct evaluation at q = 5, 7, 11 (the Hardy-type theorem for the pair is cited, not opened, E4); four corrections

nodes.name: Global Whittaker constants on covers of GL(3) as a new array (cell U6 (c)): cubic theta on the cubic cover; genuine cusp forms on the double cover (campaign round 18; deepen; the lane's proposed label
nodes.statement: Cubic cover: the constants are cubic Gauss sums. tau(p^l1, p^l2) is non-zero iff (l1, l2) = (0,0) or (1,1) mod 3 (count verified from a recalled Kazhdan-Patterson free-orbit criterion; the case l2 = 0 confirmed in the opened source, Friedberg-Ginzburg arXiv:1403.3929); tau(p, p) = kappa conj(gamma(p)) q^(-1/6) tau(1, 1) with kappa real, 0.97 to 0.99 on 34 + 23 indices at X = 1e5 and 2e5, limit not resolved (the lane's '0.989 to 0.992, rising with X' holds for its indices only; referee correction 1); periodicity at p^3 and the reciprocity cocycle on the diagonal hold to 1 to 3 percent. This is a known array (Proskurin; Bump-Hoffstein; not opened) and the cubic Gauss-sum array used by the family of rows Z14, Z15 (those rows record exponent bounds, not an array). The sign candidate (C3) for the smoothed diagonal sum is a residue statement of Patterson's series whose truth for a cubic-character twist depends on arg gamma(p) (the twist by (m/P13)_3 satisfies it at all 398 grid points; correction 2): a residue identity, not a separating inequality. Double cover: theta has no Whittaker coefficient (opened); for cusp forms the local Whittaker space has dimension 4 (verified from the recalled commutator), relations inside a class modulo squares are the identities of row Z23, and the squarefree-class values a(D1, D2) are not computed. A method is on file (genus sums of point values of a GL(3) Maass form at positive ternary forms; Jacquet's correspondence recalled), not run; the test (K3) is not yet a defined statement (eps(p, q) unspecified; a single 2 x 2 determinant is not equivalent to a pure tensor in 4-dimensional spaces; the class count for D_max = 1e4 is not derived; correction 4). The comparison at n = 4 is across covers (twist c = 0 against c odd; correction 3). Reading: a unique Whittaker model forces Gauss sums (nothing beyond the Z14 / Z15 family); a non-unique model gives global period data without a Hecke relation; neither gives an inequality. State of the cell: cubic half closed as a known array; double-cover half a cell with a method and no supporting argument for (K3) (round-19 lane `c19-u6c-double-cover-k3-run`). Addendum, campaign round 19 (`c19-u6c-double-cover-k3-run`, one referee: holds as stated, nine corrections, none changes the verdict). (K3) is made a defined statement on the period side: for primes p = q = 1 mod 8 with (p/q) = 1 the genera of <1,1,d>, d in {1, p, q, pq}, have pairwise interchanged local similarity classes at every place (Lemma Q of that lane, PROVED, re-derived by the referee), so a genus-sum array K_phi(G) = sum phi(Q)/abs(O(Q)) of a scale-invariant phi that is a product of local functions satisfies K(G_1) K(G_pq) = K(G_p) K(G_q); the referee adds that this array-level identity is the consequence of a pure-tensor period functional at the spherical vector. Direction fixed once: '(K3) holds' in the lane means the array is not a product (Delta != 0); the campaign summary writes 'the identity fails' for the same fact (correction 7). Eisenstein input (Epstein zeta at class level; closed form with Siegel's class-number product, CLASSICAL): the product identity fails for all sufficiently large real s (limit ratios R_1 = 1/6, 1/2, 3/4, 1/4, 2/3, 2, 5/2, 2/3, 2, 4, 7/2 in 11 quadruples; no explicit s_0, correction 4) and by ball arithmetic at 12 values of s in each quadruple (132 of 132: 8 real and 4 complex values; s = 0.75 + 40i not decided; radii up to 5.1e-4 at 0.75 + 25i; the certificate covers the analytic step, the class lists rest on the Minkowski bound and local invariants, compared by the referee with Eichler's mass formula; corrections 1 to 3). Cusp input: one self-dual cusp form (the symmetric square of the first odd Maass form of SL_2(Z); Hecke data by Hejhal's method; the evaluator satisfies the T_2 and T_3 eigen-equations to about 1e-8, referee test): the identity fails in 14 of 14 quadruples by 2.6e3 to 5.7e6 error bars (the count and the upper figure are the lane's table; the referee confirms the lower margin, 2596 bars, and a new quadruple with Delta non-zero by more than 1e6 spreads; the Hecke term of the error bar is a heuristic, not a propagated bound, referee correction 8) (float64, MEASURED; nothing is shown for a non-self-dual cusp form, correction 6). Controls: phi = 1 (mass) gives exactly 0. Delta takes both signs for both inputs, so the tested functional gives no one-sided inequality (scope: the functional Delta on the tested family, correction 5), and (K3) does not separate the Eisenstein member from the cusp member. Fixed-n theta coefficient arrays are not valid product controls (not scale-invariant). The reading as a statement about Whittaker functionals on the double cover passes through Jacquet's correspondence (RECALLED) and is not part of what is established. State after round 19: the double-cover half is closed by the lane as global period data without a Hecke relation and without an inequality, on one referee file; second referee owed (`c20-referee-theorem-d-headline-and-r19`).

nodes.name: Phase-blind no-go for the weld width
nodes.statement: The orthogonal root-sum-square majorant, the strongest bound from shell orthogonality plus reproducing-kernel duality, is >= m/sqrt(5) = 0.4110 > R_ex = 0.2797 for every shell-mass distribution. The width needs a phase-coherent arithmetic bound.

nodes.name: Rung Toeplitz (Herglotz) test detects DH at ln 2 / ln 4 / ln 6
nodes.statement: Rung moments m_k(p) = c(p^k)/log p; for unitary local degree 1 the Toeplitz T_p^(K) = [m_|i-j|] is PSD. DH fails: lambda_min(T_2^(2)) = -1.15558, Szego limit -1.79360. Onsets sharp against formal local Euler products: ln 2 (unitary, full), ln 4 (even data), ln 6 (Euler only). No zero-location content.

nodes.name: Interval-Newton/Krawczyk enclosure for the height of the N-th zero count
nodes.statement: For f(T)=(T/2pi)(log(T/2pi)-1)-N on an interval [T] with midpoint m: one Krawczyk step proves a unique zero T0 in [T] and encloses it; contraction factor rho about delta/U with U=log(m/2pi), delta the relative half-width.

nodes.name: RZ-PEN chain: r-uniform block symbol-pencil floor
nodes.statement: Closed-form r- and m-uniform floor on the 2x2 block symbol pencil (det/trace, pair identity, Jensen), refined through RZ-PEN2..8 (chart cover, exact root, tail-chart cap, pair extension, b-exact trace); A_unif4(2) = 1.997. Cross-block collapse decided at exact order 2. Pointwise program recorded as exhausted.

nodes.name: m-uniform Riesz lower bound for the seam Gram on the octave twin lattice
nodes.statement: The normalised seam Gram (entries sech of half the log-ratio) is block Toeplitz in the octave index; Grenander-Szego bounds lambda_min by the symbol infimum uniformly in the number m of octaves. The twin-pair symbol does not port off-lattice (onset gap 4.611560 depth units).

nodes.name: RZ-TWIN: m-uniform block Riesz lower bound on the octave twin lattice
nodes.statement: The normalised seam Gram sech((x_i - x_j)/2) on the octave twin lattice has an m-uniform closed-form lower Riesz bound A_twin > 0 with a Szego ceiling, from a Toeplitz quadratic-form sandwich, Poisson summation and Jensen.

nodes.name: S_barrier: no off-line zero of H_t above the verified height
nodes.statement: For every x > T_PT = 3e12 the function H_t has no non-real zero at the repo heat parameter. Platt-Trudgian supplies only the base case below T_PT; the statement needs a finite winding check (B1) and a semi-infinite tail lemma (B2).

nodes.name: Pointwise S(T) bounds give no Lambda lever
nodes.statement: Counting-input ceiling for mirror descent p_E(Y) = 4 rho_z (pi/2 - arctan((E+1)/(rho_z Y))): the all-real model needs E <= 3.363 for formal Lambda 0.2 while the proved E = 5.675 gives 0.2424. Beurling-Selberg extremal functions do not help: off-line zeros in short windows lack local density control.

nodes.name: S containing {2,3}: Dirichlet-rank obstruction
nodes.statement: For S containing {2,3} the positive trace exists abstractly but its remainder is not a regular function: rank(Z_S^*) > 1 makes log(Z_S^*) dense in R. The remainder share does not fall as primes are added (99.71% at ln 3 to 99.99997% at ln 4 for S2, S23, S235).

nodes.name: saddle pair count saving equivalence
nodes.statement: In the estimate system C1-C3 of the 7/8 method, a restricted fourth-moment saving U^-omega at block m* = 0.4183 implies a count saving U^-omega on plain-witness rows; detector-beside-fourth-moment needs > 53%, two-scale 48-49%, one-scale mixed moment 1/6 of the large-sieve-to-Lindelof gap.

nodes.name: Sawtooth bound for S(T)
nodes.statement: Given Trudgian 2011, |S(t)| <= sqrt(2 A rho)(1 + o(1)): 5.6748 at 3e12 against 6.6612 (Trudgian 2014); asymptotically weaker (0.137 vs 0.112 log T). Not a mirror-descent lever.

nodes.name: Sawtooth lemma for S(T)
nodes.statement: If |S_1(t2) - S_1(t1)| <= A(t2) and rho = theta'/pi, then S(t) <= A(t+delta)/delta + delta rho(t+delta)/2 and S(t) >= -A(t)/delta - delta rho(t)/2; optimal delta gives |S(t)| <= sqrt(2 A rho)(1+o(1)): 5.6748 against 6.6612 at 3e12. Input constant (Trudgian 2011) unchecked.

nodes.name: Cofinal gamma-relative bound on the prime form
nodes.statement: With V_W[f]=2Re int R_f d nu: (G_W+mu I)^{-1/2}V_W(G_W+mu I)^{-1/2}<=I for one fixed mu>0 cofinally in support would give a uniform floor. Direct absolute-transport comparison costs at least c_mu lambda/sqrt(log lambda).

nodes.name: Scalar cover bounds R entrywise and by its trace
nodes.statement: Gshear is a Gram matrix for the positive weight sinh(a tau), so R is PSD, |R_jk|<=sqrt(R_jj R_kk)<1 and ||R||<=trace R=sum_j R_jj. Each scalar-cover ratio R_jj<1 but the sum exceeds 1, so the cover does not give a contraction.

nodes.name: Volterra norm along the de Bruijn flow tracks kernel scale only
nodes.statement: With |Phi_t|_2 normalised to remove the exp(t u^2) scale, the Volterra norm sweep shows no residual zero-location signal, including on the t<0 side where the conclusion is false.

nodes.name: Archimedean vs p = 2 cancellation across ln 2
nodes.statement: Archimedean-only positivity radius a* = 0.3716 (odd) / 0.4101 (even) vs (ln 2)/2 = 0.3466. Positivity across ln 2 is a cancellation to 5-6 relative digits: residual/P_2 = 7.5e-5 at a = 0.5, 3.2e-6 at (ln 3)/2. The second adelic direction is block-diagonal over 2-power characters.

nodes.name: Connes-Consani scaling site does not extend Weil positivity past u = ln 2
nodes.statement: Weil positivity is a theorem for test support inside |u| < ln 2 (prime side empty). The scaling site gives a reflection-positive transverse Euclidean direction only at the archimedean place; finite places enter through orbit counting with weights (log p) p^(-k/2). Related rows P9, P19.

nodes.name: Causality criterion sits at the zeta(1+it) level
nodes.statement: The mirror resonance of a zero z = x + iy of H_t has Re s >= 1/2 iff |y| >= 1 iff Re w >= 1. The local all-pass factors z_p(s) = zeta_p(2-2s)/zeta_p(2s) need Re s > 1/2 and Re s < 1/2 at once: their product converges absolutely nowhere.

nodes.name: Winding split of the scattering phase
nodes.statement: W(T) = W_inf(T) + arg zeta(1 + 2iT)/pi + 1/2, with W_inf(T) ~ (T/pi) log(T/(pi e)). On the axis s = 1/2 + it the bridge is sampled at w = 2it: |chi(2it)| = sqrt(t/pi) sqrt(tanh pi t), cancelled exactly by |c_inf|.

nodes.name: Signed estimate paying E - B*D^{-1}B
nodes.statement: An actual signed arithmetic estimate strong enough to pay the Schur charge E-B*D^{-1}B of the complementary block, with physical normalization, domains and tails intact; equivalently an all-scale estimate of the true signed Schur residual.

nodes.name: Pick Schur defect equals the Suzuki screw form on exponentials
nodes.statement: P_L(x,y)=(L(x)+L(y))/(x+y). Next-node defect Delta_N(x)=d(x)-v*P_N^{-1}v=b(r_x,r_x), r_x=f_x-sum c_i f_i, f_x(t)=xe^{-xt}; generally Q_L(v)=sum b_i conj(b_j)P_L(x_i,x_j)=b(r,r) for v=sum b_j e^{-x_j t}, x_j>1/2.

nodes.name: Route A: |R_a(w)|<1 on Re w>0 by maximum principle
nodes.statement: R_a(w)=X(w-a)/X(w+a), X(w)=xi(1/2+w). |R_a(it)|=1 exactly (X even, real on R). Phragmen-Lindelof would give |R_a|<=1 inside if R_a were analytic there, i.e. if X(w+a) had no zeros in Re w>0: the single circular gap.

nodes.name: Cross-seam ratio Lambda(nu,d) of exponential sums
nodes.statement: Lambda(nu,d) = sup over signed g = sum a_i e^(-nu_i t) of int_d^inf g^2 / int_0^inf g^2 equals lambda_max of the pencil (D G D, G) with Cauchy Gram G_ij = 1/(nu_i + nu_j), D = diag(e^(-d nu_i)).

nodes.name: Sech seam Gram: Poisson dual symbol and finite-section envelope
nodes.statement: G_n[j,k] = sech((j-k) delta/2) has symbol f(theta) = 1 + 2 sum sech(m delta/2) cos(m theta) = (2 pi/delta) sum_k sech((pi/delta)(2 pi k - theta)) > 0. For every delta and n: A_opt(delta) = ess-inf f <= lambda(G_n) <= f(0). Condition number scales as exp(pi^2/delta).

nodes.name: Lean: packet estimate to de Bruijn chain with (H6) discharged by the argument principle
nodes.statement: In the section 4.7 chain, wind(H_t0/B_t0)=0 implies no zeros in the region, given B_t0 nonvanishing (side condition surfaced). Kernel-checked in the Aristotle project.

nodes.name: RH-true / RH-false Selberg control pair
nodes.statement: No RH-false control was run in the Selberg sandbox. A pair (cocompact arithmetic group with the half-plane RH-analogue, against a group with an exceptional eigenvalue) would test whether Euler-product calculi over prime geodesics see zero location. Z = det(1 - L_s^2) (Mayer) supplies a transfer operator.

nodes.name: Selberg zeta freeze sandbox lacks an RH-false control
nodes.statement: On the PSL2(Z) Selberg zeta (3,784,618 primitive classes; Euler product vs Mayer determinant 6.1e-9) Theorem U, telescope and five-shell hold verbatim; sigma = 0.55 phase gate Re Z < 0 on 6.1% vs 0% for zeta. Not run: an RH-true / RH-false Selberg pair (cocompact vs exceptional eigenvalue).

nodes.name: Geometric object with primitive length spectrum {log p}
nodes.statement: Search for a hyperbolic surface (or graph, discrete Deninger-Connes) whose primitive geodesic lengths are log p: no candidate; the discrete prime-graph construction is equally hard; the naive T^inf flow fails and Connes adelic structure is needed.

nodes.name: Theorem P: Type-I majorants lose a factor 2 at square-root scale
nodes.statement: Every Type-I majorant W of level <= X^{1-eps} with coefficient sums <= (log X)^A has B(W) >= (4 - o(1)) sqrt X, so the bound for sum Lambda(n) n^{-1/2} has error >= (2 - o(1)) sqrt X. Under ZF(7/8) this extends to coefficient sums up to X^{eta/8 - eps}.

nodes.name: Selberg companion in Theorem PC has abscissa sigma* >= 1/2
nodes.statement: Any non-negative-coefficient coupling c Z'/Z + E with the PSL2(Z) Selberg zeta has sigma* >= 1/2; Theorem PC is silent at rho/2.

nodes.name: Phase gate on sigma = 0.55: Selberg zeta against zeta
nodes.statement: On sigma = 0.55, t <= 26, Re Z < 0 on 6.1% of the grid for the PSL2(Z) Selberg zeta against 0% for zeta (min Re zeta = 0.014); modulus-first threshold sigma*(0): zeta 1.578, Selberg 1.173. Attribution confounded by the rho/2 zero family at Re s = 1/4.

nodes.name: Theorem U on the geodesic monoid
nodes.statement: For a finite set G of primitive geodesic classes the sieve algebra is span{T_D : D subset G}, dimension 2^|G|; every freeze word followed by a linear functional is L(diag(m) c) for a unique m. Telescope and five-shell identities are telescoping algebra with no zero information. Collapse: 72 instead of 256 for the first 8 classes.

nodes.name: Pole-coupled companion from the Selberg zeta of PSL_2(Z)
nodes.statement: Proposal: apply Theorem PC to a companion with independently fixed zeros: Selberg zeta of PSL_2(Z) (prime-geodesic coefficients >= 0, pole at 1, spectral zeros on Re s = 1/2, scattering zeros at rho/2). Decisive test not run: sigma* of the coupled companion vs beta_0/2 < 1/2.

nodes.name: Route 28: freeze calculus on the Selberg zeta function
nodes.statement: Run the twin-ladder freeze calculus on the Selberg zeta function, where the RH analogue holds by self-adjointness, to find which ladder statements become provable. Listed as open in the fifty-route synthesis.

nodes.name: Self-referential gap ODE reproduces the collision
nodes.statement: Substituting beta = 1/sqrt(u) into the gap ODE gives the autonomous du/ds = -8 + 4 sqrt(u): unstable fixed point u* = 4; for u0 < 4 collapse in time T_SR = log(2/(2 - sqrt(u0))) - sqrt(u0)/2 -> u0/8. No candidate form of an a-priori g_min > 0 bound closes into a positive floor.

nodes.name: Semilocal {inf,2} prolate spectrum has two eigenvalues near modulus 1
nodes.statement: The {inf,2} prolate operator has lam_S(0)=0.9999731 and a second near-modulus-1 eigenvalue lam_S(1)=-0.9927022; the second-largest signed eigenvalue is 0.6202012 (top gap 0.3798). Kato-Temple capture thresholds: adjacent 8.4e-3, bottom twin 1.2e-3.

nodes.name: Remainder share D_S/L_S cannot separate prime sets
nodes.statement: On the unit-norm W-minimiser, 1 - share = lambda_W/L_S(h0) by definition for any decomposition W = L_S - D_S; share is 99.71%-99.99997% on [ln 3, ln 4] for S = {inf,2}, {inf,2,3}, {inf,2,3,5} alike. A statement about the metric at cutoff 1, not about the S -> all primes limit.

nodes.name: Semilocal Fourier transform F_S for S = {inf, 2, 3}
nodes.statement: F_S eta(w) = sum_{a,b>=-1} c_2(a) c_3(b) eta^(2^a 3^b w), c_p(k) = 1 - 1/p (k >= 0), -1/p (k = -1); Mellin multiplier rho_2 rho_3 with rho_p(s) = (1 - p^{s-1})/(1 - p^{-s}), unimodular on Re s = 1/2. For g-support < ln 4, W = L_S - D_S exactly. Conditional on Connes-Consani framework.

nodes.name: Route H: semilocal S={inf,2} Sonine trace identity is exact but not gap-free
nodes.statement: Tr(Q_S theta(g)Q_S)=W_inf(g)+W_2(g)+poles with Q_S=Q_inf x Q_2 holds, but p=2 contributes a sign-indefinite rank-limited shift helping only the odd sector; proven positivity does not extend past support u=ln 2. Non-Sonine pole-term bridges fail by the same p=2 resonance.

nodes.name: Semilocal S = {inf,2} Sonine trace identity
nodes.statement: Tr(theta(f) P P^_S P) = W_inf(f) + W_2(f) + D_S(f), F_S = I o (u_inf u_2) (Tate factor), trace side positive (multiplier min 0.0650). The remainder D_S (log spikes at 2^k) carries 96.7% (a = 0.5) / 99.71% (a = (ln 3)/2) of the trace on the pole-free minimizer.

nodes.name: Route 12: semilocal trace identity for S = {infinity, 2, 3}
nodes.statement: Exact semilocal trace identity for S = {infinity, 2, 3} in the Connes-Consani framework (conditional). For S = {infinity, 2}: Tr(theta(f) P P^_S P) = W_infinity + W_2 + D_S with remainder D_S 96.7-99.7% of the trace on the pole-free minimizer.

nodes.name: Semilocal trace side positive and growing with S
nodes.statement: Trace-side symbol L^_S(0): +0.0650 (S = {inf,2}), +0.0504 (S3), +0.10 to +0.12 (S = {inf,2,3}), positive on [0,30]; Galerkin lambda_min(L_S23) = 0.175-0.225, lambda_min(L_S235) = 0.22-0.26. Not a certificate; the limit S -> all primes with cutoff -> infinity was not tested.

nodes.name: SEP-OPT: the lattice is the extremal delta-separated configuration
nodes.statement: The class-optimal m-uniform Riesz floor over delta-separated node sets equals the lattice Szego infimum A_opt(delta) = ess-inf of f(theta) = 1 + 2 sum_{m>=1} sech(m delta/2) cos(m theta). Conditional on two cited classical inputs, including a Carneiro-Littmann-Vaaler Gaussian-subordination minorant.

nodes.name: A probe in which the exceptional coset and principal signal separate
nodes.statement: Remaining lever after closing Prop 15.2 evaluation/subtraction/filter: a probe family where the exceptional coset and the signal separate. Not excluded: non-Poisson summation formulas and residue families of unbounded order; metaplectic Eisenstein series, higher-rank covers and multi-variable families.

nodes.name: sigma_0 = 1 - h/6 + b/12 = 5/6 + M/12 - l/6
nodes.statement: In the 7/8 manuscript sigma_0 = 5/6 + (M - 2l)/12 with h = 1 - l_x + l, M = l_x + l_y; on M + l = 1 this is 11/12 - l/4: 11/12 at l = 0, 7/8 at l = 1/6 (geometry l_x = 17/48, l_y = 23/48, b = 1/8).

nodes.name: Duality: exceptional coset exists exactly when the signal does
nodes.statement: For every sextic probe the exceptional coset e_0 t^6 a^6 exists exactly when xi^6 = 1, the same condition as for the high-side signal; the coherent block is scaled by one constant, so it can be evaluated but not filtered. Evaluation needs sextic theta coefficients at squarefree indices, unknown (no Whittaker uniqueness for GL_2^(6)).

nodes.name: Theorem A: mean square of complete sextic theta coefficients
nodes.statement: M^nat_sigma(Q) << Q^{5/6 + eps}, and sum |A - A^theta|^2 << (Q/Y') Z^eps for rho^nat with no exceptional term; Prop 15.2 holds without its P_a^2/Y' term. Proved relative to Broker-Hoffstein 2016 and the manuscript.

nodes.name: Sextic theta coefficients over Z[omega], norm <= 1e7
nodes.statement: Cubic calibration reproduces Patterson (rms 0.5%, first-moment exponent 0.8330 vs 5/6). Sextic first moments: exponent 0.683 [0.669, 0.697], consistent with 2/3; no Gauss-sum law at prime indices (alignment 0.50 vs 99% null 0.37); no twisted multiplicativity; mean-square slope 0.868, odd part 85.7%.

nodes.name: SGN-2X: exact two-rate signed constant
nodes.statement: Lambda_2 = w_1 w_2 + h^2/2 + (h/2) sqrt(h^2 + 4 w_1 w_2), h = (w_1 - w_2)(nu_1 + nu_2)/(nu_2 - nu_1). Coalescence law: Lambda_2 -> e^{-2x}(1 + 2x^2 + 2x sqrt(1+x^2)). Witness (1,2,ln 2): (13 + 3 sqrt17)/32.

nodes.name: SGN-C: signed count-priced shift certificate
nodes.statement: R <= e^(-2x) [ sum_{k<N} C(K,k)(1 + e^(x/K))^k ]^2 with N = number of distinct rates, from a polynomial shift multiplier p(e^(-(d/K)s)); subsumed by NP-CERT as one feasible interpolant.

nodes.name: All ESY-closure routes meet pair correlation at support > 1
nodes.statement: Direct Selberg, Sobolev-via-Hughes-Rudnick and higher-cumulant routes each need Montgomery pair correlation beyond support 1 (and rho_3 at a later step). Selberg trace, Goldston-Gonek, Heath-Brown fourth moment, Goldston-Yildirim, Tao entropy and Maynard sieve give the same (log T)^{1/2} Cauchy-Schwarz gap in support (1, 5/4). Mean-value inputs: map MV-CAP.

nodes.name: Decoupled pass/shear rates soften ||R|| but leave the kernel class
nodes.statement: Pass rate b != shear rate a: at s_a=3, ||R||=20.94 (s_b=1), 4.617 (s_b=3), 0.338 (s_b=6); ||R||=1 locus s_b* about s_a+1.716. Inadmissible: cosh(b tau), sinh(a tau) are parts of one exponential multiplier only when b=a.

nodes.name: Shear Gram is the hollow antisymmetric de Branges Wronskian
nodes.statement: G_shear(u,v)=Phi(u)Phi(v)sinh(a(v-u)) is antisymmetric, zero on the diagonal, indefinite with spectrum symmetric about 0; min eigenvalue about -||G_shear|| about -4.8e-6 at NPHI=10, a=0.5, U=6.

nodes.name: Rank-2 shear Gram: Hilbert-Schmidt norm = sqrt 2 times operator norm = mu
nodes.statement: For the antisymmetric Gram matrix of two vectors p, q: sum of squared entries = 2 mu^2 with mu^2 = |p|^2|q|^2 - <p,q>^2, operator norm = mu, and the Volterra shear has HS norm equal to mu. Kernel-verified.

nodes.name: Antisymmetric shear Gram is exactly rank 2
nodes.statement: i*G_shear has spectrum {+mu,-mu,0,...} with mu=sqrt(|p|^2|q|^2-<p,q>^2), so min eig=-||G_shear||; independent of the (a,U) cell and verified against a dense eigensolve.

nodes.name: Shear norm plateau ||R|| from 0.75 to 1.33
nodes.statement: The antisymmetric rank-2 shear norm obeys ||R||^2 = |p|^2|q|^2 - <p,q>^2 for core-normalized cosh/sinh vectors and creeps from 0.75 to 1.33 with degree; lambda_d decreases to 0 with sign >= 0 through d = 16 (Arb). Both are consistent with verified zeros and carry no forward information.

nodes.name: Shear obstruction depends on s = a*U only
nodes.statement: tau=U x gives R_jk=h_jk(s)/sqrt(d_j(s)d_k(s)), d_j=int_0^1 cosh(sx)x^{2j}dx, h_jk=int_0^1 sinh(sx)x^{j+k}dx. R is invariant under (a,U)->(a/lam,lam U): no orthogonal admissible lever. Four pairs with aU=3 give ||R||=4.617013710.

nodes.name: Scaling orbit does not select the operating value of s
nodes.statement: The orbit constraint is a level set of s=a*U, one equation short of fixing an operating point; every s>0 is admissible, ||R(s)|| ranges over (0,DEG+1). Whether K_a>=0 holds depends on which s the section-26 construction uses, which is not determined in this cohort.

nodes.name: De-homogenised shear/pass correlation matrix R(s)
nodes.statement: On phi_j(tau)=(tau/U)^j: D_jj=int_0^U cosh(a tau)phi_j^2, H_jk=int_0^U sinh(a tau)phi_j phi_k, R_jk=H_jk/sqrt(D_jj D_kk); pass and shear forms are the even and odd parts of one exponential e^{a tau}. ||R||=Perron eigenvalue. Representative truncation, not the section-26 Gram.

nodes.name: ||R(s)|| is monotone in s and saturates at DEG+1
nodes.statement: On s in [0.05,20] (step 0.05) ||R(s)|| is strictly increasing with no turning point for DEG=4,6,8,10, saturating toward the all-ones ceiling DEG+1 as s->infinity; the ceiling rises linearly with truncation size.

nodes.name: Perron norm vanishes linearly at small s
nodes.statement: h_jk(s)=s/(j+k+2)+O(s^3), d_j(s)->1/(2j+1), so ||R(s)||=C1 s+O(s^3) with C1 about 3.6401763947 (degree 4): inf_{s>0}||R(s)||=0, not attained. No uniform positive floor; ||R||<1 holds for small enough s.

nodes.name: Rank-two shear commutator V - V^#
nodes.statement: V - V^# = p(x) q* - q(x) p*, p = Phi cosh(a.), q = Phi sinh(a.): rank 2, range Phi span{e^{at}, e^{-at}}. Hence spec(i Gshear) = {+mu, -mu, 0}, mu = sqrt(|p|^2 |q|^2 - <p,q>^2), and ||Gshear||_op = ||V||_HS exactly.

nodes.name: Conjecture 15.2/15.3: shift-bridge positivity K_a>=0
nodes.statement: |X(w-a)|<|X(w+a)| for Re w>0, X(w)=xi(1/2+w); equivalently E_a(z)=xi(1/2+a-iz) is Hermite-Biehler and the shifted de Branges kernel K_a is positive definite for every a>0. Equivalent to RH (de Branges 1968, Lagarias 2007).

nodes.name: Shift-bridge threshold theorem (a-dial)
nodes.statement: With E_a(z) = X(a - iz) and kernel K_a, strict diagonal positivity at shift a holds exactly when a >= Delta (maximal horizontal zero displacement); K_a PSD for every a > 0 iff Delta = 0 iff RH. E_a(z) = Xi(z + ia), so T3(a) is "no zero with Re s > 1/2 + a". Obstruction map G20.

nodes.name: Finite compressions of -I+2S
nodes.statement: Every finite compression of A=-I+2S (S the unilateral shift) has eigenvalue -1, yet +1 lies in the infinite approximate spectrum. Stable finite eigenvalue data do not determine the infinite limit; it is a control against finite-stage extrapolation.

nodes.name: Strict shift comparison threshold
nodes.statement: With Delta=sup|Re rho| over zeros of X: |X(w-a)|<|X(w+a)| for all Re w>0 iff a>=Delta (endpoint included). Positivity for every a>0 is RH-equivalent. Equivalent object: E_a(z)=xi(1/2+a-iz) and its de Branges kernel.

nodes.name: shift reciprocal covariance filter
nodes.statement: RZ_b passes every prime-side identity and size inequality after s -> s+1-b, F -> 1/F; a valid argument needs a step not covariant under shift and reciprocal (sign of Lambda, or position of pole/symmetry line).

nodes.name: Corollary SF: the Euler product alone does not constrain short-length phases
nodes.statement: Arbitrary phase changes on any finite set of primes keep the MT twin's planted zero and properties (in |Im s| < gamma_0, 2a <~ 4 log gamma_0). Measured at gamma_0 = 3e12, delta_0 = 3/8: margin >= 90.5, and >= 80.7 with every prime <= 6420 set adversarially.

nodes.name: Effective abscissa sigma_B of the coefficient ladder
nodes.statement: The zero-side verdict assumes Re s_B = (1 + y0)/2 = 0.59045 < 1 (the only transcribed definition, eq. (10)). Under a reading Re s_B ~ 1.4 the zero side is unconditionally controlled, but this does not reopen the sub-0.14 contract.

nodes.name: GUE-conditional share peaks near N = 9.22e5
nodes.statement: sigma(N)=E_coll/E has an interior maximum sigma_max about 0.94943 at N_max about 9.22e5; N_max scales as E_trunc^{-1.375}, so a 10% change of the truncation floor moves it by about 15%. Landmark positions are qualitatively stable and quantitatively model-sensitive.

nodes.name: Collision share sigma(N)=E_coll/E(N) is degree-0 homogeneous
nodes.statement: E(N)=E_trunc+E_flow+E_coll; crossover E_coll=E_trunc at N~3.280294e9; far-tail local exponent of sigma tends to -1/2 with gap ~1/(2 log T0); crossing elasticities satisfy E_CC+E_ET+E_CF=0. Bookkeeping of the Polymath15-type bridge constants.

nodes.name: sigma(N) obeys a logistic flow in t = ln N
nodes.statement: With E_flow neglected, sigma=r/(1+r), r=E_coll/E_trunc: d sigma/dt=-g(t) sigma(1-sigma), inflection at sigma=1/2-g'/(2g^2). With E_flow: sigma(N_cross)=1/(2+E_flow/E_trunc) exactly. Local exponent tends to 1/2 with shortfall about 1/(2 log T0).

nodes.name: Conditional share of the bridge budget turns over near N ~ 1e6
nodes.statement: sigma(N) = E_coll/E(N) is U-shaped (min 0.841), peaks ~0.949 near N_max ~ 9.2e5, then decays since E_coll ~ sqrt(log T0/N) while E_trunc is constant; sigma = 1/2 at N ~ 3.27e9. N_max ~ (1/E_trunc)^{1.38} and exists only for a constant floor.

nodes.name: Stationarity identity at the peak of the GUE-conditional share
nodes.statement: For the share sigma(N)=E_coll/E(N), with a, b the local log-slopes of the component tails: at the peak E_flow/E_trunc = a/b and N_peak/N_flow=(b/a)^{1/(a+b)}, verified across a 0.25x..16x E_trunc sweep to 2e-4. Slope asymptote (1/2,1/2,1). C_C and E_trunc sensitivities combine additively. GUE-conditional diagnostic, not a bound.

nodes.statement: w_1(0)=-6.352, w_1<0 on about [0,3.31] and again on (6.945,10.532). The split bound lambda_min(T[sigma_2^+]) - lambda_max(T[sigma_2^-]) crosses zero at 2a=0.6026<ln2 while the true lambda_1 is far positive. Positivity is a compression (uncertainty-principle) effect; the kernel bound |ghat(w)|^2<=(a/pi)||ghat||^2 is pointwise only.

nodes.statement: The beyond-T=3200 tail residual of the Galerkin minimiser grows in N with exponent about 3.228, tracking the endpoint-weighted coefficient sum growth q_S (about 3.23), not its rank-1 square 2q_S (about 6.18). nodes.statement: A sign-blind proof of the Legendre tail needs sum_{M<=sqrt x} |M(x/M) - M(x/(M+1))| << sqrt x polylog, which implies M(x) << sqrt x polylog; this is not known under RH and needs J_{-1}(T) << T. HiGHS LP confirms equality at 1e4 (347) and 3e4 (548).

nodes.statement: Inward normalized shear of the completed function is E_+ - E_- from an unconditionally positive boundary kernel P_a. Near an off-line zero gamma+ib of multiplicity m: W_h(gamma)=m|c|^2(h-b)^{2m-1}+O((h-b)^{2m}). E_-(t,h)<=E_+(t,h) for all t and 0<h<1/2 is equivalent to RH.

nodes.statement: W=Re(F' conj F), Q=(-W)_+, K_eta=Q/(|F|^2+eta^2). For a rectangle D=(0,X)x(T0,T1) with no zeros on top, bottom, right edges: int_D K_eta^2=(pi/2)M_D log(1/eta)+O_D(1), M_D = zeros strictly inside. So no off-line zeros in D iff energy is o(log 1/eta).

nodes.name: Two-boundary Dirichlet-to-Neumann identity for the phase of the Cayley symbol
nodes.statement: On the strip 0 < x < b with S = (1 - alpha L)/(1 + alpha L), L = F'/F, S(iy) = exp(i theta(y)): -theta'(y) = (pi/(4 b^2)) int sech^2(pi (y - y')/(2b)) (-log abs S(b + iy')) dy' + sum over zeros of S in the strip of K(x_k, y - y_k) - sum over poles of S in the strip of K(x_j, y - y_j), K(x, d) = (pi/b) sin(pi x/b)/(cosh(pi d/b) - cos(pi x/b)) > 0. -theta' = 2 alpha (Xi'^2 - Xi Xi'')/(Xi^2 + alpha^2 Xi'^2), Xi(y) = xi(1/2 + iy), is the Laguerre expression. Measured: residual <= 6.4e-17 (zeta near 30), <= 7.4e-7 (zeta near 1e4, truncated kernel), <= 4.1e-13 (DH near 85.7, one pole of S at 0.17213 + 85.71597i, pole sum 11.01 against T_b 1.73). T_b is 0.74, 0.32, 0.11, 0.10 of the mean phase derivative at T = 1e2 to 1e5 (alpha = 1, b = 1/2). For zeta and b >= 1/2 the first term is positive unconditionally. The identity is the Poisson-Jensen formula of the strip; it holds for DH with its pole terms.

nodes.name: Strip ladder kappa(Strip_Y) = Y^2/2 with exact witness
nodes.statement: kappa(zeros in |Im z| <= Y) = Y^2/2. Upper bound: de Bruijn 1950 Thm 13. Lower bound witness: Lambda((z^2 + Y^2) cos(cz)) = (sqrt(1 + 4c^2Y^2) - 1)/(4c^2) -> Y^2/2 as c -> 0. Hence kappa(critical strip) = 1/2, kappa(QRH 7/8) = 9/32, kappa(QRH 11/12) = 25/72.

nodes.name: No strip schedule y*(N) serves both field-Lipschitz and front adherence
nodes.statement: Strip field Jacobian L_field = 2N/y^2 bounded forces y*(N) >= sqrt(2NS/E_acc) -> infinity; bounding the near-front error needs y* <= y_ceil = O(1). Corridor empty beyond N_crit = y_ceil^2 E_acc/(2S) (about 15.7 in the worked case).

nodes.name: Subleading constant K = 11/2 - 2 gamma - 3 pi^2/8
nodes.statement: K = lim (accumTotal(m) - 4 C_1 m) = -C_1 + (5/2) Iv = 0.644467019788 with Iv = INT v zeta(3, 1+v) dv = 1 - pi^2/12 and -C_1 = 3 - 2 gamma - pi^2/6; zeta(3) cancels.

nodes.name: Paper conjectures subsumed by RH
nodes.statement: Conjectures 15.2 (zero bridge thickness), 17.3/18.4 (ghost absence), 22.4 are RH restated; 16.4, 16.6, 18.1, 18.2 reduce to canonical-system existence; KYP / delay-Gram appendices M-O add nothing independent. Only 22.1 and 27.2 were independent, and both are now closed (P30, P20).

nodes.name: Sun's Catalan-constant irrationality preprint: partial verification
nodes.statement: Sections 6-9 ledger verified and the decisive margin hardened about 4x by re-optimising rho to 1/50 (sign-corrected optimum ~1/56, margin > 0.037); sections 2-5 core uncertified. Irrationality of G remains open.

nodes.name: Sun Prop 6.3 additive offset is exactly 4, independent of m
nodes.statement: J_raw-kappa=+4 for every modulus m, from the constant-sector correction 3/2->-5/2 of (6.21) via int_0^1 zeta(2,1+v)dv=1; checked at m=18,20,21. Catalan-constant thread (Sun 2026, unverified source).

nodes.name: Prop 6.3 additive offset equals 4 and is modulus-independent
nodes.statement: The const-sector correction 3/2 -> -5/2 of (6.21) follows from INT_0^1 zeta(2, 1+v) dv = 1; the offset is exactly 4 for all moduli m (checked m = 18..41). The claim that the Section-6 integrand is rho-independent is refuted: Q_0(v) carries rho.

nodes.name: Three-prime S-unit count approaches (ln U)^3/(6 ln2 ln3 ln5) slowly
nodes.statement: count(2^a3^b5^c<=U)/leading = 2.49, 1.90, 1.64, 1.41, 1.26 at U=1e2..1e9, extended to 1e15 with a (ln U)^2 surface correction; primitive-residue slope is exactly 1 per prime-content class with intercept ln(class Euler factor).

nodes.name: S-unit rank/density obstruction to a two-prime Sonine multiplier
nodes.statement: For S={inf,2,3} the S-units 2^Z 3^Z have Dirichlet rank 2; their logs n ln2+m ln3 are dense in the one-dimensional scaling flow. The Sonine remainder delta_S23 has log^2 spikes on a dense set, so Lhat_S23>=0 exists only as abstract operator positivity, not a bounded continuous multiplier. A rank-r subgroup of R is discrete iff r<=1.

nodes.name: Phase of zeta right of the line: counting does not locate
nodes.statement: S(sigma,T) for sigma > 1/2 is defined without circularity only when the strip is zero-free; Backlund rectangles count zeros and are decoupled from the heat flow; Voronin universality implies the image closure is all of C, so no topological lever. The quantity segmentArgDelta in the survey is not a winding number.

nodes.name: No critical coupling inside 1/2 < sigma < 1
nodes.statement: A fine survey of phase metrics (imp-2323) found all of them smooth in the open strip (1/2,1); the bulk order-parameter route is recorded as empirically dead.

nodes.name: A certified surrogate spacing law cannot seed an N-uniform interval enclosure
nodes.statement: The backward N-particle Dyson enclosure needs seed intervals [x_k_lo(N), x_k_hi(N)] that are tight, distinct-ordered with a neighbour-gap floor, and N-uniform. A surrogate spacing law (Riemann-von Mangoldt plus bounds on S(t)) cannot supply all three.

nodes.name: Finite Suzuki scalar certificates
nodes.statement: Psi(0)=0, Psi(r)>=r/(100 log(5/4)) on [0,a_0], Psi(r)>1/100 on [a_0,log 10^7]; Psi(r)>11/400 on [log 2,log 10^4] (1,280 events, 192/256-bit Arb); window mean int_t^{t+1}Psi>0.0431381 for 0<=t<=log(10^6)-1. Reserves are not monotone (q=4 to q=5 decreases).

nodes.name: Convex-conjugate reserve and its update
nodes.statement: M_n=J_n-C*(S_n); M_{n+1}-M_n=int_{S_n}^{S_n+w_{n+1}}[r_{n+1}-u(s)]ds, u the derivative of the one-sided conjugate. Convexity does not fix the sign. Under RH the almost-periodic zero expansion has arbitrarily small returns, so a uniform positive margin is the wrong target.

nodes.name: Suzuki scalar response Psi and box test
nodes.statement: Psi(W)=(W/2)q_W[W^{-1/2}1_{I_W}]. Between prime-power events Psi(r)=C(r)-S_n r+J_n, S_n=sum_{j<=n}w_j, J_n=sum w_j r_j, with convex archimedean C on r>=log 2. RH corresponds to Psi>=0 type screw positivity (Suzuki 2206.03682).

nodes.name: Suzuki localized Weil operators and spectral convergence
nodes.statement: Suzuki 2606.09096 builds localized self-adjoint operators for Weil's form via the screw function unconditionally (positive after a negative scalar shift). Suzuki 2610.32704 Thms 1.1-1.2 assume RH: monotone eigenvalue convergence to the product over distinct zero ordinates.

nodes.name: Toeplitz compression of the Suzuki/Weil form on interval cells
nodes.statement: H_{h,m}=(q_{|i-j|}), q_0=2Psi(h)/h, q_d=[Psi((d+1)h)-2Psi(dh)+Psi((d-1)h)]/h. Mesh refinement is exact: U*H_{h/2,2m}U=H_{h,m}. With positive definite interior, the two-boundary Schur complement is positive iff e>=|b|.

nodes.name: Sym^m functoriality of the contraction needs uniform Rankin-Selberg residue bound
nodes.statement: Res_{s=1} L(s, sym^m f x sym^m f) = prod_{j=1}^m L(1, sym^{2j} f) (exact). Contraction survives under a_m ~ a_0/log Q_m iff log c_m = O(log Q_m). Margin h_m = 1 - log c_m/log Q_m is bounded under GRH but unconditionally behaves like 1 - 0.778 m/log m, negative from sym^4.
nodes.underusedWhy: only node of its chunk where Hecke/Euler structure enters a contraction margin; not the same as map row P25

nodes.name: Szasz boundary: no seam localisation over Szasz-divergent rate families
nodes.statement: If sum mu_j/(1 + mu_j^2) = inf then sup_M Lam_M(d) = 1 for every d > 0, by Muntz-Szasz completeness of {e^(-mu_j t)} in L2(0,inf). Covers arithmetic progressions and the full prime-reciprocal alias family. Obstruction map row P18 states the same threshold for Pick node sets.

nodes.name: E_a(z) = A_a(z) - i B_a(z) = Xi(z + i a)
nodes.statement: With A_a(z) = 8 int Phi(u) cosh(2au) cos(2zu) du, B_a(z) = 8 int Phi(u) sinh(2au) sin(2zu) du, Xi(l) = 8 int Phi(u) cos(2 l u) du: E_a = Xi(. + ia) exactly (checked to 1e-30). Channel data built with cosh(a t) correspond to shift a/2.

nodes.name: T3 residual route = zero-free strip ladder (rows P19, G20)
nodes.statement: T3 at shift a iff E_a = Xi(. + ia) is Hermite-Biehler iff zeta has no zero with Re s > 1/2 + a. The controlled quantity is quantized (1 or +infinity, never 1 - delta); a -> 0 uniformity is margin-forbidden by Lambda >= 0. The wall is zero location, not pair correlation.

nodes.name: Lemma SL1: T3 at level a = zero-free strip
nodes.statement: Equivalent for a>0 outside a countable set: T3 kernel PSD on finite sets in C_+; K^{E_a} PSD; E_a=Xi(.+ia) Hermite-Biehler; every zero has |Im lambda|<=a; zeta!=0 for Re s>1/2+a. Grade: wall is zero-free strip plus flow rigidity, not pair correlation.

nodes.name: T3: exact Twin Ladder residual inequality
nodes.statement: K_a=K_{a,0}+D_{a,R}+K_a^(S) with K_{a,0}>=0 the positive core. Prove D_{a,R}+K_a^(S)>=-K_{a,0} as Hermitian forms for every a>0 and every finite test set in C_+. D_{a,R} cancels to second order through cos(ps)-1; absolute values spend the whole core. RH-equivalent.

nodes.name: T3(a) = zero-free strip dictionary (SL0/SL1)
nodes.statement: E_a(z)=A_a(z)-iB_a(z)=Xi(z+ia). De Branges kernel of E_a is PSD iff E_a is Hermite-Biehler iff zeta has no zero with Re s>1/2+a. T3(a) for all a>0 is RH. Trig core verified to 1e-30; canonical cosh(2au) convention gives shift a (factor-2 relabel elsewhere).

nodes.name: Theorem G3: proportion and density inputs add nothing to a strip
nodes.statement: In the de Bruijn class, proportion statements (Levinson, Conrey, PRZZ, Alpoge-Furman 2/3), zero-density bounds N(sigma,T) <= T^{A(1-sigma)+o(1)} and 'all but finitely many zeros real' have kappa(P and Strip_Y) = Y^2/2: zero yield beyond the strip they are combined with.

nodes.name: Quadratic tangency law |tau_c| = g^2/8
nodes.statement: For the full N-particle gap ODE the collision coefficient is 8 with remainder of determined sign; with the Theta-trap (Theta <= 1/4) the coefficient 8(1 - Theta) lies in [6,8], giving g^2/8 <= t_c <= g^2/6. dTheta/dW_1 ~ 1/g0 off-basin (product pinned at 16/27).

nodes.name: Restricted fourth moment (H) for B=0.874
nodes.statement: B=437/500 needs a restricted numerator fourth-moment bound of order U^{39/40+eps} on the detected class. With only #B<=U^R and global fourth moment U, Holder is sharp: first moment U^{(3R+1)/4}. Needs joint detector/numerator control losing 1/40.
nodes.closedBy: Z10 (K=(3R+1)/4-theta/2 is the LP optimum), not-covered item 2

nodes.name: Riemann hypothesis
nodes.statement: All non-trivial zeros of zeta have real part 1/2.

nodes.name: Telescoping gap kernel and projection domination
nodes.statement: Gap-difference kernel of an omitted zero y: Delta_l(y)=2 g_l/((x_l-y)(x_{l+1}-y)); pair: |Delta_l|<=4 g_l/(|x_l-y||x_{l+1}-y|). Since |x-y|>=|x-Re y|, an off-line zero with Re y outside [x_l,x_{l+1}] is dominated by the on-line zero at its projection; RvM counts cover it.
nodes.underusedWhy: proved, RH-free per-window domination of off-line zeros by their projections; holds on backward heat, needs an arithmetic partner

nodes.name: Deligne tensor-power bootstrap: excess m/2 over Z against 1/(2m) over F_q
nodes.statement: Over F_q the m-fold self-product gives exponent n/2+1/(2m), tending to the Weil weight. Over Z the Kurokawa tensor zeta has a pole of order m at s=m, excess m/2, giving Re rho<=1 for every m. Finite Euler truncations have no pole and no functional equation. No finite analogue is a partial.

nodes.name: The tensor-power squeeze bounds local parameters, not zeros
nodes.statement: Landau's lemma applied to L(s, Sym^m x Sym^m) with non-negative coefficients gives abs(alpha_p) <= p^(1/(2m)): it carries an inequality across the abscissa of convergence for the local parameters. For zeta every symmetric power is zeta. The squeeze fails for E_a at the step 'L(s, Sym^m) is holomorphic in Re s > 1 apart from s = 1' (pole at 1 + m a), is not formulable for DH, and holds at every step for sign twists and THIN. It supplies the SIZE input and nothing about zeros; the positivity form is capped by Fejer's bound a_1 <= 2 cos(pi/(K+2)) a_0 (row P25).
